default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: My name is written in kanji like this.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: It modifies the noun 名前 that comes immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: It marks the topic of the sentence with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the means or method of writing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: This demonstrative adverb modifies the verb 書きます and describes an action being demonstrated directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: It is the main predicate of the sentence in the polite form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The topic 「私の名前は」 is placed first, followed by the method 「漢字で」. The demonstrative from the コ group, 「こう」, acts as an adverb directly before the verb 「書きます」 to show the writing action to the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows a way of writing like the one the listener has just done or mentioned. It is not used when the speaker demonstrates it personally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It only comes before a noun (こんな＋N) and cannot directly modify a verb.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: To modify a verb showing the action “do it like this,” use the adverb 『こう＋V』, not 『こんな』.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: “It is too difficult, so I want to leave school.” Tanaka: “Please do not say that. Let’s do our best together.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object affected by やめる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: たいです expresses the speaker’s wish; the mark 」 ends the quotation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: そんな modifies an omitted content or way of speaking and means “words like that.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: Vないでください asks the listener not to perform that action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together; the mark 」 ends the quotation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.cn: Aな＋だ＋から; Vない形＋でください; Vます形 omit ます＋ましょう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause with だから comes before the result やめたいです. The object of leaving is 学校, so 学校を is used; Tanaka then uses ないでください to stop the negative statement and ましょう to invite them to do their best together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If だから is replaced with なので, the reason stays the same, but the tone becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ましょう is replaced with ませんか, the sentence changes from a direct invitation to a gentler invitation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use から after a noun or adjective な and forget to add だ. They may also translate ましょう as a command instead of an invitation to act together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vi: You must not send emails like that to teachers.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun for a person goes with the particle 「に」, which marks the recipient of the sending action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative prenominal 「そ」 modifies the noun 「メール」 and gives it a negative or inappropriate nuance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun goes with the particle 「を」 and is the direct object of the sending action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the て form combines with 「はいけません」 to express a rule forbidding an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.why: This sentence expresses a prohibition with the pattern 「〜てはいけません」 and the verb 「送る」; 「先生に」 marks the recipient, and 「そんな」 modifies “email” to identify an email with inappropriate content that the listener has just mentioned or intends to send.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It means “it is okay not to send it” and gives permission not to do something, rather than expressing a prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a past prohibition, “was not allowed to send,” so it is not suitable for reminding someone of a current rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q11.kobun.tip: The pattern 「〜てはいけません」 is a strict prohibition used by a superior speaking to a subordinate or when stating a rule. It is not used when speaking to a superior.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vi: Because Mr. Yamada said that, I was very surprised.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun goes with the particle 「が」 and is the subject of the subordinate reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative adverb 「あ」 shows a way of speaking that both people have witnessed or clearly know about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb combines with the connecting particle 「から」 to form a subordinate reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The degree adverb modifies the state of being surprised 「おどろきました」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite past-tense verb is the main predicate of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.why: The subject in the subordinate reason clause goes with the particle 「が」 (山田さんが); the adverb 「ああ」 is used because the speaker is referring to Yamada’s surprising way of speaking, which the listener also knows about or witnessed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It suggests that the speaker is about to quote Yamada’s exact words immediately afterward.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It simply repeats information heard indirectly and does not suggest that both people witnessed it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.tip: In a subordinate reason clause with 「から」, the subject of the subordinate clause must use the particle 「が」, not 「は」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: Is tomorrow’s class cancelled? I did not know that at all.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: It gives a time meaning to the noun じゅぎょう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: It marks the topic of the question with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: A short noun-predicate question used in informal conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The demonstrative from the ソ group modifies こと and refers to information the other person has just provided.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: It acts as the object of the following verb, with the particle を omitted in speech.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: It is the main predicate of the sentence in the polite past negative form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The information “there is no class tomorrow” is something the listener knows, but the speaker has just heard for the first time. In this context, something within the listener’s area of knowledge uses the demonstrative group ソ (そんな) to modify the noun 「こと」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used only when both the speaker and listener have clearly known the information beforehand.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It is usually used for something belonging to the speaker or something happening right in front of them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: When receiving new information just stated by the other person, always use the group ソ (そんなこと), not the group ア (あんなこと).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: Yesterday’s party was fun, wasn’t it? I want to have another party like that next time, don’t you?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の modifies パーティー and shows which party it was.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 楽しかった is the past adjective predicate い; ね is used to confirm the shared feeling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: また modifies the following action and shows repetition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: This noun phrase is the object of したい, although を is omitted in spoken language.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.4.vi: want to have one, don’t you?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: Vたい expresses the speaker’s wish; ね adds a feeling of agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.cn: Vます-omit ます ＋ たい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The time phrase comes before the noun to identify the party, followed by an evaluation. したい expresses the wish to repeat the action of having a party.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ほしい, the focus is on wanting to have a party, not directly on wanting to perform the action oneself.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with しましょう, the sentence becomes a firmer invitation or suggestion instead of simply expressing a wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake したい for “want to have,” but it is the Vたい form, meaning “want to do” that action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: That is exactly what you said. I think so too.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The subject in the relative clause modifying とおり uses the particle が changed to の.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb directly modifies the noun とおり.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure ~とおりだ shows a match and is accompanied by ですね to express agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も replaces は to show that the viewpoints are similar.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The demonstrative adverb from the ソ group replaces the content or opinion the other person has just stated.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate expresses a thought in the polite form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The first clause confirms the other person’s view with the pattern 「言うとおり」. The second clause uses the demonstrative adverb from the ソ group, 「そう」, before 「思います」 to represent all the content the listener has just stated and show agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a personal opinion that the speaker is about to present (“I think this...”), and is not used to agree with another person’s words.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It is unnatural in ordinary conversation for directly showing agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: To agree with the other person’s view, the standard fixed expression is 『そう思います』, not 『こう思います』.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた・Nの + とおり / そう + 思う
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: There is a large mountain outside the window, isn't there? That is Mount Fuji.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: Modifies the position of the noun 外.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A particle に that indicates the place where an object exists.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: An attributive word that directly modifies the noun 山.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The subject indicating the existing object, used with the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The existence verb あります combines with the group of particles よね to seek confirmation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: A demonstrative pronoun from the ア group, used as the subject to refer to an object far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: A noun predicate that identifies the object あれ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The mountain is far away outside the window, beyond the reach of both the speaker and the listener in physical space. Therefore, the demonstrative pronoun from the ア group (あれ) is used as the subject to point to that mountain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Refers to an object near the listener. It is not suitable when both people are looking at a mountain far away outside the window.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Refers to an object right next to the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: When referring to a visible scene far from both people, such as a mountain or a distant building, 『あれ』 must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: It is very delicious, isn't it? This is the first time I have eaten food this delicious.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the adjective おいしい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective predicate ending in い combined with ですね to express feelings and seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: A demonstrative word from the コ group that modifies the noun 料理 and refers to the food being directly tasted.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Moves the object to the topic position for emphasis with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb of time indicating that an action is being experienced for the first time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The food is right in front of the speaker, and the speaker is directly experiencing its taste. Therefore, under the demonstrative system for the immediate scene, the コ group (こんな) must be placed before the noun 「料理」 to mean “food this delicious.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Refers to food near the other person or carries a sense of distance. It is unnatural when the speaker is directly eating the food.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Refers to food in a distant place or food that was eaten in the past and exists in memory.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: When talking about an object or food that you are directly tasting or holding, use 『こんな + N』.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: Those shoes are really nice, aren't they?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: A demonstrative word from the so-group that directly modifies the noun 「くつ」 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun used as the topic is placed at the beginning of the sentence; the particle は has been omitted.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: An adjective ending in な combined with ですね functions as a predicate to praise something and seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The speaker uses the attributive word 「その」 to modify the shoes belonging to the listener, who is wearing or holding them. The speaker then uses the adjective 「すてき」 with 「ですね」 as the predicate to praise the shoes and seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Used when the shoes belong to the speaker, for example, when the speaker is wearing them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Used when the shoes are far from both people or when talking about shoes remembered from the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: When praising something the other person is wearing or owns, English learners often mistakenly use 「この」 because of the habit of pointing. In Japanese, 「その」 must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: Did you walk all the way here? It must have been very far, wasn't it?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A verb in the て form that functions as an adverbial complement of manner for the movement verb 「来る」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative 「ここ」 combines with the particle 「まで」 to indicate the destination of a movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A past plain-form predicate combined with the particle 「の」 to ask for confirmation in a familiar way.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.vi: it must have been very far, wasn't it?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: A past form of an adjective ending in い combined with 「でしょう」 to make a guess and share feelings.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「歩いて」 to state the manner and 「ここまで」 to indicate the speaker's current location, asking 「の?」 for confirmation. The second clause uses 「でしょう」 to guess the other person's experience and show empathy.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Refers to a place near the listener or a place just mentioned, not the place where the speaker is standing and waiting.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Refers to a place far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: When someone has just arrived at the place where the speaker is standing, the destination must be 「ここ」 (the speaker's location), and 「そこ」 must not be used by mistake.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + でしょう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: Park: "Yesterday's lesson with Teacher Yoshida was really interesting, wasn't it?" - Yamada: "Yes. I wish I had started studying under a teacher like that earlier."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name followed by an opening quotation mark at the beginning of the turn.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: A time noun combined with the particle 「の」 to modify the noun phrase that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun referring to a person combined with the particle 「の」 to show an ownership relationship with the noun 「じゅぎょう」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: A noun combined with the particle 「は」 to serve as the main topic of the comment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: A past form of an adjective ending in い combined with the particle 「ね」 to express feelings and seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The other speaker's name followed by an opening quotation mark at the beginning of the reply.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: An interjection expressing agreement and approval in a familiar conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the adverb 「早く」 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The adjective 「早い」 changes to the adverbial form 「早く」 to modify the verb 「ならいたかった」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: A demonstrative attributive word from the 「あ」 line that modifies the noun 「先生」 and recalls a person known to both speakers.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: A noun combined with the particle 「に」 to indicate the person from whom the action 「ならう」 is learned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.11.vi: I wanted to study under him."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: A verb in the たい form used in the past to express regret about wanting to do something that was not done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: When referring to an object or quality that both people have just experienced and know well, such as Teacher Yoshida's good lesson yesterday, Japanese uses the attributive word from the 「あ」 line, 「あんな」, to modify the noun.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Used only when the object is known only to the other person, or when the context gives it a dismissive tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Used when the object is right in front of the speaker or belongs to the speaker's own story.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: In a conversation recalling an event that both sides experienced in the past, the 「あ」 line (あんな) must be used instead of the 「そ」 line.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vi: The teacher may also come to tomorrow's party.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow's party the topic of the prediction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: も marks the subject added to the possibility that the teacher will come.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: いらっしゃる is the honorific form of 来る or いる, used for a teacher.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: かもしれません expresses an uncertain possibility; よ is used to give information or add emphasis.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は. Then 先生も marks the additional subject of the clause. かもしれません is placed at the end because the whole statement, “the teacher will come,” is uncertain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: でしょう usually expresses a well-founded prediction or a higher level of confidence, while かもしれません expresses only possibility.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: はずです expresses a well-founded assumption that something should or is likely to happen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: Before かもしれません, use the plain form, not いらっしゃいますかもしれません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ かもしれない／かもしれません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vi:
Suzuki: "I have been feeling very tired lately."
Yamada: "Why don't you rest for a while?"
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker states their own condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A time adverb that sets the time reference for the tired condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the ている form combines with the ending んです to explain personal feelings and the current situation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The speaker gives a reply offering advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb of amount that modifies the degree of the action of resting.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 休む changes to the たら form to suggest an action as a possible condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The polite honorific form of どうですか, used to give advice or suggest a solution.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.why: When the other person explains their tired condition using the ending 「〜んです」, the listener replies with the polite suggestion structure 「Vたら いかがですか」 to offer a solution politely.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the same meaning but sounds more familiar and casual, while いかがですか shows respect and politeness.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It states that this option is the best, so it sounds more subjective and forceful than asking for an opinion with いかがですか.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.tip: In this suggestion pattern, the verb must first change to the past Vた form before ら is added (Vたら); Vるたら cannot be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q10.kobun.cn: Vたら ＋ いかがですか / どうですか
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vi: It is better not to exercise immediately after eating, okay?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The object of the action of eating (the particle を is omitted in casual speech).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 食べる changes to the た form to modify the noun あと, which refers to a time point.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun あと combines with the particle は to emphasize the period after eating as the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing immediacy that directly modifies the verb 動かない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 動く changes to the negative ない form and modifies ほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: A pattern advising someone not to do something, with the particle よ・ね adding a friendly reminder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.why: The sentence combines the time structure 「Vたあと（は）」 to set the point when eating is completed, and the advice pattern 「Vないほうがいい」 to give health advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means after doing something, but emphasizes that the following action happens immediately after the first action ends.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It is a direct request (“please do not...”), so it is more of a reminder or request than an optional piece of advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.tip: When modifying the noun あと, the verb must always be in the past Vた form. Learners often confuse it with Vる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q11.kobun.cn: Vた・Nの ＋ あと（で/は）; Vた・Vない ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vi: Are you allowed to keep a pet in the apartment where you live?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の replaces が as the subject in a clause modifying a noun.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 住む changes to the ている form and directly modifies the noun “apartment.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the activity of keeping a pet takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が accompanies the object of a potential-form verb.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 飼う changes to the potential かえる form and combines with the particle か to ask whether keeping a pet is allowed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.cn: V可能形 ＋ か（Group 1 verbs: change the ending to the え row + る; the particle を changes to が）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.why: The subordinate clause 「あなたの住んでいる」 modifies the noun for a place 「アパート」. Because the main verb is in the potential form 「かえます」, the pet being kept takes the particle 「が」 instead of 「を」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It only asks whether the actual action of keeping a pet is done or not. It does not ask about rules or whether keeping one is allowed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It has the same meaning of ability, but the potential form is much shorter and more natural in conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q12.kobun.tip: When a verb changes to the potential form, the object marker usually changes from the particle を to が. Learners often forget this and keep を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vi: It is better to learn English from a young age.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase combined with the particle から, indicating the starting point of an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of studying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb changes to the た form and connects with ほうがいい to give advice about what someone should do.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: A pattern that gives gentle advice and suggests the best thing to do.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: The sentence advises the listener to do an action using the pattern Vたほうがいい. The time phrase 子どものときから is placed at the beginning to limit the advice to the most suitable time period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It gives a more neutral comparison between options than a firm recommendation such as Vた.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It is a direct request or command, not advice about what would be beneficial like ほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: When advising someone to do something, learners often mistakenly use the dictionary form Vる instead of changing it to Vた before ほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.cn: Vた / Vない ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vi: I am big. This outfit is size S. Do you think it will fit me?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the main topic of the sentence: the speaker themself.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the smaller subject, the body part whose quality is being described.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The i-adjective ending in い acts as the predicate describing a physical characteristic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun 服 immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は makes the clothes the topic of the second clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が connects a clause that states a real premise before the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: A Group 2 verb changes to the potential form and combines with the particle か to ask whether the clothes will fit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.cn: V（Group 2: remove る + られる）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the structure “A は B が...” to describe a physical feature. The second sentence uses ですが to state the shirt size, then uses the potential form 着られる to ask whether the speaker can wear it successfully.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It changes the sentence into a question about the intention to wear something normally, rather than asking whether it will fit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It changes the sentence into a statement that the clothes can be worn, rather than a question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: For a Group 2 verb such as 着る, the potential form requires adding られる. Do not confuse it with a causative form or with the Group 1 conjugation rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: You are injured, aren't you? It takes about 10 minutes to walk to the station. Can you walk there?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A predicate describing the current condition, with the particle ね showing awareness and sympathy.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle まで indicates the destination of the journey.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: A time expression used with ぐらい to estimate the time needed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle けど connects a clause that gives background before asking about the person's condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: A Group 1 verb changes to the potential form (the ending く changes to け) to ask whether the other person is able to walk.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.cn: V（Group 1: change the ending in column う to column え + る）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: The speaker notices that the other person is injured, so first gives the distance and time as background using the connecting clause けど. Then they use the potential form 歩ける to ask whether the listener can walk that distance alone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply asks whether the other person chooses to walk. It does not show concern about whether they can manage to walk while in pain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It changes the sentence into a request for the other person to walk, which does not fit the context of checking on someone who is injured.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the ending from row う to row え for a Group 1 verb and incorrectly conjugate it as 歩きられる using the Group 2 pattern.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vi: Do you have a fever? Why don't you go to the hospital and get checked?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が accompanies a natural phenomenon or a physical symptom.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The sentence ending んですか is used to confirm the other person's condition after noticing an unusual sign.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action of going to see a doctor.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed into the conditional form たら to connect with a structure that gives a suggestion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: Combined with たら, it forms a suggestion pattern that advises the other person to try doing something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: After confirming that the other person has a fever with the ending んですか, the speaker uses the suggestion pattern たらどうですか to offer a gentle and polite solution.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a more direct and subjective recommendation from the speaker. It does not invite or explore the other person's opinion like どうですか.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It functions as a request or instruction for the other person to act, with little attempt to politely ask for their opinion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: The structure たらどうですか is used only to make suggestions to people of the same or lower status. It should not be used with superiors or older people because it may sound like giving them a lesson.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: Since it is summer vacation, Mr. Sato may be free.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun connected with だから functions as a conjunction showing an actual cause or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は identifies the person whose condition is being guessed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な comes before the speculation pattern, with the ending な removed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: This pattern expresses a guess with a fairly low level of certainty, about 50%.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな (remove だ)・N (remove だ) + かもしれません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses だから to state the objective basis that it is summer vacation. The second clause uses the pattern かもしれません to make a cautious guess about Mr. Sato being free.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows a considerably higher level of certainty than かもしれません, about 70–80%.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It states that something must certainly happen, based on a clear logical basis.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: When it follows an adjective ending in な or a noun, かもしれません connects directly without adding だ. Do not confuse this with ひまだかもしれません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vi: Before the meal, you had better not eat too many sweets.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The honorific prefix is attached before the noun 飯.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects a noun phrase that modifies the time point 前に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun indicating a time point combines with the particle に to identify when an action takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: This degree adverb is used with a negative predicate to express not doing something excessively.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of eating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb in the negative form ない comes before ほうがいい to form advice against an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: This sentence pattern advises the other person that it is better not to do the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: The sentence uses the advice pattern Vないほうがいい to advise the listener not to eat sweets so that the meal is not affected. The time phrase ご飯の前に is placed at the beginning to clarify the situation for the advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses regret about something that happened in the past, rather than giving advice for the present or future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a strict prohibition, not a gentle recommendation like ほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: When giving advice about what not to do in the present or future, always use the form Vない (Vないほうがいい). Learners often confuse it with the negative past form Vなかった.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.cn: Vた / Vない + ほうがいい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: Tomorrow, I would like you to help me prepare for the festival. Can you come at 10 o'clock?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A time adverb that sets the time point for the request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb modifying the action of preparing together with the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects the noun meaning festival and modifies the noun meaning preparation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of preparing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.4.vi: I would like you to help, but
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜てほしい expresses the wish for the other person to help, and combines with んですが to introduce a polite request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the specific time when the action of coming will take place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb 来る is changed into the polite potential form to ask whether the other person can come.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: The speaker uses the structure 「〜てほしいんですが」 to express a wish to ask for help and use it as an introduction. Then the speaker uses the potential form 「来られますか」 to politely ask whether the listener can come at the set time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used to directly ask the other person to do something, so it is more of a request for action than an expression of desire like てほしい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used only when the speaker wants to do something personally. It is not used to express a wish for someone else to do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: When the verb 来る changes to the potential form, it is pronounced こられる. Learners often confuse it with きられる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi:
Yamada: "What is ahead?"
Tanaka: "That place is dangerous, so you had better not go."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name at the beginning of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun 先 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks a location and combines with は to make the place the topic of discussion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: An interrogative word that combines with the particle が to function as the subject in an information question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The existence verb ある combines with the particle の to form a casual question in conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The speaker's name at the beginning of the answer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: A place pronoun that combines with the particle は to function as the topic of the explanation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The adjective ending in い combines with から to form a clause showing a cause or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb 行く is changed into the negative form ない and directly modifies ほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: A grammar pattern advising whether or not to do something, together with the modal particle よ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: Tanaka first gives an objective safety reason using 「〜から」. Then he uses the advice structure 「Vないほうがいい」 to advise avoiding an unfavorable action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the meaning of a strict legal prohibition, not a casual recommendation like ほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: It is usually used to suggest trying something in the affirmative form. Its negative form is rarely used for strong advice against an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: When advising someone NOT to do something, the standard pattern is Vないほうがいい. Learners often confuse it with Vなかったほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない + ほうがいい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: I was very surprised because your Japanese, Alice, is so good.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の shows possession and modifies the noun meaning Japanese.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object whose ability level is evaluated by the adjective 上手.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な changes to the form ending in で and links the clauses to show a reason or cause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate describes a sudden emotional reaction caused by the reason in the previous clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: The adjective ending in な is changed into the て form, with the ending で, to state the direct cause of the surprise and amazement「びっくりしました」in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Use から to emphasize a subjective reason involving intention, while で/て sound more natural when describing a cause that leads to a sudden emotion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: ので is explanatory, objective, and formal, but more wordy than the short linking form with で.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: When connecting a reason clause using て with an adjective ending in な, we remove な and add で (上手で). Learners often mistakenly change it to 上手なで.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aなで + 感情・心理動詞
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vi:
Hotel staff: "Please do not open the window and go to sleep, because it is very dangerous."
Nguyen: "Yes, I understand."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.sk:
N(person)「N を V-て + V-ないでください。 Aい + ですから。」
N(person)「Interjection、 V-ました。」
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker gives a request or reminder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The object affected by the action 開ける.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the て form describes the state that accompanies the later action of sleeping.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜ないでください is used to politely ask or advise someone not to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The following clause uses から to immediately explain the reason for the request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The listener receives the information and responds.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The predicate confirms that the reminder has been clearly understood.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.cn: Vない形(remove ない) + ないでください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.why: The hotel staff member uses the 「〜て」 verb form to describe the accompanying state (the window being open), combines it with 「〜ないでください」 to advise the guest not to sleep in that state, and adds the reason with 「〜ですから」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「〜てはいけません」 is used, the sentence expresses a strict prohibition based on rules, not a considerate piece of advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If only 「〜ないで」 is used, the sentence sounds casual and rough, so it is not suitable when staff speak to a guest.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.tip: The verb must first be changed correctly to the ない form, and then 「でください」 is added (for example: ねる → ねないでください).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vi: Because Thanh is a student, the price of the smartphone becomes lower.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.sk: N は + N なので + N の N が + Aい(remove い) + くなる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: Names the person who is the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun combines with なので to state an objective premise or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: Modifies the noun ねだん that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The structure A(remove い) + くなる expresses a change in quality or state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.why: The topic is 「タインさんは」, followed by the reason clause 「学生なので」 connected with 「ので」. The later clause uses the change pattern 「安くなる」 with the particle 「が」 to show a change in price.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「学生だから」 is used, the reason feels more direct. 「なので」 describes the price reduction as obvious and objective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「安くする」 is used, it describes the seller actively lowering the price, while 「安くなる」 shows that the price changes by itself.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.tip: When a noun connects with 「ので」, it must change to 「 N なので」, not 「 N ので」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(な)・Nな + ので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vi: Because the road is crowded, I will not arrive on time for the appointment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.sk: N が + V-ている + ため + N の N に + V(negative)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The subject of the action or state in the subordinate clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern ため indicates an objective cause leading to being late.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: Modifies the noun 時間 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the time of the appointment that one must arrive in time for.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb phrase 間に合う is in the negative form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「 Vている + ため」 to state an objective situation currently happening as the reason. The later clause uses 「〜に間に合わない」 to show the result of not making it by the agreed time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「こんでいるせいで」 is used, the sentence emphasizes blame and frustration about the traffic jam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「こんでいるのに」 is used, the sentence expresses an unexpected contrast, not simply a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.tip: The phrase 「間に合う」 (make it in time) always goes with the particle 「に」 to indicate the appointment time (for example: 時間に間に合う).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(な)・Nの + ため(に)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: Last night, I went to sleep without turning off the lights.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates when the action of sleeping happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb けす.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The Vないで form connects to the following verb and means doing the later action without doing the earlier action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the object 電気を of the negated action. けさないで connects directly to ねました to show the two actions: not turning off the lights and then going to sleep.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it gives a similar meaning, but the expression is more formal and more common in written language.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ないで as “not do,” but they should remember that it connects to the following action to mean “do the later action without doing the earlier one.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vi: Because I forgot my wallet, I went back home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object that was forgotten.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ため connects the reason to the result 家に帰りました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of returning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first, and the result comes after the comma. 忘れた uses the past form because forgetting the wallet happened before returning home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more natural in conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with から, the expression becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put the reason after the result, but with ため the reason clause usually comes first.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + ため
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vi: Because the teacher was sick, there was no class.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state 病気.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: With the noun 病気, ため must connect with の to indicate the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks something that exists or does not exist in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: 先生が病気 forms the reason clause, in which 先生 is the subject in the sick state. The main clause uses 授業がありませんでした to say that no class existed because of that reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the reason stays the same, but the expression sounds softer and more common in conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: You must distinguish が in 先生が from が in じゅぎょうが: one belongs to the reason clause, and the other belongs to the main clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + ため
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vi: This room is a little old, but it is convenient because it is near the station.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this room the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies 古い and makes the degree of oldness less strong.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: although it is a little old
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects two contrasting ideas: the room is old, but it is still convenient.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle から gives the reference point for judging the distance as near.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the reason 駅から近い with the result べんりです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: は sets the topic. Then ですが creates a contrast between “a little old” and “convenient.” The phrase 駅から近いので comes before the predicate to give the reason for the evaluation べんりです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ですが, the contrast stays the same, but the expression is fuller and more formal.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ので, the reason becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に with 駅, but when saying “near the station” in the pattern 駅から近い, use から.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.cn: Aい + ですが／V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: Nozomi injured her leg in an accident.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Nozomi as the person being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the cause of the injury.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the body part affected by the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: After the topic comes the cause じこで, followed by the injured body part 足を. で here indicates the cause, not the place where the action happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning emphasizes “having an accident” before getting injured.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate で as “at,” but in this sentence で means “because of.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vi: Asuka is still under 18, so she cannot drink alcohol.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は shows that Asuka is the person being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ adds the meaning that she still has not reached the age of adulthood.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: なので connects the noun １８さい to the result clause with the meaning “because, so.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: With the potential verb 飲めません, the thing that someone can drink usually takes が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the negative potential form of 飲む. It expresses the inability or lack of conditions to drink.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: The phrase １８さいなので gives the reason before the result, which is being unable to drink. 飲めません is the negative potential form, so the object おさけ is marked with が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with だから, the reason becomes more direct and conversational.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 飲みません is used, the sentence only says that the person does not drink. It does not emphasize being unable to drink.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with potential verbs, but the pattern 飲める usually uses おさけが飲める.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ ので／Aな・N ＋ なので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vi: Because I was busy with work last week, I could not meet my partner.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.sk: N(time) は ＋ N が ＋ Aい(past) ＋ ため、 ＋ N に ＋ V可能形(past negative)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: It sets a time reference as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The subject of the adjective that expresses the cause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The conjunction ため connects an objective cause clause in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the object of the meeting action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is in the past negative potential form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「〜ため」 to state an objective cause leading to the result in the second clause. The second clause uses the negative potential verb 「会えませんでした」 together with the particle 「に」 to show that the speaker could not meet the person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「から」 is used, the sentence sounds more subjective and is more common in everyday speech.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「ので」 is used, the sentence sounds gentle and polite in conversation, but it is less formal than 「ため」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: With the meeting verbs 「会う/会える」, the person met takes the particle 「に」, not 「を」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(な)・Nの ＋ ため(に)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vi:
Teacher: "Rai, what do you usually do on your days off?"
Rai: "Because I like movies, I often go to watch them."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.sk:
先生「N(person)、 N の N には N(question word) を V-ますか。」
ライ「N が Aな＋なので、 adverb ＋ V(remove ます) に 行きます。」
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The first speaker asks a question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: A term used to address and call the listener's name.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates a time and combines with は to emphasize the topic of discussion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The question-word object is used with the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite question predicate ends the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The second speaker answers the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle が indicates the object of the preference adjective 好き.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The adjective ending in な combines with なので to explain the reason politely.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The frequency adverb modifies the verb 見に行きます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: The structure V(remove ます) + に行く expresses the purpose of going somewhere.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: The teacher gives a time reference with 「休みの日には」 to ask about a habit. Rai explains his preference with the reason clause 「〜なので」, then uses the movement-purpose structure 「V(remove ます)＋に行きます」 to state what he often does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to 「好きだから」, the answer sounds more subjective and direct, and less polite when speaking to a teacher.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern 「V(remove ます)＋に行く」 shows the purpose of movement. It must be distinguished from 「Vて行く」, which shows moving farther away.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: Before 「ので」, adjectives ending in な and nouns must add 「な」 (for example: 好きなので), and cannot use 「だ」 or leave the form unchanged.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(な)・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vi: Whenever this toy's red switch is pressed, it moves.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The main topic is placed at the beginning of the sentence with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective modifies the noun スイッチ immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The object affected by the pressing action おす.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The conjunction と shows a necessary condition, after which the machine operates automatically.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate shows the necessary result that occurs after the button is pressed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: The topic 「このおもちゃは」 is placed at the beginning of the sentence. Then the necessary-condition structure 「V辞書形＋と」 describes how the device works when its switch is pressed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「おしたら」 is used, the sentence expresses a supposition or a specific one-time instruction, while 「と」 emphasizes the obvious operating rule of the toy.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「おせば」 is used, the sentence emphasizes the condition needed for the toy to work.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: The second clause of the conditional pattern 「〜と」 must never use commands, requests, intentions, or invitations, such as ください and ましょう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ と
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vi:
Yamamoto: "Are you going to tomorrow's study group?"
Sato: "If Mr. Yamamoto goes, I will go too."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: States the name of the person who starts the conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A time noun modifies the noun “study group” through the particle の.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite predicate ends with the particle か to ask about the other person's plans.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: States the name of the person who responds.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the subject in a hypothetical conditional clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern なら takes the other person's intention as the basis for the speaker's decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle も shows that the speaker will do the same action as the other person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: The main predicate shows the speaker's intention and decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（remove だ）・N（remove だ） ＋ なら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.why: The respondent uses 「なら」 to immediately accept the information just heard from the other person (that Mr. Yamamoto is going) as the basis for expressing their own intention or decision in the second clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: 「行ったら」 emphasizes the order of events: the action of going actually happens first, and then the speaker follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 「行けば」 only shows an ordinary logical condition. It does not clearly express the meaning of accepting information from the conversation context as 「なら」 does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q10.kobun.tip: With the pattern 「なら」, nouns and adjectives ending in な connect directly without adding だ (for example: 先生なら and 静かなら). Learners often automatically add だ and make だなら.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vi: No matter how tasty it is, if it is expensive, I will not buy it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing a high degree, used with the concessive pattern ても.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective ending in い changed to form ても to show a hypothetical concessive condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the stative adjective 高ければ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in い changed to the conditional form ば to show a hypothetical obstructing condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: A negative predicate stating the speaker's firm decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.cn: どんなに + Vて・Aいくて・Aなで・Nで + も ／ Aい(omit い) + ければ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.why: The sentence combines the concessive structure「どんなに〜ても」(no matter how high the degree) to raise the level of tastiness to the maximum, then uses the condition「〜ば」(高ければ) as the deciding factor leading to the negative result「買いません」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「ねだんが高くても買いません」 were used, the logic would change incorrectly to "even if the price is expensive, I will not buy it" instead of the hypothetical structure "if the price is expensive".
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 「いくら〜ても」 has exactly the same meaning as 「どんなに〜ても」 and can be used naturally in this sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q11.kobun.tip: Learners often form the conditional form ば of adjectives ending in い incorrectly (the correct form is to omit い and add ければ, such as 高ければ; it is often confused with 高いなら or 高いば).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vi: When we wake up tomorrow morning, if it is raining, let's not go outside.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: A time word modifies the noun "morning" through the particle の.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun showing the time when an event takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: A past-tense verb た modifies the noun とき, showing the time when waking up has been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern ときに identifies the reference time for observing the following event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the subject of the natural phenomenon of rain falling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: A verb changed to ていたら shows a hypothetical condition involving an ongoing state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: A verb clause is nominalized with the particle の and, together with を, serves as the object of やめましょう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: A persuasive predicate suggesting that the listener and speaker stop the action of going outside.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.why: The pattern「〜たら」is used because the following clause is a suggestion or proposal (やめましょう) for a specific hypothetical future situation. The form「〜ていたら」emphasizes that rain is falling at the exact time of waking up.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: The pattern「〜と」cannot be used with a suggestion, proposal, or command in the following clause, such as「やめましょう」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern「〜ば」expresses a general logical condition and has very limited use with persuasive or volitional endings in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the pattern「〜と」when the following clause is a suggestion or command (incorrect: 雨がふると出かけるのをやめましょう). Remember that only「〜たら」can freely be used with the forms 〜ましょう/〜てください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q12.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vi: If there are clothes with a nice design, I want to buy them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: An adjective ending in い directly modifies the following noun "design."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun combines with the particle の to modify the noun "clothes."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists together with the verb ある.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb ある changes to the conditional form 〜ば to state a hypothetical premise.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate changes to 〜たい and combines with です to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.cn: V(group 1: change the ending to the え column + ば / group 2: omit る + れば / group 3: すれば・くれば) ・ Aい(ければ) ・ Aな/N(なら/であれば)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses the conditional form 〜ば to set up the assumption that a suitable item exists, naturally leading to the desire to buy it (〜たい) in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It sounds more conversational and natural when the following clause expresses will or desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It cannot be used because the structure 〜と forbids a following clause expressing personal will or desire, such as 買いたいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use the conditional pattern 〜と when the following clause expresses desire (〜たい), a suggestion (〜ましょう), or a request (〜てください).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vi: If the weather is nice tomorrow, let's go to the zoo together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.sk: N(time) 、 N が + Aい(かったら) 、 N に + Vましょう。
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of future time that sets the time for the event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject in the conditional clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective いい changes to the past form + ら to create a hypothetical future condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows the destination of movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate changes to 〜ましょう to invite the listener to perform the action together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: A conditional clause using 〜たら allows the following clause to freely make a suggestion or call to action expressing will, such as 〜ましょう, without grammatical restrictions.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It is still grammatical but sounds formal and is less common in casual invitations.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It cannot be used because the following clause is an invitation expressing the speaker's will.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: When the adjective いい changes to the conditional form 〜たら, its stem must change to よかったら; いいたら must never be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: If you plan to go out early tomorrow morning, you should finish preparing today.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.sk: N1 の + N2 + Adv + V辞書形 なら、 + N(deadline) に + Vた + ほうがいいですよ。
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time noun combines with the particle の to modify the noun 朝.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun for a part of the day combines with the adverb 早く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb modifies the verb 出かける, showing that the action of going out happens early.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜なら takes the other person's plan as a premise for giving advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に follows a noun showing a deadline and indicates the final time by which something must be completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: A verb changed to た modifies ほう, forming a pattern for advising what should be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: A formal noun combines with the particle が and serves as the subject referring to the recommended action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: A positive evaluative predicate with the particle よ conveys sincere advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(omit だ)・N(omit だ) + なら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: The structure uses 〜なら to accept the listener's future plan, and the following clause gives advice to prepare in advance with the pattern 〜たほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It means "prepare only after going out tomorrow morning," which reverses the logical time order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It cannot be used because the following clause is advice expressing the speaker's subjective will.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: When advising someone to prepare in advance for an event that has not happened yet, use 〜なら, not 〜たら, because 〜たら means that the action in the first clause must be completed first.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vi: If we pass the exam, let's celebrate together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the target that receives the action of passing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb changed to 〜たら states a hypothetical condition completed in the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the celebration action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate changes to 〜ましょう to make a suggestion to organize the event together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.why: The pattern 〜たら expresses a condition after passing the exam has been completed, naturally providing the basis for suggesting a celebration together in the following clause (〜ましょう).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It is still grammatical but expresses a more rigid logical condition and sounds less natural in a casual invitation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It cannot be used because the following clause is an invitation expressing the speaker's will.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.tip: After the clause 〜たら, commands, suggestions, and requests (〜ましょう, 〜てください) can be used freely. This is completely different from the objective nature of 〜と.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q5.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から shows the starting quantity for beginning the calculation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the quantity being subtracted, which is the object of the action ひく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: A dictionary-form verb combines with the particle と to show an inevitable mathematical rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows the result produced by the calculation and goes with the verb なる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate describes the objective result of change produced by the calculation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.why: This sentence expresses an obvious mathematical truth based on an absolute rule of nature, so the required preferred conditional pattern is 〜と.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: The listener will still understand it, but in mathematics and objective truths, standard Japanese always prefers 〜と.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It is unsuitable because 〜なら is used to receive a topic or give advice, not to express an inevitable rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.tip: When expressing mathematical calculations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division) or necessary scientific truths, the conditional pattern 〜と must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + と
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vi: If you buy a ticket, you can enter the movie theater.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of buying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the conditional form 〜ば expresses a necessary condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination that the subject can enter.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the potential form to express the state of being able to enter when the condition is met.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.cn: V (Group 1: change the ending to the え column + ば / Group 2: remove る + れば / Group 3: すれば・くれば) ・ Aい(ければ) ・ Aな/N(なら/であれば)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.why: The sentence uses the conditional form 〜ば to set a necessary condition (buying a ticket), which then enables the action in the following clause (entering the theater).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It has a similar meaning, but focuses more on the time order: 'after finishing buying it, you will be able to enter.'
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It means 'if you plan to buy a ticket...', emphasizing the intention to buy rather than treating buying as the condition for entering the theater.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q7.kobun.tip: When the following clause contains a potential-form verb (〜可能形), Japanese speakers often use the form 〜ば to emphasize the necessary and sufficient condition relationship.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vi: As soon as you go up to the rooftop of this building, you can see Mount Fuji.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase modifies and specifies the noun 'rooftop' that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination toward which the upward action is directed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vると expresses an unavoidable condition: once you go up to the rooftop, you immediately see the scene that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が is used with a natural potential verb to indicate the thing that is seen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: A natural potential verb describes scenery that naturally comes into view.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses the pattern「Vると」to express an obvious condition or an unavoidable natural result (once you go up to the rooftop, the scene opens up before your eyes). The second clause uses the natural potential verb「見えます」, so the object being observed takes the particle「が」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using「あがったら」emphasizes the time sequence of a person's action after going up, rather than a natural rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 「見られます」shows intentional ability to see something (when the conditions or tools are available), while「見えます」refers to scenery that naturally comes into view.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle を with 見えます (incorrect: 富士山を見えます). Remember that this is an intransitive/natural potential verb, so it always takes the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vi:
Lee: "What does natto taste like?"
Yoshida: "Just try it, and you will know."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: Introduces the name of the speaker at the beginning of a turn.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The colloquial form って replaces the particle は to introduce the topic being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: An interrogative word directly modifies the following noun 味.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate ends with なの? This is used in casual speech to ask about a quality.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Introduces the name of the speaker answering.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb in the conditional form ば expresses the premise that leads to knowing the answer in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The main predicate is accompanied by the modal particle よ to confirm the information to the other person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.cn: V (Group 1: -u → -eba; Group 2: -ru → -reba; Group 3: すれば・くれば) + ば
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.why: The question uses the informal form「って」to explore the topic and the speaker's feelings. The reply uses the conditional form「〜ば」(食べれば) to emphasize the key premise: simply eating it will automatically lead to knowing the result.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 「食べたらわかるよ」has a similar natural colloquial meaning, but emphasizes the point in time after finishing eating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 「食べるとわかるよ」has a more objective sense of an obvious rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often form the ば of Group 2 verbs incorrectly, changing 食べる into 食べば or 食べれば according to the Group 1 rule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t12-q9.tokens.2.m: as for / speaking of (emphasizes the topic)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vi: I asked my friends whether Salina was really a good person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the embedded question clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb modifies the degree of the noun phrase いい人.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective directly modifies the following noun 人.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.vi: whether she is a good person or not,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern かどうか embeds a question without an interrogative word as the content being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に indicates the people to whom the question is directed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate is in the polite past tense.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（remove だ）・N（remove だ） + かどうか
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: A question clause without an interrogative word is embedded in the main sentence through the pattern「〜かどうか」to serve as the content of the verb「聞きました」. The noun「人」is directly attached to「かどうか」without adding だ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using「いい人か」is still grammatically correct, but「かどうか」makes the uncertainty between the two possibilities, yes or no, clearer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Using「人だということを」turns it into a statement reporting a confirmed fact rather than an interrogative question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: When combined with a noun or an adjective ending in な, learners often incorrectly add だ before かどうか (incorrect: いい人だかどうか; correct: いい人かどうか).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vi:
Yumi: "Did you argue with your boyfriend again?"
Kana: "Yes. I no longer know whether I like him or not."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Only identifies the person asking the question in the conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb indicating that an action happens one more time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates the other person taking part in the mutual action (arguing).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The short past-tense predicate with の is used for a casual question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: Only identifies the person answering in the conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: An interjection used to confirm information in everyday communication.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb emphasizing that the situation has changed to the point where it is no longer clear.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle が indicates the object toward which the adjective 好き is directed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.8.vi: whether I like him or not
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: An embedded question clause (~か〜どうか) comes before the verb わからない to serve as the unknown content.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: The verb わかる changes to the negative form ならない and then changes into なくなった to indicate an emotional state in which the answer is no longer clear.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形 / Aい / Aな (remove だ) / N (remove だ) + かどうか
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.why: To embed an uncertain question (whether I like him or not) as the complement of the verb わからなくなった, use the pattern かどうか. When the adjective ends in な (好き), だ must be removed before combining.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 好きかわからなくなった is grammatically correct and has the same meaning, but adding どうか emphasizes the two possibilities, yes or no, more clearly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q10.kobun.tip: When connecting an adjective ending in な or a noun with かどうか, learners often forget to remove だ (and incorrectly write 好きだかどうか).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vi: I told my daughter to clean the inside of the room.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person who receives the instruction or order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の modifies the location noun 中.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を indicates the object affected by the cleaning action (かたづける).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern V辞書形 + ように is used to convey the content of an indirect command or request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is the past tense of the verb 言う.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.why: The structure 〜ように言う is used to report a reminder, instruction, or command indirectly and more gently than a direct quotation of the command.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「へやをかたづけなさい」と言った gives a direct quotation of the command, with a stricter and more rigid tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.tip: In the indirect instruction structure 〜ように言う, the verb before ように is always in the dictionary form or the ない form; it is not changed to the て form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / Vない形 ＋ ように (言う / 頼む / 伝える)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vi: I will try to work part-time so that I can travel to Hokkaido during the winter vacation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the time when the trip takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the purpose and destination of the movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The potential-form verb 行ける combines with ように to express a purpose aimed at achieving an ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object that the speaker is trying to work on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate expresses the speaker's intention and determination to act.
