default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.why: Because the purpose in the first clause is a state of ability (being able to go), the sentence must use the potential form 行ける together with ように; the second clause is a deliberate effort to achieve that ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: To use ために, the verb before it must be the original volitional verb 行く (北海道旅行に行くために), because the potential form does not combine with ために.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.tip: Potential-form verbs (行ける, 買える, 話せる...) can only combine with ように to express purpose; they must never be combined with ために.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q12.kobun.cn: V可能形 / V無意志 / Vない形 ＋ ように
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: Since I started working, I have gradually become used to using English every day.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the verb "start."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern 〜てから marks the time when the action began and sets the basis for the change in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を identifies the object used every day.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb of frequency that modifies the verb "use."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb combines with ように to modify the entire phrase describing a change of state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜ようになる describes a gradual change into a new habit or ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「〜てから」 to mark the starting point. The second clause uses the structure 「V辞書形 ＋ ようになる」 to show a natural change in habit over time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a deliberate effort by the person to do something, rather than a natural change in habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses an objective decision or rule that has been fixed, not a change in state or habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 「ようになる」 (a change in habit over time) with 「ようにする」 (a deliberate effort by the speaker).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / V可能形 / Vない形 ＋ ようになる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: My son broke my watch, causing me trouble.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.sk: N (person causing trouble) に ＋ N (possessed object) を ＋ V受身形
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who caused the damaging action in the passive sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object owned by the speaker that was damaged in an indirect passive sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb こわす is put into the passive form to show that the speaker suffered trouble or damage because of the son's action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.cn: Passive-form verbs (Vられる): Group 1 changes the final u sound to a and adds れる; Group 2 removes る and adds られる; Group 3: される / こられる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: This is an indirect passive sentence (迷惑受身). The unstated subject is "I," who suffers the damage; the person performing the action is marked with に, and the damaged possession keeps the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes that the breaking happened regrettably and unintentionally, but it does not highlight the feeling of being harmed by another person as the passive form does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It implies asking for help and gratitude, which is completely opposite to the trouble and damage expressed by the passive form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: In an indirect passive sentence (when one's object is damaged by someone else), the object still takes the particle を, not the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.sk: N (product) は ＋ N (raw material) から ＋ 作られる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes wine, the product, the topic that the sentence explains.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から marks a raw material that has been processed and completely changed into the product.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 作る is put into the passive form to describe the production process of the finished product.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: The sentence uses the passive form to explain how the product is made. It uses the particle から because the grapes undergo a chemical change and no longer keep their original shape in the wine.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It refers to a material whose original substance can still be clearly recognized by sight, such as furniture made from wood.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: Distinguish carefully: 「から作られる」 is used for materials that change into a different substance (grapes into wine, milk into butter), while 「で作られる」 is used for materials that keep their original substance (wood into a table).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.cn: N ＋ から / で ＋ 作られる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vi: The teacher told Luka not to be late from tomorrow onward.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the teacher as the person giving the reminder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the reminder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This noun phrase combines から and は to emphasize the time when the requirement begins to apply.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: so as not to be late
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Vない ＋ ように expresses the content of an instruction or reminder aimed at a desired goal.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate describes the action of conveying the reminder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.why: The structure 「Vないように言う」 is used to report an order or request indirectly and politely, instead of using a direct imperative sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It quotes the exact words spoken directly instead of reporting the content of an instruction or request indirectly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It is a direct request made to the other person at the time of speaking, rather than a report of a past reminder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.tip: Before 「ように言う」, use only the dictionary form or the ない form of a verb; do not use the past form (Vた) or the polite form (Vます).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / Vない形 ＋ ように言う / 伝える / 頼む
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.sk: N (structure) は ＋ Time に ＋ V受身形
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the structure the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に follows a specific time expression to identify when the structure was built.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 建てます is put into the passive form to describe the completed construction without naming the builder.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.cn: Vられる (Group 2 verb: remove る and add られる)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.why: When talking about buildings, structures, or historical events where the builder is not important or is unknown, the sentence uses the passive form with the structure as the subject.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the intransitive verb 建つ to describe the structure rising and standing prominently, rather than emphasizing the act of building it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q6.kobun.tip: With the passive form for an object or structure, if you want to name the person or organization that created it, you must use 「によって」, not 「に」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vi: The doctor told me not to take a bath today.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.sk: N (person giving the instruction) に ＋ Vない形・V辞書形 ＋ ように ＋ 言われる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who gives the instruction in the passive structure.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は emphasizes the time period during which the restriction applies.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action of getting into the bath.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Vない ＋ ように expresses the content of an instruction or warning not to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 言う in the passive form shows that the speaker is the person receiving medical instructions.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.why: The indirect-reporting pattern 「〜ように」 combines with the passive form 「言われる」 to show that the speaker received advice or instructions from a professional.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows that the speaker personally gives instructions to someone else, which is the complete opposite direction of communication.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It directly quotes a prohibition that is stronger than the indirect instruction pattern ように.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.tip: Pay attention to the direction of the action: 「〜ように言われる」 means that I am told or instructed by someone else, while 「〜ように言う」 means that I tell or instruct someone else.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / Vない形 ＋ ように言われる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vi: I write in my notebook so that I will not forget what I learned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase (Vた + こと) combines with the particle を and serves as the object of the action in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.vi: so that I will not forget,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vない + ように connects a purpose clause that describes a negative state (so that it will not be forgotten).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the place or destination where the information is recorded.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate is in the polite form ます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.why: The sentence describes a deliberate action (writing in a notebook) to achieve the desired state in the first clause (not forgetting). A negative purpose clause must use Vないように.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 忘れないために would be grammatically incorrect because ために does not combine directly with the negative form Vない to express purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.tip: When you want to say "in order not to do... / so as not to be..." (a negative purpose), you must always use Vないように, not Vないために.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / Vない形 ＋ ように
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vi: Teacher: "Pun, your Japanese has really improved recently, hasn't it?" - Pun: "Thank you, teacher. Recently, I have become able to understand Japanese television dramas."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: It identifies the speaker in the first turn of the conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: A form of address used to call the other person's name directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject whose ability is being commented on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb that modifies the degree of the predicate 上手になりました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending な changes to に to modify the change verb なる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The past-tense verb なる is used with the particle ね to seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: Identifies the person responding in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: A polite way to thank someone in response to a compliment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: An adverb that indicates the point in time when a change occurs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: The particle の connects the noun 日本, which modifies ドラマ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: The particle が marks the object understood by the ability verb わかる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: The stative verb わかる combines with ように to show that the ability has been achieved.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.12.n: The polite past-tense form 〜ようになる describes the process of changing from not understanding to understanding.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.why: To describe a change in state or ability over time, from being unable to do something to being able to do it, use the non-volitional or ability verb わかる with the pattern 〜ようになる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using わかることになりました means that this understanding was arranged or decided by someone else or by outside circumstances, so it is unnatural when talking about personal ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.tip: Before ように in the pattern 〜ようになる, there must be an ability verb or a non-volitional verb, such as わかる, できる, or 見える. Do not use an ordinary volitional verb.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t13-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / V可能形 / Vない形 + ようになる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vi: Since today is an important party, I have decided to wear a suit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the time as the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective that modifies the noun パーティー immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern なので follows a noun to give an objective cause or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A verb clause that directly modifies the noun 服.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object that is chosen or decided on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に combines with します to show the result of a personal choice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The predicate forms the structure for deciding on a choice (〜にする).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.why: The grammar pattern 〜にする expresses a personal choice or decision from several available options, such as choosing a suit as the outfit. The preceding clause uses なので to give the reason for the decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using スーツになります means that the result naturally changes into a suit or is arranged by objective circumstances. It does not express the speaker's deliberate choice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish 〜にする, in which the speaker personally decides what to choose, from 〜になる, in which the result changes objectively or is decided by a group.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vi:
Yamamoto: "What will you order?"
Sato: "I choose curry."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Identifies the person asking the question in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A question word combined with the particle を to serve as the direct object of the verb 注文する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The main verb in polite form that ends the question about ordering food.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Identifies the person answering in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は presents the speaker as the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に combines with します to form the pattern 'Nにする', which expresses a choice or decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb する combines with 'Nに' to finalize the speaker's choice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.why: When ordering food or choosing between several options, the structure 'Nにする' is the most natural way to decide to choose that dish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a natural change into N, not the speaker's personal choice as in Nにする.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It simply describes the action 'I will eat curry' and does not clearly express the decision to choose the dish, as カレーにします does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particle を, saying カレーをします, instead of the particle に when they want to express a choice of dish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q10.kobun.cn: N + にする / にします
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vi: Because I have had a headache since this morning, I decided to go to the hospital near my home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から marks the time when the headache began.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the body part that is the subject of the adjective いたい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The conjunction ので connects a clause stating the objective reason that leads to the decision in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: Modifies the location noun 近く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action 行く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb in dictionary form combines with the pattern ことにした.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: The past-tense pattern 〜ことにする expresses a decision about an action made personally by the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.why: The first clause uses '〜ので' to give an objective reason, while the second clause uses '〜ことにした' to express a personal decision made by the speaker to deal with the situation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows that something was decided by a rule, objective circumstances, or another person, rather than by the speaker's own will.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows an effort to maintain a habit or keep trying to do something, rather than a definite decision made at one particular moment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse '〜ことにする', meaning that the speaker decides personally, with '〜ことになる', meaning that circumstances or a group makes the decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ことにする
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vi: If you have time, please be sure to try reading this book.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists for the verb ある.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb ある takes the たら form to set the hypothetical condition 'if there is time'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb used to make the advice or suggestion that follows more enthusiastic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun 本.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of reading.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 読む takes the て form to combine with the pattern てみてください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern 〜てみる combines with ください to give advice or suggest that the other person try doing something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.why: The first clause gives the condition 'たら'. The second clause uses the adverb 'ぜひ' together with the pattern '〜てみてください' to form a very polite and enthusiastic suggestion to try a new experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It is only a request or suggestion to 'read this book' and does not have the nuance of suggesting that the person try it to see what it is like.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: A question used to invite or encourage someone, meaning 'Would you like to try reading it?' It is more tentative than an enthusiastic recommendation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.tip: The pattern '〜てみてください' often goes with the adverb 'ぜひ' (definitely) to make the suggestion more enthusiastic. Do not confuse 'ぜひ' with 'ぜんぜん'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + みる / みてください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: At the meeting, it was decided that the entrance ceremony would be held on April 11.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で marks the context or place where the decision is made.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the event or object that receives the result of the change.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に follows a time reference to show the result of a change or the time that was decided.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb なります in the past tense shows that a state or event has completed its change.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: The sentence describes an event or date that was decided, 入学式が April 月 11 日になりました, through a process of group discussion at the meeting, 会議で.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses the speaker’s own subjective decision rather than an objective or group result.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often translate it into English as “decide the date...” and therefore easily confuse particle を with particle に before verb なる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.cn: N + になる / になりました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vi: For shoes, you should try them on before buying them and then check the size again.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes the noun “shoes” the main topic discussed in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern V辞書形 + 前に acts as a time complement showing when the next action should be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in form 〜て with みる expresses trying the action and then continuing to the next action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle を marks the size as the direct object to be checked.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vた + ほうがいいです acts as the predicate giving advice about what to do.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: Complete advice sentence: it states the topic with は, marks the time point with 〜前に, suggests trying the action with 〜てみて, and ends with the advice pattern 〜たほうがいいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes trying an action to see the result. If only the ordinary verb (はいて) is used, it does not have the meaning of trying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Gives specific advice about what should be done, with a stronger suggestion than an ordinary statement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: Remember to change the verb to form て before particle みる (はいてみて). Do not mistakenly use the dictionary form or past form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: I was very honored that you enjoyed my cooking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に marks the person who performs the action from which the speaker receives a favor in the pattern 〜ていただく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle の shows possession and modifies the noun “food.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を identifies the food as the direct object of the action of eating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: This humble predicate phrase expresses gratitude when a person of higher status performs an action for the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: The humble giving-and-receiving structure expresses that the speaker received consideration from the customer. The person performing the action goes with に, and the predicate ends in the humble form 〜ていただきました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Changes the grammatical subject to the customer (the customer ate for me), while 〜ていただきました focuses on the speaker (I had the customer eat for me).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This is an ordinary informal expression and is not suitable when the person performing the action is a customer (おきゃくさま).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.tip: In the pattern 〜ていただく/もらう, the person who performs the favor always takes particle に; particles を and が are not used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + いただく / いただきました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vi: The teacher took the time to visit my home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle が marks the teacher as the subject who performed the action of visiting the house.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle の shows possession and modifies the noun “house.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に marks the destination of the movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The honorific predicate form of 〜てくれた shows respect when a superior does something kind for the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.why: The subject is the teacher, a superior, who willingly did something kind for the speaker by visiting the house. Therefore, the sentence uses the honorific structure 〜てくださる with particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this only when the person doing the favor is a friend or someone junior. Using it with a teacher would be disrespectful.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Shifts the viewpoint toward the speaker (I had the teacher come to my house). In that case, the noun “teacher” must take particle に instead of が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.tip: Always distinguish these clearly: when a superior does something for you, that person goes with が and you use 〜てくださる; when you receive an action from a superior, that person goes with に and you use 〜ていただく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q5.kobun.cn: Vて + くださる / くださいました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vi: I will study hard and have decided to take the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test this year.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of manner modifying the action of studying with full effort.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in form て links the effort to study with the later decision to take the exam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: A time complement for the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle を marks the object affected by the action of taking the exam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vる + ことにする acts as the predicate expressing the speaker’s own subjective decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.why: The sentence describes a determination or choice made by the speaker after making an effort, so the pattern 〜ことにしました is used after the verb in dictionary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Shows that something was arranged by a group, organization, or objective circumstances, rather than decided by the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Only expresses an intention in one’s thoughts. It does not have the firm decision meaning of 〜ことにした.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 〜ことにする, meaning that the speaker decides personally, with 〜ことになる, meaning that something is decided by circumstances or other people.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ことにする / ことにしました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vi: I heard that it has been decided to open a supermarket near the station.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に marks the place where the supermarket will appear or be built.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle が marks the subject of the event of being built or opened (できる).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.3.vi: that it had been decided to open,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The quoted clause contains the pattern 〜ことになった, meaning that it was decided objectively, combined with particle と.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The main verb shows that the speaker received information from an outside source.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.why: The sentence reports information that was heard using the structure 〜と聞きました. Inside the quoted clause, 〜ことになった emphasizes that opening the supermarket was an objective decision made externally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Shows that the speaker personally decided to open the supermarket, so it does not fit a context in which the supermarket is opened because of urban planning or a company’s decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern 〜そうだ is also used to report heard information, but 〜と聞きました places clearer emphasis on the act of hearing the information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.tip: When talking about public buildings or social facilities that are built or opened, use 〜ことになる, which is objective, rather than 〜ことにする, which is subjective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ことになる / ことになった
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vi: If I have a chance to go to Japan, I would like to try climbing Mount Fuji once.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb used to emphasize the hypothetical meaning of the conditional clause たら that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に marks the destination of the movement verb 行く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in form たら creates a hypothetical “if... then...” clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing the number of times and modifying the later action of climbing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: Particle に marks the destination or target of the verb のぼる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: Verb のぼる changes to form て to connect with the pattern てみたい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.6.vi: would like to try doing it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern 〜てみたい expresses a wish to try doing something as an experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses “もし...たら” to set a condition for something that has not happened. The second clause uses “〜てみたい” to express the wish to experience an action for the first time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses the intention to “try doing” a specific action, without emphasizing a personal wish or desire as 〜てみたい does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: It only means wanting to climb and loses the meaning of wanting to try it as an experience found in 〜てみる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.tip: Do not mistake “〜てみる,” meaning “try doing it,” for an ordinary particle or verb related to looking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + みる / みたい / みます
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vi:
Teacher: "Has anyone checked the Japanese part of the report for you yet?"
Student: "Yes, Teacher Yamada corrected it for me."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: Identifies the speaker of the first sentence in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Modifies the noun 日本語 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the Japanese part the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The indefinite pronoun だれか with the particle が serves as the subject of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite past-tense question predicate ends the teacher's line.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: Only identifies the respondent in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle に marks a superior person who performs an action to help the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb なおす changes to the て form to combine with the honorific expression いただく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The humble form of もらう, showing gratitude for receiving help from a superior.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.why: When receiving help from a person of higher status (Teacher Yamada), the speaker uses the humble structure '〜ていただく' with the particle に, which marks the person who performs the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means 'someone did something to help me,' but it is informal and not polite or respectful enough when describing a teacher's action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Shows that someone helped the speaker in an ordinary way, but with a superior, 〜てくださいました must be used for proper politeness.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particle を instead of に before the helper in the structures 〜てもらう / 〜ていただく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t14-q9.kobun.cn: Vて + いただく / いただきます / いただきました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: A bicycle is useful for carrying things.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of carrying 運ぶ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The structure 'dictionary-form V + のに' shows the purpose or area of use of the predicate that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that is useful for the stated purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A part of the fixed expression やくに立つ (useful / practical).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The main verb combines with やくに to form the complete predicate phrase やくに立ちます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.why: The pattern 'V辞書形 + のに' expresses a purpose of use or an aspect of evaluation ('for...'), and it is usually followed by words describing functions or evaluations, such as 役に立つ and 便利だ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means 'in order to,' but '〜ために' emphasizes the intentional purpose of an action (the following clause describes a volitional action), while '〜のに' emphasizes usefulness or a quality.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: When it means 'although / even so,' '〜のに' connects two contrasting clauses and expresses the speaker's surprise or dissatisfaction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse '〜のに,' which shows purpose or use (the verb is always in the dictionary form), with '〜のに,' which shows contrast (it uses the plain form and carries a feeling of dissatisfaction).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のに（役に立つ / 便利だ / 使う / 時間がかかる）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vi:
Yamamoto: "Yan, how is life in Japan?"
Yan: "It is fun, but money is very difficult. The biggest problem is the rent."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name together with a form of address for the other person in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun with の modifies the noun せいかつ that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes life in Japan the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: An interrogative predicate phrase asking about the situation, followed by a line break to Yan's speech.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending in い combines with ですが to connect two clauses with a mild contrast.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the aspect or object that is difficult.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective ending in な functions as a predicate expressing a difficult situation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: An adverb showing the highest degree, modifying the phrase 問題な.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: The adjective phrase ending in な combines with なのは to form the topic of a cleft sentence and prepare to emphasize the predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: The noun combines with です and serves as the key information emphasized at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.why: Yan uses a cleft sentence with のは to turn the content 問題な into the topic of the sentence, directing all attention and emphasis to the noun やちん in the final predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: A normal statement would only state the fact and would not highlight the main information as strongly as the cleft pattern のは.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.tip: When using the structure のは, the adjective ending in な must keep な before の (such as 問題なのは); learners often forget this and connect them directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + のは 〜 です
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vi: The thing I left on the bus is a paper bag.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The subject in the subordinate modifying clause is marked by the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the place where the object was left in the forgetting action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb combines with のは to nominalize the clause and make it the topic of a cleft sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: A noun showing material combines with の to modify the noun ふくろ that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate is a noun for an object, presented as the main point to be emphasized.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.why: The clause 私がバスに忘れた is nominalized by のは to turn known information into the topic, directing the listener's attention to the new information, 紙のふくろ, in the predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: A normal statement would simply describe the act of forgetting an item and would not emphasize the identity of the item as the cleft structure does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.tip: In the subordinate clause before のは, the subject must use the particle が rather than は to avoid confusing it with the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + のは 〜 です
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vi: I am saving money to buy a cool car.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the car as the object of the action of buying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 買うために shows the purpose of saving money.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: している describes an action in progress.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.why: The clause 買うために states the purpose and comes before the main action ちょきんしている. 車を is the direct object of 買う, so it uses を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ように, the sentence usually emphasizes a goal or a state to be achieved rather than the purpose of an intentional action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse using のために after a verb; after a verb, the dictionary form + ために is required.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + ために
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vi: To prepare for the July exam, I study for 10 hours every day.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase showing a time point modifies the noun meaning exam that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The structure N のために expresses the purpose of the study action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb of frequency directly modifies the predicate verb.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: A quantity expression showing the length of the study action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the ています form describes a habit repeated every day.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「N + のために」 to clearly identify the purpose. The second clause combines a frequency expression, a quantity expression, and the ending 「〜ています」 to emphasize that the action continues as a regular habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If using 「7月の試験に合格できるように」, the sentence would emphasize creating the conditions for or reaching the state of passing the exam rather than a willful action directed toward the event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.tip: Remember that ために used directly with a noun must have the particle の (N のために); do not connect N ために directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: On Saturday, I talked on the phone with my partner for as long as five hours.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に goes with a specific time point in the week.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と indicates the person who takes part in the conversation with the subject.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle も follows a quantity to emphasize that it is more than usual.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is in the past tense and describes a completed action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.why: The sentence places the time adverb and the other participant at the beginning, then places the quantity combined with the particle 「も」 immediately before the predicate to highlight surprise at the length of the call.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「５時間しか電話しませんでした」 is used, the meaning changes completely to express that the amount was small: they could make a call for only five hours.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: The particle も follows a quantity in an affirmative sentence and means “as many as.” Do not confuse it with the structure しか, which always goes with a negative sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vi: I work part-time to earn money for tuition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を identifies the object of the verb している.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: the activity I am doing is,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Use の to turn the clause into a noun phrase, then combine it with は to make the part-time job the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action はらう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The structure V辞書形 + ためです serves as the predicate and explains the main purpose of the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.why: The sentence uses the emphasis pattern 「〜のは、…ためです」 to make the event in the first clause the background and highlight the purpose of the action in the final predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「がくひをはらうからです」 is used, the sentence simply explains a reason or cause instead of emphasizing an active purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.tip: Before ためです, the verb that explains the purpose must always be in the dictionary form (V辞書形), not in the ます form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ためだ/ためです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vi: Going to Kyushu by plane costs about 30,000 yen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of an action involving movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure V辞書形 + のに is used to state the purpose for which time or money is spent.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: A quantity combines with くらい to estimate the necessary cost.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate verb shows that money or time is spent.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.why: When describing money or time spent for a purpose, Japanese uses 「V辞書形＋のに」 to make the scope being evaluated clear before the verb かかります.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「行くために３万円くらいかかります」 is used, it sounds unnatural because Japanese normally uses のに when talking about costs or time spent.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse ために with のに when talking about the cost or time required (かかります/必要です).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・N ＋ のに（用途・評価・費用）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vi: Mr. Miura went to Italy to study music.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person's name the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the study action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure V辞書形 + ために expresses the intentional purpose of studying abroad.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of studying abroad.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate verb is in the past tense and indicates a completed action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.why: Because both actions—studying music and studying abroad—have the same subject and clearly express intention, the pattern 「ために」 is chosen to connect the purpose with the main action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「音楽を勉強できるように」 is used, the sentence changes to express a purpose that creates the conditions or ability to study music.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.tip: When both verbs are intentional actions performed by the same subject, ために must be used instead of ように.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vi: When studying Japanese, I think the most difficult thing is grammar.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of studying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern 〜とき connects a subordinate clause that sets the time context.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing the highest degree modifies the adjective that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Use の to turn an adjective ending in い into a noun phrase, then combine it with は to create an emphasized topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle と introduces the evaluated content that comes before the verb of thinking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate verb expresses the speaker's opinion or thought.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.why: The sentence begins with a context clause「〜とき」, then uses the emphasized noun-forming structure「〜のは…だ」inside the phrase expressing an opinion「〜と思います」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「いちばんむずかしいことは」 is used, the sentence sounds more formal and written, while のは is more natural and familiar in conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.tip: Before the noun-forming phrase「のは」, an adjective ending in い keeps its い form; do not insert だ or な between them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q7.kobun.cn: 普通形（Aなだ→な・Nだ→な）＋ のは ＋ N だ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vi: To catch the 8 o'clock flight, I left home at half past five.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A time noun phrase modifies the noun ひこうき that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the vehicle or object that one comes into contact with or boards, together with the verb 乗る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb combines with ために to express an intentional purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に follows a specific time and indicates when the action takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を goes with the verb 出る to indicate the place from which someone starts or leaves.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate is conjugated in the polite past tense.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses V-る ＋ ために to express the speaker's intentional purpose. The second clause uses the particle に to indicate the time and を to indicate the starting point, stating the specific action taken to achieve that purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ように, the first clause usually has to go with a potential verb or an intransitive verb, so it is unnatural with an intentional verb such as 乗る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle marking the place of departure with から or で, but with the verb 出る, the particle を must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vi: The most difficult thing about life in Japan is that food is expensive.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun combines with の to modify the noun せいかつ that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で limits the scope of the comparison.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb showing the highest degree modifies たいへんな.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending な combines with なのは to nominalize the quality and make it the topic of a cleft sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The subject of the predicate clause explains the content.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending い directly modifies the noun こと that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The noun こと nominalizes the clause that explains the matter, and combines with です to form the main predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.why: The sentence uses the cleft structure 〜のは…ことです to state a specific situation (food is expensive) and clearly explain the content emphasized in the topic (the most difficult thing).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If you only say 〜のは食べ物が高いです and leave out ことです, the sentence structure is incomplete because when the first part nominalizes a matter, the second part also needs to package it with こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence would simply compare the prices of different goods. It would not express that expensive food is the most difficult thing in life.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.tip: When the emphasized predicate is a complete clause rather than a single noun, ことです must appear at the end of the sentence to nominalize that clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のは 〜 ことです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vi: I heard that a new teacher will come next year.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A future time expression used as the time adverbial for the subordinate clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い directly modifies the noun 先生 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The subject of the action 来る in the subordinate clause, marked by the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.3.vi: there is a plan to come
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern という follows the clause and explains its detailed content in apposition to the noun 話.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The direct object of the verb 聞きました, receiving the entire preceding part as its modifying content.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate is conjugated in the polite past form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.why: The pattern という links a complete content clause with the abstract noun 話, giving specific details about the story that was heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If という is omitted and the parts are connected directly, the sentence sounds abrupt and unnatural when conveying complete information or a rumor.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 先生が来るそうです, the sentence becomes a direct report of information. It does not form a noun phrase that serves as the object of 聞きました, as in the pattern という 話.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.tip: Before the pattern という, N must always be a clause in the plain form, even when the sentence ending is the polite form ます or です.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.cn: 普通形 ＋ という ＋ N
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vi: Sato: “I am planning to go to Okinawa in September.” Yamada: “There are many typhoons in September, so you should not go.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時 point に ＋ N に ＋ V意向形 ＋ と思っている ＋ んだ ／ N は ＋ N が ＋ Aい ＋ から、Vないほうがいい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker’s name appears before the quoted words.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of 行く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 行こうと思っている expresses an intention; んだ adds an explanatory tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The next speaker’s name appears before the quoted words.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: は makes September the topic for a comment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks the subject of the adjective 多い.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: から connects the reason to the advice in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: Vないほうがいい is used to give advice to avoid an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.why: The time and destination come before the verb 行く. The clause with 台風が多いから gives the reason, and then 行かないほうがいい gives suitable advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced here, the sentence becomes advice to go instead of advice not to go.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the intention is stated more directly and firmly 思っている.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse ほうがいい, which is used only for things one should do; the form Vないほうがいい means that one should not do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と思っている; Vない形 ＋ ほうがいい; 普通形 ＋ から
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vi: Because work is busy, I do not watch as much television as before these days.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the cause and the subject of the busy state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い changes to くて to connect with the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: は indicates the time period being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of 見る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: それほど modifies 見なくなりました and is usually used with a negative expression.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 見ない＋なる expresses a change to a state of no longer watching.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.why: 仕事がいそがしくて gives the reason, while 最近は limits the time of the change. The object テレビを comes before 見る, and 見なくなる shows that the habit has changed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says that the state of not watching is continuing. It does not emphasize a change in the habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q4.kobun.tip: Do not connect directly with 見ないなる; use the form 見なくなる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vi: If I study abroad in Japan, I must get a passport.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where studying abroad takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: なら connects a condition or assumption with the conclusion in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing on which the action 取る must be performed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: なくてはいけない expresses an obligation to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.why: The conditional clause 留学するなら comes before the necessary requirement. パスポートを is the object of the action, while なくてはいけません turns that action into an obligation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたら is used instead, the sentence focuses more on a condition occurring or being completed, rather than simply stating an assumption like なら.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning of obligation is almost the same, but the tone is more formal and rigid.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may forget て in なくてはいけない; do not say なくはいけない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ なら; Vない形 ＋ なくてはいけない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vi: You must not take a day off without contacting the company.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person or organization receiving the notice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ないで connects the omitted action with the main action, meaning that the first action is not done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.2.vi: must not take a day off
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: てはいけない expresses something that is prohibited.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.why: 会社に identifies the place or person to contact. れんらくしないで shows the missing condition before taking a day off, and then 休んではいけません states the prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a polite request not to do something, which is softer than a prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is close to ないで, but it is more formal and often appears in written language.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.tip: ないで here does not mean “please do not do”; it connects two actions with the meaning “without doing.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q6.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ ないで; Vて形 ＋ はいけない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vi: To carry many drinks, could you lend me your car? The given sentence repeats the request once more after ので.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさんの modifies the noun 飲み物.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being transported.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb＋のに expresses purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the item being requested to borrow.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.4.vi: could you lend it to me
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: てあげる／もらう combines with the negative potential form to make a polite request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ので usually connects a reason to a result, but here it comes after a complete question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: を continues to mark the car as the item being requested to borrow.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.7.vi: could you lend it to me
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern てもらえませんか ends the polite request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のに（purpose）; Vて ＋ もらえませんか（request）; 普通形 ＋ ので（reason）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.why: 運ぶのに states the purpose of borrowing the car, and 車を貸してもらえませんか forms the request. In the given sequence, ので comes after a complete question, and the request is repeated, so the whole sentence is structurally unnatural.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used in the correct position after a reason clause, it connects the reason to the result more gently than から.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is replaced with ために, the purpose is expressed more formally and clearly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse のに, which indicates purpose, with のに, which means “although”; look at the clause that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vi: Because Yoshida is very busy, he may not be able to come.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces Yoshida as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: すごく modifies the adjective いそがしい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.3.vi: may not be able to come
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 来られない is the negative potential form, while かもしれない expresses uncertain possibility.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.why: は introduces Yoshida as the topic, and すごくいそがしいので then gives the reason. 来られない expresses the inability to come, while かもしれません lowers the level of certainty to a guess.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with でしょう, the prediction sounds more like something the speaker believes to be true than かもしれない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来ない is used, it only says that he may not come; it does not emphasize that he cannot come.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.tip: 来られない means “cannot come,” unlike 来ない, which means “does not come” because of a wish or decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t16-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; V普通形 ＋ かもしれない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vi: Because she is intelligent, she will probably pass the exam for sure.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that she is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the adjective いい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the object or target of passing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: だろう is placed at the end of the sentence to express a prediction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects to the result with から. だろう comes at the end of the sentence, so the speaker predicts the possibility of passing based on the previous information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing だろう with でしょう keeps almost the same meaning of prediction but makes it more polite.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Using はずだ expresses a stronger basis for the expectation, close to “she is sure to pass.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily think that から can only follow a noun; in fact, it can also connect to a clause in the ordinary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ だろう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: "Is Ms. Inoue taking the day off?" - Tanaka: "I heard that she fell down the stairs and was injured."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The name of the person asking the question opens the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the person being asked about as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.2.vi: is she taking the day off?"
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun combines with ですか to form a polite question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The name of the person answering in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle から indicates the starting place of the falling action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb in the て form connects an earlier action in time order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.6.vi: I heard that she was injured."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern V(た形) + らしいです expresses information heard from someone else, with the particle よ emphasizing that the information is new.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.why: Tanaka did not directly witness Inoue's accident. Tanaka only heard about it from someone else, so Tanaka uses the reporting pattern 「〜らしい」 to explain the reason to Yamamoto.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This also reports information heard from someone else, but it simply passes on the information, while らしい also shows that the speaker trusts the source.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This expresses a subjective judgment based on direct observation, so it is not suitable for reporting news received from a third person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.tip: When reporting information heard from another person that you did not see yourself, use らしい or そうだ instead of making a direct statement in the ordinary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ らしい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vi: Because the western sky is bright, the weather will probably be very fine tomorrow.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the noun sky by showing direction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the subordinate clause expressing the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending い combines with the particle から to give the factual basis for the prediction in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は marks the time point as the topic of the weather prediction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb showing a high degree; it modifies the following adverb よく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb showing favorable weather; it modifies the verb はれる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern V(dictionary form) + だろう expresses the speaker's prediction or estimate about a future event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.why: The first part gives evidence from an observed phenomenon through 「から」 (the western sky is bright), providing a basis for the second part's well-founded weather prediction with 「〜だろう」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This expresses an uncertain possibility, only about 50% or less, while だろう shows greater confidence and a higher possibility, about 70–80%.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This means “will certainly,” based on an unavoidable rule or absolute evidence, and is much stronger than the natural prediction of だろう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.tip: 「だろう」 is the ordinary form of 「でしょう」. It connects directly to verbs and adjectives ending in い, but with adjectives ending in な and nouns, だ must be removed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹・N ＋ だろう / でしょう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vi: Mr. Nakamura looks very sad because his precious watch is broken.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the main subject/topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な directly modifies the noun watch.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the intransitive verb for breaking, こわれる, in the reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the て form indicates the reason leading to the emotional state in the following part.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Aい (remove い) + そうでした expresses the speaker's observation of another person's past emotional state through outward appearance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.cn: Aい語幹（remove い）・Aな語幹 ＋ そうだ / そうでした
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.why: Because sadness is the internal feeling of a third person, Mr. Nakamura, which the speaker can observe only through his expression, the appearance-based prediction ending 「〜そうでした」 must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this directly only for the speaker's own emotions, in the first person. Do not use it to directly state another person's inner feelings.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This describes another person's specific outward actions or behavior showing sadness that the speaker directly observes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q12.kobun.tip: Do not directly use an adjective expressing an inner emotion, such as 悲しい or 嬉しい, for the third person. Use the inference structures 〜そうだ / 〜ようだ or the auxiliary predicate 〜がる instead.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vi: Because I got wet in the rain, I look like I am about to catch a cold.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the reason why the speaker got wet.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the previous clause to the following clause, while しまう emphasizes that the event happened unintentionally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb ひく in the expression かぜをひく.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです is attached to the verb stem to talk about signs or the possibility of something about to happen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.why: で gives the reason, and then てしまって connects it to the unwanted result. そうです comes at the end to make a prediction based on the current signs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ようだ focuses on a conclusion based on the situation or evidence, not only on outward signs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using らしい usually presents information heard from someone else or a more objective judgment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.tip: Do not attach そうです directly to the dictionary form of a verb. Use the stemます, such as ひきそうです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹・Aい（いを除く）・Aな語幹 ＋ そうだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vi: According to the weather forecast, I heard that it will be sunny tomorrow.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: によると indicates the source of the information supporting the following statement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that tomorrow is the time being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.vi: I heard that it will be sunny
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: らしい follows a clause in the ordinary form to report information that was heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: The information source is introduced with によると, followed by the time topic with は. らしい at the end shows that this statement is based on reported information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: そうだ in its reporting meaning聞 can also mean “I heard that,” but its tone is more direct in passing on the information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Using でしょう turns the sentence into the speaker's prediction and does not emphasize the information source.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the reporting らしい聞 with そうだ, which only indicates a sign; before らしい, use a clause in the ordinary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ らしい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: The friend I had not seen for a long time looks very healthy.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に turns the time phrase into an adverbial phrase that modifies 会った.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form comes before a noun to modify ともだち.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks the friend as the topic of the comment that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: そうでした describes an appearance observed at a past time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.why: The clause 会った comes directly before ともだち to identify which friend. そうでした comes at the end because the speaker comments on the friend's appearance at the time they met.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This form suggests an inference or a recollection based on evidence, rather than simply an impression from seeing something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This form usually means that people say the person is healthy, and it does not have to come from direct observation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: A clause that modifies a noun must come before the noun, so 会ったともだち means “the friend I met,” not the reverse order used in English.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.cn: Aな語幹 + そうだ; Vます形の語幹 + そうだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vi: Since you are no longer a child, you must speak like an adult.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: では combines with ない to negate the noun 子ども.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: のだから gives a reason with an explanatory or reminding tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: らしい comes after a noun to modify 話し方 and shows a quality suitable for adults.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the way of speaking as the object of the required action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.5.vi: if one does not do it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: しなければ is a negative conditional form that combines with なりません to create the meaning of obligation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: なりません completes the double negative pattern meaning “must.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.why: The clause ないのだから gives the reason, while 大人らしい modifies 話し方 to describe the required way of speaking. なければなりません comes at the end to express obligation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing らしい with のような emphasizes resemblance to an adult rather than a quality naturally suitable for adults.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means “must speak,” but it directly uses the verb 話す instead of focusing on the “way of speaking.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may misunderstand なければ as “if not”; when it goes with なりません, the whole phrase means that one must do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q5.kobun.cn: N + らしい; Vない形のなければ + なりません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vi: Since there is a festival tomorrow, the town will probably be very lively.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic of the reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the noun おまつり to the result clause to give a reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は shifts the topic to the town, whose condition is being predicted.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: でしょう comes at the end of the sentence to predict the town's condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.why: だから explains the reason in the first clause, and the sentence then shifts to the main topic, 町. でしょう comes at the end to give a polite prediction about how lively the town will be.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is almost the same, but だろう sounds more casual or direct.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using はずです shows a prediction based on stronger evidence, close to “it should definitely be lively.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.tip: With the adjective な, keep the dictionary form before でしょう as in にぎやかでしょう, and do not add な.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + でしょう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vi: Since I did not study much, I do not seem likely to pass the exam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of degree, usually used with a negative form to express a low degree.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the negative past form combines with the particle から to give the reason for the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the goal or target of passing the exam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.3.vi: does not seem likely to pass
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern V(remove ます) + そうもありません expresses a strong negative judgment, meaning that something is almost impossible.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.cn: Vstem（ます形 remove ます） + そうにない / そうもない / そうにもない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason—studying little—using 「から」. The second clause then uses the strong negative prediction pattern 「〜そうもありません」 to emphasize that the chance of passing the exam is almost zero.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It is only an ordinary negative form meaning “does not seem...,” without the strong sense of “having no chance at all” found in そうもありません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It is mainly used as the negative form for adjectives or nouns when making an appearance-based judgment, and it does not combine directly with verbs like そうにない / そうもない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q7.kobun.tip: To make a negative appearance-based judgment about a verb, change it to V(remove ます) + そうにない / そうもない, rather than combining Vない + そうだ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vi: According to my friend in Japan, I hear that the cherry blossoms in Kyoto are very beautiful.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the noun for friend that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern N + によると clearly shows the source of the information received.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の indicates a place and modifies the noun for cherry blossoms.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は marks the main topic described and commented on in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb showing a high degree, modifying the adjective きれい that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern Aな (remove な) + らしいです expresses information heard from another person or an inference based on outside evidence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.why: The sentence begins with 「〜によると」 to introduce an indirect source, so it must end with the corresponding reporting or inference pattern 「〜らしいです」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This is also used to report information, but it presents it as a completely exact report, while らしい also suggests an inference from that information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used when the speaker observes something directly with the senses and makes a judgment, and it is not used directly with a phrase showing the information source, 〜によると.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in な combines with らしい, use the basic form without な, such as きれいらしい, and do not add な or だ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹・N + らしい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vi: Tanaka: "What are you doing? You look like you are having fun." - Yamada: "It is a new game."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The name of the first speaker in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the question object of the action している.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the ている form combines with the particle の at the end of the sentence to ask casually.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.3.vi: you look like you are having fun."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Aい (remove い) + そうだ expresses an intuitive judgment based on visual observation of someone's appearance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The name of the second speaker who replies in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending in い directly modifies the noun for game that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The noun combines with the ending だよ to explain and give information casually to the other person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.cn: Aい語幹（ remove い）・Aな語幹 + そうだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.why: Tanaka directly sees Yamada's actions and facial expression, so he naturally uses the appearance-description pattern 「〜そうだ」 to comment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a more careful logical inference based on several clues, rather than the quick visual impression expressed by そうだ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: It means information heard from another person or an indirect judgment, so it is not suitable when speaking directly to the person being described.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t17-q9.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in い connects to the appearance-description pattern そうだ, the ending い must be removed (楽しい -> 楽しそうだ), while いい changes to よさそうだ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vi: Because my part-time job is busy, the time I have for studying is gradually decreasing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the clause that gives the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い changes to the て form to connect clauses and show the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb directly modifies the noun 時間 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the change in state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending い changes to the くなって form to express a change in state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜てくる describes a continuous change that has continued from the past to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.why: The first clause uses the て form to state that the part-time job is busy. The second clause uses the change structure 少なくなる together with the pattern 〜てくる to describe the gradual decrease in study time from the past up to the time of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes a changing trend that will continue from the present into the future, rather than from the past to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.tip: Note the difference between 〜てくる (a change from the past to the present) and 〜ていく (a change from the present toward the future).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q1.kobun.cn: Vて形 + くる / きました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vi:
Yamamoto: "What a beautiful watch."
    Tanaka: "Thank you. I have continued using it for about 10 years."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.sk: Aな + N ですね + approximate duration + Vます-stem + 続ける + ています
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name comes before 「 to open the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: すてきな modifies the noun 時計.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね ends the comment and adds a feeling of agreement and admiration.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Tanaka's name opens the second line of dialogue after the line break.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The expression of thanks stands alone and ends with a punctuation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: くらい indicates an approximate length of time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: 使い＋つづける expresses continuing to do something, and ています shows that the state continues up to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.why: The first line is a comment about the watch. After saying thank you, the period of 10 years acts as an adverbial phrase for the continuous use of the watch, expressed with 使い続けています.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If you only say 使っています, it means that someone is using it or still uses it, without stressing that the action has continued for a long time.
