default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 使い始めています, it means that someone is starting to use it, which is the opposite of the meaning of continuing to use it for many years.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate 続ける as a separate action. It follows the ます-less form of the preceding verb to create the meaning of continuing to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q10.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + 続ける; Vている
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vi: After starting work, my son has become fatter.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose change is being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に＋なる expresses a change into a new state, and て connects it to the result that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 太ってくる describes a change that has gradually progressed toward the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.why: 社会人になって gives the point when the circumstances changed, and then て connects it to the physical change. てくる shows that the process of becoming fatter has occurred and that the result is clear in the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 太っている, it only describes the state of being fat and does not stress the process of becoming fat.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 太っていく is used, the direction of the change is viewed from the present toward the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.tip: てくる in this sentence does not mean moving here. It only indicates a gradual change leading to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q11.kobun.cn: N + に + なる; Vて + くる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vi: After finishing the meal, please clean up.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food that is eaten.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べ＋おわる expresses completing the action of eating, and then たら connects it to the request that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: てください is used to make a polite request to clean up.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.why: 食べおわったら creates a time point when eating is finished. After that point, かたづけてください requests the next action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べてから is used, it only says that the next action happens after eating, while 食べおわったら stresses that the eating is completely finished.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.tip: たら here attaches to the past form 食べおわった, not directly to 食べる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q12.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + 終わる; Vた形 + ら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vi: After the presenter finishes speaking, please ask questions.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.sk: V-ている + N が + Vます without ます + おわってから + V-てください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The ている-form verb phrase acts as a modifier for the noun 人.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the doer of the presentation in the modifying clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜おわってから combines the compound verb 〜おわる with 〜てから to show the order after an action has been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The main verb changes to the て form to combine with the request pattern ください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: A polite request pattern asking the other person to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.cn: Vます (without ます) + おわる / おわって
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.why: The sentence uses a modifying clause for the noun person, combines the compound verb V-おわる with the pattern 〜てから to set the action order, and then gives the polite request 〜てください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It marks the time after speaking has started, rather than after speaking is completely finished.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It also expresses the order after doing something, but V-おわってから clearly stresses that the speaker has completed the whole presentation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q2.kobun.tip: The compound verb 〜おわる combines only with a verb in the V-ます form without ます. It does not combine with the dictionary form or the て form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vi: Because I kept waiting for more than one hour in front of the ramen shop, I became extremely hungry.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.sk: 数量 + 以上 + N の 前で + Vます without ます + つづけて、 + N が + V-ました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A quantity phrase indicating the length of time the waiting action continued.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の links the place noun with the location noun that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the waiting action occurs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The compound verb 〜つづける changes to the て form. It both shows a continuous action and connects to the clause giving the result.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が combines with the noun おなか to form the subject of the hungry state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate verb combines with the preceding noun to form an idiomatic expression meaning to be hungry.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.cn: Vます (without ます) + つづける / つづけて
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.why: The sentence uses the compound verb V-つづける to stress that the waiting continued for more than one hour. It then changes to the て form to connect to the hungry result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It indicates that the action of waiting has just begun, instead of continuing for a long period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It stresses completing the waiting action instead of highlighting the long waiting process.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q3.kobun.tip: The compound verb 〜つづける combines only with the V-ます form without ます to show a continuous action. Do not confuse it with the adverb ずっと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vi: After thinking for a while, Meinan began to talk about their family.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.sk: N は + 副詞 + V-た + あと、 + N の こと を + Vます without ます + だしました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the person being discussed as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb indicating the short length of time spent thinking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-form verb た modifies the noun あと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The noun あと connects the two clauses in time order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle の links the noun 家族 to modify the noun こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を identifies the direct object affected by the action of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The compound verb V-だす describes an action that begins suddenly and comes out.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.cn: Vます (without ます) + だす / だしました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.why: The sentence uses the pattern V-たあと to show that the thinking was completed first. It then uses the compound verb V-だす to describe the sudden beginning of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means to begin, but V-はじめる describes an intentional beginning that follows a normal process, while V-だす has a more sudden and spontaneous feeling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It indicates that the storytelling has been completed, instead of just beginning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.kobun.tip: The pattern V-だす combines only with V-ます without ます. It is used for sudden beginnings, not for events that have been scheduled in advance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q4.tokens.3.m: for a while, for a short time
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vi: My father came home early today.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は combines with a time expression to set the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of returning home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 早く functions as an adverb and modifies the time of the verb.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb changes to the て form to connect with an auxiliary verb showing the direction of movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜てくる describes movement toward the speaker's location.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.why: The sentence describes the father's return toward the place where the speaker is present (at home), so it uses the structure V-てきました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes movement away from the speaker's location instead of movement closer to it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.tip: Pay attention to the speaker's viewpoint when using 〜てくる (movement toward the speaker's location) and 〜ていく (movement away from the speaker's location).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q5.kobun.cn: Vて形 + くる / きました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vi: Even after getting married, I will not quit my job. I will keep working forever.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The pattern 〜てからも means that even after an event happens, the following action continues.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the object of the action of quitting a job.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite negative verb form expresses the determination not to quit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb describes a continuous state without interruption that extends into the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb changes to the て form and combines with an auxiliary verb showing an ongoing direction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜ていく describes an action that continues and carries on into the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the structure 〜てからも to show that the plan will not change even after entering marriage. The second sentence uses 〜ていく to express the intention to keep working into the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes an action that has continued from the past to the present instead of continuing toward the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 〜ていく (an action continuing from the present into the future) with 〜てくる (an action progressing from the past to the present).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q6.kobun.cn: Vて形 + いく / いきます
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vi: She looked at my face and suddenly burst into tears.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who performs the actions in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the owner to the noun 顔.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being looked at.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action of looking with the next action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: に changes the adjective な 急 into an adverb that modifies the action of crying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: なきだす is the form Vます-stem なき + だす, expressing the beginning of crying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.why: The sentence places the person performing the action first, followed by the object of looking. The form 見て connects the earlier action with the following result, while なきだす emphasizes the sudden beginning of crying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with なき始めました, it still means beginning to cry, but the meaning is more neutral and does not emphasize suddenness as だす does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may understand 見て as only meaning the action of looking, but in this sentence it also connects two consecutive actions.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vi: After you finish drinking the soft drink, please throw the plastic bottle into the trash can.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the drink being consumed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 飲み + おわる creates the meaning of finishing drinking, and then たら connects it to the following action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being thrown away.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the plastic bottle is thrown.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: てください is used to make a polite request or ask someone to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.why: The clause 飲みおわったら sets a time condition for the request that follows. The object being thrown away uses を, while the receiving place uses に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 飲んでから, it means to do the next action after drinking, but it does not emphasize that the drink was finished.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 飲んだあとで is used, it only states the order after drinking, with less emphasis on completing the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use を after ゴミばこ because the trash can is the destination of the action, so に must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q8.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + 終わる; Vた形 + ら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vi: Jun: I am worried that I may not pass tomorrow's exam. Teacher: You have been working hard all this time, so you will be fine.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name comes before the mark 「 to open the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a time with the noun 試験 that it modifies.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object or goal of passing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause ending in か states what Jun is worried about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 心配です is the predicate expressing worry and ending the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The line break and the speaker's name open the second dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: は states that Jun is the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: ずっと modifies the action of working hard continuously.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: てくる expresses continuation up to the present, while ので connects the reason to the conclusion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: だいじょうぶ states the conclusion, while よ adds a reassuring tone for the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.why: The clause ごうかくできるか states the content of the worry, while 試験に marks the goal of passing. ずっと + がんばってきた show effort continuing up to the present, providing a basis for the teacher's reassurance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If がんばっている is used instead, it only says that someone is working hard now and does not emphasize the process continuing from the past until now.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If がんばってきたから is used, the reason is more direct and informal than ので.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may leave out て in がんばってきた, but て is required to connect the action with くる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t18-q9.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; V普通形・Aい + ので; Aな + な + ので; N + な + ので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vi: I drank too much cold water, so I got a stomachache.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective ending in い stays in its basic form and directly modifies the noun 水 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of drinking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb changes to the Vます form by removing ます and combines with すぎて to show that excessive action as the reason for the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the body part negatively affected by the predicate こわしました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.4.vi: got a stomachache / had digestive problems.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The phrase おなかをこわす is the main predicate of the sentence in the polite past tense, describing having a stomachache.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.cn: Vます形（remove ます）・Aい（remove い）・Aな（remove な） + すぎる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.why: The structure 〜すぎて is placed in the first clause to show that the cause made something exceed the normal level, leading to the unwanted bad result in the second clause, おなかをこわしました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the dictionary form of the grammar pattern. It generally means doing something too much or having a quality at too high a level.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 飲みながら, the sentence means drinking water and having a stomachache at the same time, which is illogical as a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q1.kobun.tip: When combining an adjective or verb with すぎる, learners often forget to remove the verb ending ます or the adjective ending い/な.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vi:
Smith: "Is Hokkaido cold?"
Yamamoto: "It is not as cold as Alaska."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name begins the line of dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は sets Hokkaido as the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 寒い acts as the question predicate with the ending ですか to ask for information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The respondent's name begins the answer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle ほど follows the noun used as the comparison standard and means 'to the level of/as much as Alaska'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective's polite negative form combines with ほど to create the unequal comparison structure 'not as cold as'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Aくない・Aくありません (or Vない / Aではない)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.why: Smith uses a question with the adjective 寒い to ask about Hokkaido's weather. Yamamoto uses the unequal comparison pattern 'N ほど + negative', taking Alaska as the highest standard and stating that Hokkaido does not reach that level of coldness.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If アラスカより寒くない is used, the sentence expresses a negative comparative meaning, but it is less natural than 'N ほど + negative' when highlighting the highest point of comparison.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If アラスカくらい寒くない is used, the sentence is grammatically incorrect because くらい is not used to express an unequal comparison structure ('not as...as').
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q10.kobun.tip: When the structure 'N ほど' means 'not as ... as N', the predicate in the following clause must be in the NEGATIVE form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vi: This company's products break easily, so I do not want to buy them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative word comes before and modifies the noun 会社.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun phrase + の modifies the noun しょうひん that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes 'this company's products' the main topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb takes the ending やすい to describe the property of breaking easily, and combines with から to state the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.4.vi: I do not want to buy them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 買う changes to the polite negative desire form and acts as the main predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.cn: Vます(remove ます) ＋ やすい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.why: The sentence makes 'this company's products' the topic with は. It uses a reason clause with から and the pattern やすい (easy to break) to provide a logical basis for refusing to buy them (たくありません) in the main clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to こわれにくいから, the sentence has the completely opposite meaning: 'because it is difficult to break...'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If こわれがち is used, it suggests that something often tends to break, while やすい emphasizes the property of being easy to break.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q11.kobun.tip: Both 〜やすい and 〜にくい attach directly to the verb stem in the ます form after removing ます (for example: 壊れます → 壊れやすい).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vi: Because I drank coffee at night, I could not fall asleep for a long time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に identifies the time when the action of drinking coffee took place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object directly affected by the action 飲む.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb's past form combines with the particle から to state the cause or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb なかなか combines with a negative potential predicate to describe struggling and being unable to sleep.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The group 2 verb ねる changes to the plain negative potential form and acts as the predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.why: The sentence shows a cause-and-effect relationship: the first clause states the action of 'drinking coffee at night' with the conjunction から, leading to the result in the second clause—being unable to sleep for a long time—with the adverb なかなか and a negative potential verb.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 全然ねられない is used, it emphasizes a complete 0% result: not being able to sleep even for a moment. なかなか emphasizes that the person tried to fall asleep but could not for a long time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If どうしてもねられない is used, it suggests 'even after trying every possible way, I still cannot sleep'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.tip: Distinguish these meanings: なかなか with an affirmative sentence means 'quite/relatively', but with a negative sentence it means 'cannot... even after a long time'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q12.kobun.cn: なかなか ＋ V可能形否定 / Vない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vi: This road has many stones, so it is difficult to walk on. Therefore, I will take another road.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative この combines with a noun and the particle は to identify the topic being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 多い changes to the て form to connect clauses and explain why the road has many stones.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is difficult to walk on,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 歩く removes ます and combines with にくい to show that the action is difficult. It goes with から to give the reason for the decision in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を follows a noun referring to a place and indicates the space or route through which movement takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is in the polite form and expresses the action of traveling through a route.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.cn: Vます形（remove ます） ＋ にくい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.why: The topic 'this road' is placed first with は. The next clause uses a chain of causes (many stones -> difficult to walk on -> から) leading to the main-clause action of choosing another road.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 歩きづらい, it focuses more on the speaker's subjective discomfort while walking, whereas にくい emphasizes the objective quality caused by the uneven road surface.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 歩きやすい is used, the sentence has the completely opposite meaning: 'easy to walk on'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the particle を with で in the phrase 道を通る, because を here indicates the space through which movement continues.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vi: This computer is easy to use, so I like it very much.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase combines with the particle は to make the computer the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is easy to use,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 使う removes ます and combines with やすい to mean easy to do. It combines with the conjunction から to state the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The i-adjective ending な serves as the main predicate to express feelings of liking toward the topic at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.cn: Vます形（remove ます） ＋ やすい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.why: The topic 'this computer' is stated first with は. The following reason clause uses the structure 〜やすいから (easy to use) to explain the conclusion 好きです at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 使いにくい, the sentence means the opposite: 'difficult to use'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern 〜がち means that something bad tends to happen or often happens. It is not used to describe an object's convenience or ease of use.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q3.kobun.tip: The verb must first be changed to the ます form, then ます must be removed before combining it with やすい. It cannot be attached directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vi: In the morning, the roads are crowded, so the bus does not come even after a long time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は emphasizes the morning as the time setting for the event in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が identifies the subject of the preceding reason clause ので.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb こむ combines with ので to connect an objective reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the main clause, which performs the action of coming or not coming.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The adverb combines with a negative form to describe an expected event that still does not happen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 来る changes to the short negative form and acts as the main predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.why: The first clause uses the conjunction ので to give an objective reason (the roads are crowded in the morning). This leads to the result in the second clause, where the adverb なかなか modifies the negative verb 来ない and emphasizes the delay after waiting for a long time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: With an affirmative sentence, なかなか instead means 'quite/relatively' and suggests praise, unlike its meaning 'even after a long time' with a negative form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ぜんぜん来ない, it has the absolute meaning 'does not come at all', losing the impatient feeling of waiting expressed by なかなか.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often forget that なかなか with a negative verb means 'does not... even after a long time/can hardly...'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.tokens.8.m: does not... even after a long time
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・Nな ＋ ので ／ なかなか ＋ Vない形
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vi: John gives good speeches, but he is not as good as Ken.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes John the topic being evaluated and compared in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object or content of the ability expressed with the adjective 上手.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 上手 combines with ですが to acknowledge the ability in the first clause before shifting to a contrast.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle ほど follows the noun Ken and makes it the standard in the unequal comparison.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite negative form of the adjective 上手 combines with ほど to form an unequal comparison sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.why: The first clause acknowledges that John has good speaking skills. The following clause uses the linking conjunction ですが to compare the level with Ken using the structure 'N ほど + negative', showing that John does not reach Ken's level.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ケンさんより is used, the sentence expresses a higher comparison ('better than Ken'), and the following clause is usually affirmative.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern くらい is also used to compare levels, but ほど emphasizes a higher standard and is more grammatically appropriate in an unequal comparison.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.tip: The unequal comparison pattern 'Aは Bほど ...ない' requires the following predicate to be in the negative form. The affirmative form cannot be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q5.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Vない形・Aくない・Aではありません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vi: These shoes are too small, so I cannot fit into them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aい（remove い） ＋ すぎて、 ＋ V辞書形 ＋ ことが できません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase with particle は identifies the shoes as the topic being commented on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The 小さい-ending adjective removes い and combines with すぎて to show that the shoes are smaller than the acceptable limit and to express the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The nominalized action structure Vこと combines with particle が as the object of the ability predicate that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite negative ability verb expresses the inability to perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.cn: Aい（remove い）・Aな（remove な）・Vます形（remove ます） ＋ すぎる ／ V辞書形 ＋ ことができる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.why: The shoe topic is placed at the beginning with は. The first clause gives the reason, using the compound adjective 〜すぎて to show that the shoes are too small. The result in the second clause is that they cannot be worn properly, expressed with the negative ability pattern 〜ことができません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 小さそうで is used, it only shows an outside impression that the shoes seem small. In contrast, すぎて shows that their size has actually gone beyond the acceptable limit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with はきにくい, it means that putting the shoes on is difficult but still possible. できません means that they cannot be put on at all.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q6.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to remove the ending い from the い-ending adjective when combining it with すぎる, and mistakenly form 小さいすぎて.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vi: For a baby's cup, choose one that is hard to break even if it is dropped.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase + の modifies the noun コップ that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は introduces the topic for discussion and gives advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the ても form expresses the hypothetical concessive condition “even if it is dropped.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Vます remove ます + にくい expresses a quality that is difficult to occur and modifies the noun もの.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The formal noun もの combines with particle が to identify the object being evaluated.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective いい acts as the predicate giving advice and ends with particle よ to make the statement sound encouraging.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.cn: Vます(remove ます) ＋ にくい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.why: The sentence makes “the baby's cup” the topic with は. It uses the concessive clause “even if it is dropped” together with the attributive phrase “hard to break” to modify the recommended item, with いいですよ as the predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using われづらい would sound unnatural because づらい is usually used for actions that are intentionally difficult psychologically or physically, while にくい is used for an objective quality of an object.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is changed to われやすい, the sentence means the complete opposite: “an item that breaks easily.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q7.kobun.tip: The pattern 〜にくい goes with the verb in the ます form with ます removed, for example 割れます → 割れにくい. Do not mistakenly keep ます or use the dictionary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vi: Kanji are so difficult that I still cannot remember them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes 漢字 the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The い-ending adjective changes to the て form to connect the clauses and give the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb なかなか combines with a negative predicate to show frustration because something still cannot be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The group 2 verb 覚える changes to the polite negative ability form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.why: The sentence introduces “Kanji” as the topic with は and uses the て form of the adjective to give the reason “difficult.” It then combines the adverb なかなか with a negative ability verb to express that the speaker has tried but still cannot remember them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 全然覚えられません is used, it means the absolute negative “cannot remember any characters at all.” なかなか means “I have tried, but I still have not achieved the result.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If あまり覚えられません is used, it means mildly “cannot remember very many.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.tip: When it means “still cannot...,” なかなか must be used with a predicate in the negative or negative ability form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q8.kobun.cn: なかなか ＋ V可能形否定 / Vない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vi: Yamada: “You have not been well lately, have you?” Tanaka: “I am so tired that I soon become unable to walk.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name comes before the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 最近 identifies the time period of the state being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.vi: you have not been well, have you? Tanaka says
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 元気 as the subject of the state ない; ね shows mild confirmation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the degree of tiredness.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Vすぎる expresses excess; て connects the reason with the situation that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: すぐ modifies the inability to walk.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: 歩けなくなってしまう describes a change into a state of being unable to walk and adds a regretful feeling; んです is used to explain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ すぎる; Vて ＋ しまう; V普通形 ＋ んです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.why: The first clause comments on the current condition. The second clause follows a cause-and-effect relationship: being too tired causes a change in the ability to walk, while てしまう shows that the result is unwanted.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 歩けません is used, the sentence only says that the person cannot walk now. It does not emphasize the process of changing into that state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 歩けなくなります is used, there is still a change of state, but the regretful nuance of てしまう is lost.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t19-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate なくなる as “not.” This pattern more precisely means “become unable to do something or no longer be able to do it.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: My mother sent me a letter.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.sk: N(giver) は ＋ 私 に ＋ N(item) を ＋ くれました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は marks the mother as the person who gives the item.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に identifies the speaker (私) as the receiver, matching the predicate くれる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the direct object being given.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb expresses another person giving an item to the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.cn: N(another person) は ＋ 私(speaker) に ＋ N(item) を ＋ くれる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The sentence describes another person, the mother, giving an item to the speaker (私). When the receiver is the speaker or someone in the speaker's family, the predicate must use くれる instead of あげる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Use it only when the speaker gives something to another person, not when another person gives something to the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If もらいました is used, the subject must change to “I” (私は母に...): I received a letter from my mother.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often mistakenly use あげる when another person gives something to them. Remember that when another person gives an item to you, always use くれる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: "Phew, this is heavy. My hand really hurts." Tanaka: "Are you okay? I will carry it for you."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: An interjection showing a sigh caused by hard work.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The い-ending adjective acts as the predicate describing the quality of being heavy.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle が identifies the body part that feels pain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: An exclamatory predicate about the feeling of pain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: A question showing concern about the other person's condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: Particle が emphasizes that the speaker will perform the helping action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: The pattern てあげる shows that the speaker voluntarily does something to help the other person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.why: Tanaka sees that carrying the heavy item has made his friend’s hand hurt, so he offers to carry it for him, using the pattern てあげる together with particle が to emphasize who performs the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this when another person does something for you, not when you do something for another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Use this when you receive help from another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.tip: Avoid using てあげる directly with someone above you because it may sound impolite, as if you are doing them a favor.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + あげる/あげます/あげた
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I ate the cake my father gave me and then went to bed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: A time adverb that sets the point when the whole event happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the source of the gift in the modifying clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb combines with the previous part to form a clause that modifies ケーキ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of eating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern てから shows that eating was completed first, followed by going to bed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate is in the polite past tense.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.why: The subordinate clause 父からもらった modifies the noun ケーキ. Then the pattern てから expresses the order: eating was completed before going to bed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means “after,” but てから emphasizes that the later action began immediately after the earlier action was fully completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It only lists actions in their usual order and does not emphasize fully finishing the first action before starting the next one.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q11.kobun.tip: Do not confuse てから, which shows time order, with から, which connects clauses to show a reason or cause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: Because Wan said he was hungry, I gave him a piece of bread.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.sk: Clause + から、 + 私 は + N (receiver) に + N (object) を + あげました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the speaking action in the subordinate clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が is used with the fixed expression おなかが空く to describe being hungry.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indirectly quotes what Wan said.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The conjunction から follows the plain form to give the cause or reason for the next clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は marks the main subject, the person giving the object in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the object.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the object being given.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: The main predicate shows that the speaker gives or hands an object to another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から; N (another person) に + N (object) を + あげる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason (Wan said he was hungry) and uses the plain form with から. In the main clause, the speaker (私は) gives something to another person (ワンさんに), so the predicate uses あげました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: The person is wrong because くれました is used only when another person gives or presents something to the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This means that I received bread from Wan, which is the complete opposite of Wan being hungry.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Pay attention to the direction of the transfer: “I give to another person” uses あげる, while “another person gives to me” uses くれる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: My younger brother received a new game from Yamamoto.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.sk: N (receiver) は + N (giver) から/に + N (object) を + もらいました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the younger brother, who belongs to the speaker’s group, as the receiver.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the source or the person giving the object.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending い directly modifies the noun ゲーム that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object received.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate shows that the subject receives an object from another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.cn: N (person) から/に + N (object) を + もらう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The subject is the receiver (弟は), and the giver is marked with から. Therefore, the predicate must use もらいました, meaning “receive.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This changes the meaning to the younger brother giving the game to Yamamoto, so 山本さんに must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれました is used, the giver must be the subject, marked with 山本さんは弟に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: When the subject is the receiver, use もらう. The giver is used with に or から, but if the source is an organization or institution, から is required.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: I cooked for my classmate Amal. Amal ate everything.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.sk: 私 は + N (receiver) に + N を + Vてあげました。 N は + 副詞 + Vました。
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the speaker as the person performing the helpful action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: It directly modifies the noun クラス that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects nouns and clearly identifies Amal as a classmate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the helpful action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object being cooked.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern Vてあげる shows that the speaker does something, such as cooking, for another person’s benefit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle は introduces the topic of the next sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: An adverb that modifies the extent of the eating action in the predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.8.n: The predicate shows that the person ate all of the food.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The first sentence shows that the speaker (私) cooked to serve or help another person (アマルさん), so it uses the structure Vてあげました. The next sentence continues by reporting that the person ate everything.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This changes the meaning to Amal cooking for me, which is opposite to the subject 私は at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This means that I asked Amal to cook for me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Avoid using 〜てあげる directly with someone of higher status or someone you have just met because it may sound as if you are showing off your favor or reminding them of what you did for them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: I did not understand the difficult words at the meeting. Later, Mr. Ota explained them to me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.sk: 私 は + N で + N が + わかりませんでした。 N (time) + N (person who acts) に + Vてもらいました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the topic and the person experiencing the event in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で shows the context or place where the situation of not understanding the words occurred.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending い modifies the noun 言葉 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が is used with the ability or knowledge verb わかる to mark what is understood.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The past negative predicate of わかる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: A noun phrase that shows the time when the next action occurred.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle に marks the person who explained something to help the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: The structure Vてもらう shows that the speaker receives help from another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence states the difficulty the speaker faced. In the second sentence, the unstated subject is still the speaker (I), and the person who helps is marked with に (大田さんに). Therefore, the benefit-receiving structure Vてもらいました must be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If てくれました is used, the person who helps must be the subject, marked with が (大田さんが説明してくれました).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This changes the meaning to me explaining something to Mr. Ota, which completely conflicts with my not understanding the difficult words.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Remember that in the structure 〜てもらう, the person performing the action is marked with に, while the person receiving the favor is the subject of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: When I forgot to bring a pen, my friend lent me one.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the object that was forgotten in the subordinate clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: A past-tense verb modifies the noun とき.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun that indicates a point in time forms a dependent conjunction linking to the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle が marks the person who performs the lending action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern てくれる expresses that another person kindly does something for the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: The first clause states when the event happens with the conjunction とき. The second clause uses the pattern てくれる to show that the lending action is help from another person to the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This expresses that the speaker does something to help another person instead of receiving help.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Change the subject to the speaker, and use particle に with the person who helps.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: Avoid using てあげる when another person kindly does something for you; when you receive help from someone, use てくれる or てもらう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる/くれます/くれました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vi: My friend corrected my Japanese mistakes for me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は states the subject and topic of the sentence, who is also the person receiving help.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に marks the person who performs the helpful action for the subject.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle の connects a noun that modifies the noun まちがい after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle を marks the object affected by the correcting action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.4.vi: asked someone to correct them for me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern てもらう shows that the subject received the correction from a friend.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: Because the subject of the sentence is 私, use the pattern てもらう to express receiving help from another person, with the helper followed by particle に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use てくれる, the subject must change to the friend and be followed by particle が or は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle for the person who performs the action in the pattern てもらう and use が instead of に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう/もらいます/もらいました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vi: Jun: "Teacher, what a beautiful shirt." Teacher: "Thank you. My daughter gave it to me."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun used to address the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The な-ending adjective modifies the noun シャツ after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: An evaluative predicate expressing praise, used with the modal particle ね to seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The opening of the teacher's reply.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: A phrase of thanks in response to the compliment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: Particle に marks the person who gives an object to the recipient.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: A predicate expressing the action of receiving an object from one's daughter.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: Because the speaker received a gift from his daughter, he uses the verb もらう with the giver followed by particle に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use くれる, the subject must be the daughter (娘がくれました).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This indicates that the speaker gives something to another person rather than receives it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: When receiving an object from someone, the giver is followed by particle に or から, not by particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.cn: N に/から + もらう/もらいます/もらいました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vi: I only bought this umbrella last week, but it has already broken.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes the noun for the object the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun phrase indicating the time when the buying action took place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.2.vi: I only just bought it, but,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The grammar pattern 〜たばかり combined with なのに expresses contrast and regret when something has just happened but the result is not as expected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb emphasizing that the umbrella broke much faster than expected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate is a past-tense intransitive verb describing the umbrella's broken state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.why: The sentence uses particle は to state the object being discussed, combines the time expression 先週 with the structure 買ったばかりなのに, and highlights the paradox and surprise that the newly bought object broke so soon.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This only indicates a point in time that happened a short while ago in objective terms, so it cannot be used for a period that ended a week ago, such as ばかり.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.tip: Remember that 〜たばかり depends on the speaker's subjective feeling, so it can still be used even if the event happened a few days or weeks ago, as long as the speaker feels that not much time has passed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q1.kobun.cn: Vた + ばかりだ・ばかりなのに
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vi: Fen: “What will An do after graduating from university?” An: “I want to work at a Japanese company.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that アンさん is the person being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 大学 as the object of graduating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 卒業したら is the form Vた + ら, expressing a time point or condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: どうしますか asks about an action or plan after the stated time point.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: の connects 日本 with 会社, showing that the company belongs to or is located in Japan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: で indicates the place where the work action takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: Vます without ます + たいです expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら/Vます without ます + たいです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.why: 卒業したら places a time condition before the question about plans. In the answer, 日本の会社で identifies the workplace, while はたらきたいです states An's wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with はたらくつもりです, the meaning changes from “want to work” to “plan to work,” which is more certain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 卒業してから, the sentence only emphasizes working after graduation and does not have the conditional nuance of たら.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q10.kobun.tip: When using たい, remove ます from the verb: はたらきます → はたらきたいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vi: Even though I have already taken the medicine, I still do not feel any better at all.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the medicine as the object of the action of drinking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.1.vi: even though I have drunk it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects the completed action of taking the medicine with the unexpected result of not feeling better.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん usually goes with a negative predicate to emphasize a complete lack.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: よくなりません is a negative predicate that describes a condition that has not improved.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.why: 飲んだのに places the completed event first, while よくなりません shows a result contrary to expectations. ぜんぜん modifies the negative predicate to emphasize that the condition has not improved at all.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 飲んでも, the sentence means that even if one takes medicine, the result will still be the same, with more emphasis on a condition or assumption.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 飲んだけれども, the sentence simply connects two contrasting ideas more mildly and shows less of the unexpected contrast expressed by のに.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that ぜんぜん in its basic use usually has to go with a negative predicate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のに
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vi: I have just seen Mr./Ms. Niwano's email. I will write a reply from now on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: たった今 indicates that the action happened immediately before the time of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: からの connects the source of the message with the noun メール that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the email as the object being viewed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたところです describes an action that has just been completed at the time of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: これから indicates the starting point of the next action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the content that will be written.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: 書きます is the predicate and describes an action that is planned to be carried out afterward.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.why: たった今 combines with Vたところです to emphasize an action that has just ended. これから opens the next action and creates a clear time sequence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたばかりです is used, it also means “have just done,” but the time that has passed may be longer and more subjective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vています is used, the action is in progress or the state is continuing, not that the viewing has just finished.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse たところです with たばかりです; たところ usually emphasizes the time immediately after the action ends.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vi: This town still has few shops even now, and it remains inconvenient without any change.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the town as the main topic being described.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb emphasizes that the condition has continued from the past until the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が goes with the subject of the adjective 少なくて.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending い changes to form て to connect a clause showing the cause of the inconvenience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending な keeps な unchanged and goes with まま to express an unchanged state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb changes to form ていません to describe a result that remains unchanged without any development.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.why: The beginning of the sentence introduces the topic このまちは、. The middle clause uses form て to state the cause, namely the lack of shops and restaurants. Finally, it combines ふべんなまま with the verb かわっていません to emphasize that the inconvenient condition has continued without change.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means keeping a state unchanged, but it is usually used for neglect or carelessness after a person's action, such as forgetting to turn off a light or leaving a door open.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.tip: Note that when the adjective ending な goes with まま, な (ふべんなまま) must be kept. Do not omit な or change it to の.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q3.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ まま
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vi: Even though I did not study, I got a good score on the test.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.0.vi: even though I did not study,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The subordinate clause uses のに to show the unexpected contrast between not studying and the result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states the topic whose result is being evaluated.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun predicate ending in でした indicates a good score in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.why: The structure のに connects two contrasting clauses and shows surprise that a good result occurred despite the earlier lack of studying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used for the assumption “even if I do not study...,” and does not express surprise at a fact that has already happened in reality, as のに does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.tip: Be careful about the form before のに: verbs and adjectives ending in い go directly in the plain form, while adjectives ending in な and nouns must go with な (for example: 暇なのに, 雨なのに).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vi: I just ate lunch, but I already want to eat something more.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb indicating a time point that has just passed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The direct object of the action of eating, accompanied by the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: even though I have just finished eating,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure 〜たばかり with なのに expresses the contrast between having just eaten and feeling like eating again.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing that the desire to eat is repeated.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: An indefinite pronoun referring generally to food that the speaker wants to eat more of.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb ending たい expresses the speaker's desire to eat.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.why: The opening states the time さっき and combines it with 食べたばかりなのに to emphasize how unusual and strange it is to want to eat again after just finishing a meal (また何か食べたい).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It only indicates the objective time when the action has just been completed and carries less of the emotional sense of unusually quick timing than ばかり.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q5.kobun.tip: When the phrase 何か is used with the desire form たい, as in 何か食べたい, Japanese speakers often omit the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vi: Do not leave things you do not understand in that state of not understanding them; ask questions.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.0.vi: as for things I do not understand,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The relative clause わからない modifies こと and goes with は to make it the topic that needs to be dealt with.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: leave something in a state of not understanding it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vない + まま goes with the particle に and modifies the state of the verb しないで.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.2.vi: do not leave it like that; do not,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative form て of する links the clause giving a prohibition before presenting the correct action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb changes to form 〜てください to give a polite request or instruction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.why: The sentence sets the topic わからないことは、、, then uses the phrase ままにする (leave the state unchanged) in the negative, followed by しないで to prevent leaving the uncertainty unchanged, and finally gives the instruction 質問してください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If one only says わからないで, it simply means “do not understand” and does not express the idea of deliberately keeping the state of not understanding for a long time, as わからないままにする does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish `〜ままにする` (intentionally leaving something in that state) from `〜ままである/だ` (simply describing a state that is being maintained).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q6.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ まま
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vi: My friend is Japanese, but cannot write kanji.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes my friend the topic; the spaces between the kana are kept as in the example sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.1.vi: even though my friend is Japanese,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: なのに connects an expected fact with the opposite result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: With the potential verb 書けません, が marks the object that can or cannot be written.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 書けません is the negative potential form and expresses the inability to write.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.why: は makes my friend the topic, while なのに creates a contrast between being Japanese and being unable to write kanji. In a potential sentence, が usually marks the object of the possible action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If けれども is used, the sentence simply connects two opposing ideas neutrally and has less of the sense of “although...but.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ても is used, the meaning is “even if..., still...,” emphasizing a concessive condition rather than an unexpected result.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 書けません, but potential verbs usually go with が to mark the object of the possible action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ のに; Aな・N ＋ なのに
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vi: When this document is finished, please send it to me immediately.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies しりょう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject as reaching a completed state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: できたら is the form た＋ら, linking a condition or an earlier time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐに modifies the action of sending in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.why: The clause できたら is placed first to give a condition or time point. Then すぐに emphasizes that the action 送ってください must be done immediately.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with できると, the sentence focuses more on a certain result or a natural event, so it is less suitable for a request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If できてから is used, it means “after completing it,” emphasizing time order more than the condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use the present form before ら in this sentence; the verb must change to the た form: できたら.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q8.kobun.cn: Vた形＋ら／Aい＋かったら／Aな＋だったら／N＋だったら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vi: Mother: The meal is ready. Let’s eat quickly. Daughter: I am doing my homework now, so I will eat when I finish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ご飯 means something that has been finished; the particle が is omitted in spoken language.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: できた is the past form of できる and describes something that has been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 早く is an adverbial form that modifies 食べよう.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べよう is the volitional form of 食べる, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: 今 indicates the time when the action is taking place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: を marks the object of している.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: している describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.9.vi: because I am in the middle of
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: ところだから links the reason to the following clause, meaning that the speaker is currently in the middle of doing that activity.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: Vたら links a condition or time point; here, it means after finishing the activity.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: よ emphasizes information that the speaker wants to tell the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.why: The clause しているところだから states what is happening and gives the reason for the promise that follows. 終わったら places the condition before たべる, so the natural order is “I will eat after I finish.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, it means “while doing it” and does not emphasize that it is happening at this exact moment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてから is used, it means “eat after finishing,” focusing on the order rather than the condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put から at the end of the sentence and forget that the reason clause must come before the result.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t20-q9.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ ところだ ＋ から; Vた ＋ ら
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vi: Since it is only 5 o’clock, the library should still be open.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: まだ modifies the time “5 o’clock” and provides a basis for the guess at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the cause to the conclusion in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that 図書館 is the topic being judged.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 開いている describes the state of being open, not only the action of opening.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: はずだ shows a reason-based guess; よ is used to confirm information to the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.why: The clause だから gives the time as a basis, and then 図書館は becomes the topic of the guess. 開いている is used because the point is the library’s state of being open.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 開いているでしょう, the sentence becomes a softer guess and does not stress a firm basis as はずだ does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 開いているにちがいない is used, the level of certainty is stronger, close to “it is certainly open.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate はずだ as the future; this pattern usually describes something believed to be true based on evidence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の＋はずだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: Have you asked where the meeting will be held? Yoshida: I heard that it will be in the meeting room on the second floor.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 会議 the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action やる takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the question どこでやる into an interrogative clause inside a larger sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きましたか is the main predicate and uses the polite past form to ask whether the action has been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 2かい with 会議室 and modifies the place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.5.vi: I heard that it is the meeting room
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: だそうです is attached after a noun to pass on information heard from someone else.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.why: どこでやるか is a question inserted as the object of 聞きました. The answer uses 2かいの to identify 会議室, and then だそうです shows that this is reported information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: と聞きましたか asks about the content heard or the exact words spoken, without focusing on an indirect question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: と思います expresses the speaker’s guess or opinion, not information reported聞.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit か in an indirect question clause; どこでやるか must have か before 聞きました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q10.kobun.cn: 疑問詞＋V普通形＋か; N・Aな＋だそうです／V普通形・Aい＋そうです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vi: Since it is food from a famous restaurant, it should certainly be delicious.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 有名な modifies レストラン, so the adjective な keeps な before the noun.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects レストラン with 料理 to show that the food belongs to the restaurant.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: だから connects the noun 料理 to the following clause to give a reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしい is the adjective い that gives the conclusion inferred from the preceding reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: はずだ expresses a conclusion based on evidence; よ emphasizes information that the speaker wants to tell the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.why: The phrase 有名なレストランの料理 successively modifies 料理 and forms the basis. だから connects the basis with the conclusion おいしいはずだ, meaning that deliciousness is a reasonable prediction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Changing it to と思います leaves only the speaker’s opinion or thought, which is weaker than the evidence-based conclusion of はずだ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: でしょう is a softer guess and does not clearly show a firm basis like はずだ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect a noun directly to から and forget だ; they must say 料理だから.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q11.kobun.cn: N・Aな＋だから／V普通形・Aい＋から; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋はずだ／Nの＋はずだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vi: I heard that Mr. Yoshida has a fever, so he will take the day off.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states 吉田さん as the topic of the reported information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks ねつ as the subject of the state ある.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: あるから gives the reason for taking the day off.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.3.vi: I heard that he will take the day off
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです follows the plain form 休む to report what the speaker has heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.why: ねつがある is the state that gives the reason, connected to 休む by から. 休むそうです places the reported-information pattern闻 at the end to cover all the information heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: ようです is a guess based on signs or circumstances and does not necessarily come from something someone said.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: つもりです expresses the intention of the person who will take the day off, not reported information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put そうです after 休みます; for reported information, the plain form must be used: 休むそうです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だそうです／N＋だそうです; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋から／N＋だから
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vi: There was a call from Mr. Yamamoto, and I heard that he will be late because of a train problem.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source of the call.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 電話 as the subject of あって; て connects this event to the following information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the reason why being late happened; の connects 電車 with じこ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 遅れる is a verb in the plain form, and it carries the information being reported.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです follows the plain form to report information heard from someone else.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.why: 山本さんから identifies the source of the information, while 電話があって connects receiving the call with the content of the call. 電車のじこで gives the reason, and then 遅れるそうです reports what was heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 遅れそうです, it means “it looks like someone will be late,” based on an observed sign rather than information heard from someone else.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 遅れるらしいです, the sentence is also a guess or indirect information, but it is less direct than そうです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish reported information with そうです from a prediction with そうです: 遅れるそうです means “I hear that someone will be late,” while 遅れそうです means “it looks like someone will be late.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋そうです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vi: There was a loud noise from the kitchen. It seems that someone dropped a plate.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates where the sound came from.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the sound that occurred.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the person who performed the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the object that was dropped.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: A verb in the past plain form usually comes before ようです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: ようです expresses a guess based on a sign heard by the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.why: から gives the source of the sound, while が marks the sound that occurred with しました. In the second clause, the past form comes before ようです to guess the cause based on the sound just heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with みたいです keeps the meaning “it seems,” but the tone is more conversational and informal.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から to show the cause here, but in this sentence から shows the source or place where the sound came from.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ ようです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vi: I can hear a voice from the next room. It looks like the child has woken up.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates where the sound comes from.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the sound that can be heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞こえます describes a sound that naturally reaches the ears, without focusing on the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject who woke up.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The past form comes before みたいです to provide the basis for the guess.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: みたいです expresses a judgment based on something observed or heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.why: The phrase から comes before 声 to give the source of the sound. Then 聞こえます describes the natural ability to hear it. The second clause uses みたいです to guess the child’s state from the sound that was heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ようです leaves the meaning almost unchanged, but the tone is more formal than みたいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate 聞こえます as “I hear,” because this verb usually describes a sound that is heard naturally, not the action of listening actively.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ みたいです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vi: My stomach hurts as if something had cut it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that feels pain.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the tool imagined to have caused the cut.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: られた is the past passive form, describing a state of being cut.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ように turns the preceding clause into a comparison for いたい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.why: The clause 切られた ように modifies いたい and describes how much it hurts through a comparison. で gives the assumed tool, while the passive form emphasizes that the stomach is the part affected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: ような must come before a noun, so using it here would require a following noun such as ような痛み.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: みたいに also means “as if,” but it is more informal than ように.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 何か, but when saying “cut with something,” they must use で to indicate the tool.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ ように
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vi: Today is Sunday, so the post office is probably closed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the reference point for the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason to the conclusion in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the post office the topic being judged.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みの modifies はず, creating the form noun ＋ の ＋ はず.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: はずです shows a well-supported conclusion with a high level of certainty.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.why: The first clause gives a fact and uses だから to create a cause-and-effect relationship. はずです comes at the end because it is a conclusion inferred from the day of the week.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: でしょう shows a softer prediction, while はずです emphasizes a well-supported conclusion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: にちがいありません expresses very strong belief and is more certain than the usual tone of はずです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.tip: With the noun 休み, Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の before はず; they need to say 休みのはずです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ はずです
