default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vi: It seems that the time when Mr. and Ms. Sato are happiest is when they are eating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は shows that Sato is the person being described.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food involved in the action of 食べる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 食べている modifies とき, while が marks the time considered the happiest.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: いちばん modifies the adjective that describes the level of happiness.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: しあわせな is an な adjective that comes before ようです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ようです shows that this is the speaker’s observation or guess.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.why: The phrase 食べているときが turns “while eating” into the subject being evaluated. いちばん comes before the adjective to create the highest degree, and then ようです comes at the end to give an uncertain observation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If you change が to は, “while eating” becomes the topic or a point of contrast, so it is no longer emphasized as the happiest time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: そうです usually relies on direct outward appearance, while ようです is suitable for an observation based on behavior or a situation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place いちばん after ようです, but the word showing degree must come before the adjective it modifies.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ ようです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vi: There are few cars in this area, and it seems quieter than the area near the station.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the area being compared and gives an observation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that has a small quantity.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the feature of having few vehicles with the observation in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: より marks the object used as the basis for comparison.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 静か is an adjective な, placed directly before みたいです to express a judgment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.why: て connects two features of the same area. より creates the comparison point, while 静かみたいです ends the sentence with an अनुमानed observation; the adjective な does not need な before みたいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: よりも emphasizes the object being compared slightly more, but the basic comparison structure stays the same.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 静かなようです also means “seems quiet,” but it is more formal than 静かみたいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な before みたいです, but with the adjective な, you must say 静かみたいです, not 静かなみたいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ みたいです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vi: Yamayu: It is very hot today, isn't it? Tanaka: Even though it is only April, it feels like summer, doesn't it?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the time topic of the statement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 暑い is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate; ですね adds a mild tone of confirmation and seeks agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.4.vi: even though it is only April
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: なのに connects a situation that goes against expectations: it is only April, but it is hot like summer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: みたいだ comes after the noun 夏 to make a comparison and express the feeling that it is like summer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.why: 今日は states the time being discussed, while とても modifies 暑い. なのに connects two contrasting ideas, while 夏みたいだ uses the noun 夏 as the standard for comparing the feeling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing みたいだ with ようだ keeps almost the same meaning, but the tone is more formal and more suitable for writing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 夏のようだ／夏みたいだ means like summer, while 夏だそうだ means that someone says it is summer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse なのに with けど; なのに emphasizes a result that is different from what should normally happen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t21-q9.kobun.cn: N＋みたいだ／V普通形・Aい・Aな＋みたいだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vi: Because the store was crowded, I was made to wait for a whole hour.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the store as the subject of the crowded state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of こんでいる connects the crowded state of the store with what happened next.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle も emphasizes a period that is longer than usual or expected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 待たされました is the causative-passive form, expressing that the speaker was forced to wait.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.why: こんでいて states the cause or background condition, and then the sentence moves to the result that the speaker had to wait. １時間も emphasizes the long duration, while 待たされました shows that the speaker did not wait willingly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 待ちました, the sentence only says that I waited; it no longer has the sense that another person or circumstance forced me to wait.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 待たせられました is used, the meaning is still that I was forced to wait, but this is the fuller form of the causative passive; 待たされました is the commonly used shortened form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 待ちました as if the action were voluntary; to say that someone was forced to wait, use the causative-passive form 待たされました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q10.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ て；V使役形＋られる → V使役受身形
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vi: My mother made me clean my room.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に identifies the person who forces or makes the subject perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks へや as the object of the cleaning action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: させられました is the polite past form of the causative passive, expressing that someone was forced to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: sound う＋あせられる; Group 2 verbs: remove る＋させられる; する→させられる; 来る→こさせられる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.why: 私 is the person who directly performs the action but does not do so willingly, so this person becomes the topic of the causative-passive sentence. 母に identifies the person causing the force, while へやを is the object of そうじする.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence can mean that I made my mother clean the room, because the subject 私 is the person causing the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence says that my mother cleaned the room herself; it does not mean that I was forced to do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake 母に for the person performing the action; in the causative passive, 母に is the person who forces, while 私 is the one who actually performs the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vi: When I was young, I did not like swimming, but my mother made me learn to swim.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N のとき ＋ N が ＋ Aな past negative ＋ が ＋ N に ＋ N を ＋ V使役受身
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed throughout the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates the time when the main event happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object of the adjective 好き.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きじゃありませんでした is the polite past negative form; が connects two contrasting ideas.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: に identifies the person who makes or forces the subject to perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks what is being learned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: 習わされました is the causative-passive form, expressing that someone was forced to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.why: The time phrase comes before the main clause. が connects the state of not liking something with the opposite event; に identifies the person causing the action, while を marks what was forced to be learned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that my mother made me learn, but it does not emphasize my feeling of being forced.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it only means that I learned to swim; it does not show that my mother forced me to learn.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に and を in the causative form; に is the person causing the action, while を is the content or action being affected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q3.kobun.cn: V使役形＋られる（五段: Vあ段＋される、上一段: Vさせられる）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.sk: 場所 に ＋ N を ＋ Vます形 remove ます ＋ なさい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination of the writing action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: なさい creates a relatively gentle request or command, often used with someone of lower status.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます ＋ なさい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the verb. に identifies where to write, を identifies the content, and なさい turns the verb into a request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence is more polite and softer, meaning please write.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence is only a statement that I will write; it is no longer a request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for a place; for the destination of the writing action, use に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vi: I cannot decide this right now. I am sorry, but please give me a little time to think.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時点 に ＋ V可能 negative ＋ 前置き が ＋ 程度 ＋ V使役てください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the matter being decided the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 今すぐに modifies the verb and indicates the time and level of urgency.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: られません expresses negative ability here: cannot decide.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects the opening apology with the following request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 少し modifies the act of thinking and makes the request softer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: 考えさせてください is a way to ask for permission to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.cn: Vない形 remove ない＋せる; V使役て形＋ください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time adverb and the negative ability form. が creates a soft transition from the apology to the request for permission; 少し reduces the directness of the request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, it means please think, without the sense of asking for permission to think.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the request for permission becomes more polite and more clearly asks for the listener's opinion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand させてください as making another person do something; in this sentence, the speaker is asking to do it personally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vi: Because it is raining today, I will not let the children play in the park.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.sk: N は + N が + Vて + いるので + N を + 場所 で + V使役 negative
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time range of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the phenomenon that causes the situation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb ふる with いる to create an ongoing state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ているので gives the reason for the action in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the person who is made or allowed to perform the action in a causative sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: で shows where the action of playing takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: あそばせません is the negative causative form, meaning not to allow someone to play.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので; Vない形 remove ない + せる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before the main clause and ends with ので. In the causative clause, を marks the children as the people who are allowed or not allowed to act, while で shows the place of play.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern says that someone is not allowed to play, focusing on the adult's permission.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means that the children do not play, without clearly saying that an adult stopped them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out ている when saying that it is raining; ふっている emphasizes that the rain is continuing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vi: At the party, I was forced by the section chief to sing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the setting where the event takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the person affected by the event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the person who makes the subject perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the song that is sung.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 歌わされました describes the speaker being forced to perform the action of singing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.why: The setting comes first, followed by the person affected and the person who causes the action. 歌を is the object of 歌う, while 歌わされました shows that the speaker did not sing willingly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the subject is the person who makes someone sing, not the person who is forced.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it only says that I sang and does not show that I was forced.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse the roles of 私は and に; in the causative passive form, は is the person who is forced, and に is the person who forces them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q7.kobun.cn: V使役形 + られる（五段: Vあ段 + される、上一段: Vさせられる）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vi: Mother: “It is already late at night, so go to bed quickly.” Child: “Oh, but the game is still not over.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is late at night
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 早く is an adverb that modifies the action of sleeping.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてなさい is used to give advice or a mild command, usually from an adult to a child.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: まだ shows that the state has not ended up to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: が marks the subject of the state おわらない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.9.n: おわらない is the present negative form, showing that the game is still unfinished.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.why: 夜遅いから gives the reason before the advice ねてなさい. The pattern Vてなさい is added after the て form to create a direct request with an adult's advising tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the speech is more polite and has less of an adult instructing a child.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vなさい is used, it is still a mild command, but it does not clearly show the ongoing-action structure of Vてなさい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake なさい for a polite expression; this pattern is mainly used when a superior makes a subordinate do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + なさい; 普通形 + から
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: “Mr. Yamanaka, you look tired. Are you all right?” Tanaka: “Yes, the company president made me work until 11 o'clock last night, so I am a little tired.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: さん marks the person being addressed directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: みたいだ comes after a clause to express appearance or a guess.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: か at the end of the sentence turns it into a question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: A time word is placed before the action to identify when it happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: に identifies the person who causes the action in the causative passive sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: まで shows the ending point of the working period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.9.vi: was forced to work and then
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: The causative passive form connects with て to lead to the result of being tired.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: ています describes the current state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.why: 社長に is the person who made Tanaka work, while はたらかされて shows that Tanaka was forced to work. て connects a cause or an earlier event with the current state つかれています.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active causative form is used, it means “let or make someone do something,” without emphasizing that the speaker was forced.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If the ordinary passive form is used, it only means “have something done to you,” without clearly showing that the person was forced to do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に in this sentence for the object of the action; here, に identifies the person who forces the subject to work.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q9.kobun.cn: V使役受身て: 五段 Vあせられる・一段 Vさせられる・する させられる・来る こさせられる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vi: Because I have just come home, I am still wearing my jacket.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 identifies the time of the state being described.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the destination of the verb 帰る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I have just come home
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたところだ describes an action that has just been completed; から connects the cause clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the clothing being worn.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: Vたままです describes a state that remains unchanged after an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ところだ; usually clause + から
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.why: 帰ったところですから gives the reason that the speaker has just arrived home. Then, まだ combines with 着たまま to say that the state of still wearing the jacket has not changed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it emphasizes an action in progress, not one that has just been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means that something has just been done, but its time range is wider and it does not emphasize the state immediately after the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use 着ているまま in this sentence; when you want to say that the state remains unchanged after putting something on, use 着たまま.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vi: Tanaka: “Did you receive any message from Ms. Sato about what time she will arrive?” Yamada: “Yes, I received a phone call. I heard that she will arrive at 3 o’clock.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the source of information or communication.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the expected arrival time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: か changes a direct question into the content being asked in a sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the content of the communication as the subject of ありました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: か comes at the end of a question asking whether the communication has arrived.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: が marks something that has appeared or arrived.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: に indicates the time Sato is expected to arrive.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.10.vi: I heard that she will arrive
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.10.n: そうです comes after the plain form to report information that was heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ; indirect question: question word + 普通形 + か
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.why: 何時に着くか is the specific content of れんらく, so か comes before the noun being reported. 着くそうです reports what Yamada heard from the phone call.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it follows the form without る, such as 着きそうです, it means “looks like someone is about to arrive,” based on signs rather than heard information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern clearly says who said it, so its tone is more direct and specific.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put か at the end of the whole sentence; in an indirect question, か comes immediately after the clause being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vi: Mori: “Huh? These sweets are delicious, so why didn’t you eat them?” Imai: “Yes, because I have gained weight recently, I have stopped eating sweets.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase is presented as the topic of the comment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: のに connects two ideas that go against the expectation: they are delicious, but the person did not eat them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: んですか both asks a question and requests an explanation for not eating them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: ので connects a reason with a result and has a softer, more objective tone than から.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: は presents sweets as the object that was given up.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.10.n: んです is used to explain the reason for not eating them.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.why: のに shows a result that goes against what the speaker would expect because the sweets are delicious. ので places the reason 太った before the result やめたんです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If けど is used instead, the contrast is lighter and more conversational, without emphasizing the opposition as much as のに.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.tip: Do not connect のに directly to a noun by removing な; use a suitable form such as Nなのに.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + のに; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vi: At last week’s drinking party, my manager made me sit next to someone I dislike, so I felt very uncomfortable.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 先週 with 飲み会 to modify the noun that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place or situation where an action occurs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the person who makes the subject perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: きらいな modifies 人, forming “a person I dislike.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 人 with となり to show the position beside that person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: に shows the position where the subject is made to sit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The causative-passive form shows that the speaker was forced by the manager to sit there; て connects this with the feeling that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.why: The phrase きらいな人のとなりに identifies the seat’s location, while ぶちょうに identifies the person who forced the speaker to sit there. すわらせられて connects the forced action with the unpleasant feeling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active causative form is used, it means “make or let someone sit,” without emphasizing that the speaker was forced.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If the ordinary て form is used, it simply means “sit,” and loses the meaning that someone else forced the speaker to do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ぶちょうに for a place; in the causative-passive pattern, に usually indicates the person who causes the force.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q4.kobun.cn: V使役受身て: 五段 Vあせられる・一段 Vさせられる・する させられる・来る こさせられる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vi: This shop is no longer as tasty as it used to be.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks this shop as the object being compared.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ほど is placed after the comparison standard to express “not as much as in the past.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: Aい changes into おいしくない and then combines with なる to express a change of state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.why: この店は is the topic, and むかしほど is the standard for comparing present quality with past quality. おいしくなくなりました expresses a change from tasty to no longer tasty.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is replaced with this one, the meaning is “like in the past,” and it does not create the negative meaning “not as good as before.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If より is used, it only states the comparison point “compared with the past.” Its meaning is less direct than ほど～ない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.tip: ほど in this pattern usually goes with a negative form; do not simply translate it as “very,” as in some other patterns.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q5.kobun.cn: Nほど ＋ Aいくない・Aなではない・Vない; Aい → Aくなる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vi: Tanaka: Oh, it is already this late. I completely forgot the time. Yamada: That is true. We were having so much fun that we talked for too long.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: もう only indicates that the state has occurred, while こんな modifies 時間 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.2.vi: it is already this late, isn't it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used to confirm and share the same feeling with the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object that was forgotten.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 忘れてしまう expresses an unintended completion or a feeling of regret.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: ので connects a reason to a result and sounds softer and more explanatory than から.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: すぎる attaches to the verb stem ます to mean doing something too much.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.cn: Vて＋しまう; Vます形の語幹・Aい（い remove）・Aな語幹＋すぎる; V普通形＋ので
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.why: Time is the object of forgetting, so it goes with を. ので is placed after the reason clause 楽しかった, while すぎる attaches to the stem 話し to say that the action of talking went beyond a suitable amount.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still expresses a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If てしまいました is omitted, the sentence only says that the person forgot; it no longer has the feeling of accidentally forgetting or regret.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that すぎる connects to the stem ます, as in 話しすぎる, rather than connecting directly to the dictionary form 話す.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vi: The weather is sunny this week, and pleasant summer-like weather continues.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the period currently being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the state 晴れて with the main clause that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: らしい modifies 天気 and describes a typical feature of summer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the continuing state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses a state that continues over time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.why: 今週は limits the topic to a time period. 晴れて connects with 夏らしい天気 to describe two features existing at the same time, while が marks 天気 as the subject of つづいています.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 夏のような天気 emphasizes being similar to summer, while 夏らしい emphasizes a true summer-like quality.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 夏そうな is unnatural in this sentence because そうだ usually expresses appearance or a direct prediction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.tip: Do not understand らしい here as a rumor; when it follows a noun such as 夏らしい, it usually means having that noun's characteristic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q7.kobun.cn: N・Aい・Aな・V普通形＋らしい; Vて＋いる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vi: When you finish reading that book, please lend it to me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the book as the object being read.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 読み終わる means to finish reading, and たら connects a condition or time with a request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.why: その本を is the object of 読む. 終わる attaches to the stem 読み to show that the reading is complete, while たら places a condition before the request 貸してください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 読んだら only means after reading; it does not clearly emphasize that the reading has been completed as 読み終わったら does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 読むと tends to express an inevitable result or something that usually happens, so it is less natural than たら in this request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.tip: With the compound verb 終わる, use the stem ます, as in 読み終わる, and do not use 読む終わる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t23-q8.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹＋終わる; Vた形＋ら; Vて＋ください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vi: Because she could not swim, my younger sister was forced by her father to practice at the swimming pool.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.sk: N は ＋ negative potential verb ＋ ので ＋ N で ＋ N に ＋ N＋させられる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person affected by the action they were forced to do.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 泳げない is the negative potential form, and ので connects the reason to the following event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates where the practice took place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the causative action in a causative-passive sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: させられる expresses being forced by another person to do something; ました makes the sentence polite and past tense.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.cn: negative potential verb＋ので; causative-passive verb: Vさせられる; N に marks the person causing the action
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.why: 妹は is the affected person, so it is made the topic. 父に indicates the person forcing the action, while プールで indicates the place; させられました combines the meaning of being forced with the action 練習する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 練習させました means that the father made someone practice, with the person causing the action as the subject; it does not emphasize the sister being forced.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 練習しました only says that the sister practiced and does not show who made her do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse に in a causative-passive sentence with を; に marks the person forcing the action, while the person being forced usually goes with は or が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vi: For shoes, it is better to choose a pair that is a little expensive but easy to walk in.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that shoes are the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies the degree of the price being high.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the state 高くても.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The form 高くても connects a concessive clause and means “even if the price is high.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 歩きやすい modifies もの and indicates a type of shoe that is easy to walk in.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the object evaluated as いい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: いい serves as the predicate and expresses a suitable choice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.why: くつは puts the topic first, then states the concessive condition 高くても. The phrase 歩きやすいものがいい means “a type that is easy to walk in is better,” with the adjective clause placed before the noun to modify it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ながら is used instead, it usually expresses two actions happening at the same time and does not emphasize “even though” as 高くても does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If やすい is replaced with にくい, the meaning changes to “difficult to walk in.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that the adjective ending in い must change to ～くても, rather than using ～いても directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q10.kobun.cn: Aいくても; Vます-stem ＋ やすい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vi: Tanaka: “I will climb Mount Fuji next week.” Yamada: “That sounds great. If you climb Mount Fuji, you should take a hat with you.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name comes before the dialogue and the opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 来週 indicates the time of the mountain-climbing action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the action のぼる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: んです is used to explain or present information; after that, the dialogue shifts to a new speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ですね is used to express an impression and seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: なら connects a condition based on the information just mentioned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks an item being carried.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: て connects 持つ with 行く, forming a sequence of actions involving taking something along.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.8.vi: it would be better to go
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.8.n: ～たほうがいい is used to give advice; よ makes the advice more informal and direct.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.why: The information “climb Mount Fuji” is used as a condition with なら. After the object ぼうしを, 持って connects with 行った to express taking a hat along, and then ～たほうがいい gives advice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～たら is used, the condition has a hypothetical meaning or happens after completion; なら is more suitable when it is based on information the listener has just mentioned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: ～べきだ is also advice, but it is stronger and more rigid than ～たほうがいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may simply translate なら as “if,” but remember that it usually depends on information or an intention mentioned earlier.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ んです; N・V普通形 ＋ なら; Vた ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vi: Recently, more people have started growing vegetables in their home gardens.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the recent period as the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the vegetable-growing activity takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the growing activity.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause そだてる modifies 人; が marks the subject that is increasing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ～てきました expresses a change that has progressed up to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.why: 最近は sets the time as the topic, followed by the place and object of the action. The phrase そだてる人 is used as the subject, while ふえてきました shows that the number has gradually increased up to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ています is used, it only describes a state that is increasing or continuing, without emphasizing a process of change toward the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: ～ようになる expresses the beginning of a new ability or habit, so it is less suitable than ～てくる for saying that a number is increasing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand てくる as “go to,” but in this sentence it only shows a gradual change toward the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vi: Ueda: “Hmm, this dish seems to be a little lacking in flavor.” Yamamoto: “How about adding a little more soy sauce?”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker’s name appears before the dialogue and the opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: う一ん expresses hesitation or that the speaker is thinking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょっと reduces the strength of the comment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject being described as insufficient.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.4.vi: it is lacking in flavor; Yamamoto says
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りない is a predicate meaning “be insufficient”; な adds a tone of speaking to oneself or making a mild comment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks soy sauce as the thing being added.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: ～たらどうですか is used to suggest or advise trying an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.why: 味が is the subject of the state 足りない. After commenting that the dish lacks flavor, the speaker suggests an action by placing the item to be added before を and using ～たらどうですか at the end.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: ～たほうがいい gives more direct advice, while ～たらどうですか is softer and closer to suggesting that someone try something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: ～ませんか usually invites someone to do something together, while ～たらどうですか advises the listener to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use どうですか as a simple question asking for an opinion, but ～たらどうですか here is a pattern for making a suggestion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vi: Eri returned to her country without saying goodbye.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Eri as the subject being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content of the action 言う.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ないまま connects to the following action and describes keeping the state in which the action has not been done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place of return.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ～てしまいました expresses that the action was completed, often with a sense of regret or something unintended.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.why: ～ないまま shows that the state of not saying goodbye remained before returning home. 帰ってしまいました appears at the end to finish the sentence and emphasize that the action was completed, with some regret.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ないで, it only describes the manner “without doing it,” and the regret expressed by ～てしまう is lost.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: ～たまま is used when keeping a completed state unchanged, while ～ないまま is used for something not done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may omit まま and connect directly with ないで, making the meaning “keep the state of not having done it” less clear.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q14.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ まま; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vi: I finished reading this book during the holiday.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the period during which the action was completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the book as the object being read.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 読みにおわる creates the meaning of finishing the reading; the past form shows that it is complete.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.why: 休みの間に places the time first, followed by the object この本を. The verb 読む combines with 終わる to emphasize that the reading was completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: ～終える also means to finish doing something, but it usually emphasizes that the subject actively completed the task.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ています is used, it only says that someone is reading or is in a state of having read, without directly emphasizing “finish reading.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may divide 読む into 読んで終わった, but the natural pattern here is the stem ます 読み ＋ 終わる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vi: No matter how sleepy I am, I review the lesson before going to bed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: どんなに modifies the degree of sleepiness in the concessive clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ねむくても uses the くても form of the い-ending adjective to connect with the meaning “even if...”.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects the noun before it with the noun ふくしゅう, creating the modifying relationship “review the lesson.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct content of the action して.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: してから uses the て form of する plus から, showing that sleeping happens after reviewing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: ねます is the main predicate, in the polite present form, and describes the action of sleeping.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.why: どんなに combines with ても to state a concessive condition, but the main action is still carried out. The phrase してから sets the time order, so reviewing happens before ねます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If してから is replaced with したあとで, the sentence still means “sleep after reviewing,” but it emphasizes more clearly the time after the action has been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If ねむいのに is used, the sentence becomes “although I am sleepy” and emphasizes contrast, rather than the general conditional meaning of ても.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse から in してから with から, which means “because,” but here から only marks the time “after.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q16.kobun.cn: Vて形・Aいくても・Aなでも・Nでも ＋ も; Vて形 ＋ から
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vi: I hear that Hayashi has watched this movie as many as five times.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Quantity も ＋ Vたそうだ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person mentioned in the reported information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the movie as the object of watching.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: も follows a quantity to emphasize that the number is higher than expected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです follows the plain form of a verb to show information heard from someone else.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.why: この映画を is the object of 見る, while 5回も adds the number of times and creates emphasis. そうです appears at the end to turn all the preceding content into reported information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: 見そうです means that someone seems about to watch it or may watch it, not that they reportedly watched it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: 5回しか見ていません means watching it only five times, emphasizing a small number rather than a large one.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.tip: も after a quantity often means “as many as...” or “even...”; it should not be mechanically translated as “also.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ＋そうだ（伝聞）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vi: Yamaguchi: Mr. Tanaka's cooking was delicious, wasn't it? Morita: Yes, I also want to be able to make dishes like that.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the speaker in the next line.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a noun 田中さん with 料理, creating the modifying phrase "Mr. Tanaka's cooking".
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 料理 is the topic being commented on; は is omitted in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしかった is the adjective い in the past tense, while ですね is used to confirm the statement and show shared feelings.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 森田 is the speaker in the second line; ええ is an agreeing reply that begins the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: も replaces は and adds the meaning "also," showing that the speaker has the same wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks 料理 as the object of the action 作れる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: 作れる is the potential form. It connects with ように to indicate a state or goal that someone wants to reach.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: なりたい expresses the wish to reach the state mentioned before ように.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.why: In the first sentence, the possessive phrase 田中さんの comes before 料理. The comment then ends with the past-tense adjective and ですね. In the next sentence, 作れるように states the desired state, while なりたい expresses the wish of 私.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 料理を作れるために were used instead, the sentence would sound unnatural; ために usually shows the purpose of an intentional action, while ように focuses on reaching a state or ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If なれるようになる were used, it would mean "become able to do," describing an actual change rather than the wish expressed by なりたい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily misunderstand ように here as "like," but it only refers to the state or ability that the speaker wants to reach.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.tokens.19.m: to become; to be able to
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.tokens.20.m: want to become; want to be
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・V可能形 ＋ ようになる; V辞書形・Vない形・V可能形 ＋ ように ＋ Vたい
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vi: About tomorrow's meeting, I will be at the company all day, so any time is fine.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N に ＋ Vいますので、＋ question word＋でも ＋ かまいません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: あしたの modifies 会議 and identifies which meeting it is.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ですが both introduces the topic and connects it to the main information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: １日中 indicates the period during which the speaker is at the company.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に indicates where the speaker is.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ので connects the reason to the result and gives a gentle explanatory tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: いつでも refers to every time when the action can be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: かまいません expresses acceptance or that something is not a problem.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.why: ですが makes tomorrow's meeting the topic, and then は introduces the speaker. The phrase 会社にいますので gives the reason, and いつでもかまいません concludes that any time is suitable.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から makes the reason more direct and informal.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: いつでもいいです also means that any time is fine, but it is simpler than かまいません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で to indicate where someone is, but with いる, they must use に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vi: Because there is a clock in the classroom, it is fine not to bring my own clock.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates where the clock exists.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますから connects the existence of the clock with the conclusion that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: の replaces a known noun, while を marks the object being brought.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.4.vi: it is fine not to bring it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 持ってくる in the negative form combines with てもいいです to say that something does not need to be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.why: 教室に時計がありますから gives the reason that there is already a clock in the classroom. Therefore, the action of bringing one's own clock is put in the negative form and connected to なくてもいい to express that it is unnecessary.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used here, the meaning would change to "must bring it."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means that it is fine not to do something, but it is slightly more formal.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use ないでもいい in every situation; with this standard pattern, it must be changed into なくてもいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q5.kobun.cn: Vない形＋なくてもいいです／Vて＋もいいです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vi: My daughter says that her leg hurts and wants to miss Saturday's match.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ Aい ＋ と言って、＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vます omit ます＋たがっています
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the daughter as the topic being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: いたい is the adjective い and serves as the predicate for the condition of the leg.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of the speech, while 言って connects the speech to the following action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 土曜日の modifies しあい and identifies the match held on Saturday.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the match as the object of missing it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: 休みたい combines with がる to form 休みたがる, expressing an observable wish in another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます＋たがる／Vます omit ます＋たがっています
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.why: 足がいたい is the content of the speech introduced by と. Then, 休みたがっています expresses the daughter's wish through outward signs, so 休みたい is not used directly as it would be when expressing one's own wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 休みたい is usually used when the speaker expresses their own wish, but here the subject is someone else.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 休みそうです only predicts that the person is likely to miss it soon; it does not confirm that the person wants to miss it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use たい for another person's wish, but they should use たがる when observing that person's wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vi: I will turn on the air conditioner in advance before my father comes home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of coming home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 帰る前に indicates the point in time when turning on the air conditioner happens before coming home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the air conditioner as the object being turned on.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ておく expresses doing something beforehand to prepare for a later purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.why: The clause 帰る前に sets the time point for the main action. つけておきます shows that turning on the air conditioner is completed beforehand as preparation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Vてあります emphasizes the resulting state of something being left ready, while ておきます emphasizes the preparatory action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてみます means to try doing something and does not have the meaning of doing it beforehand as preparation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate ておく as keep or store; in this sentence, it means to do something in advance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vi: I am very happy because I received a package from my mother.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle から shows the source of the package.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the package as the thing that arrived.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the package arriving with the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: うれしいです is the predicate showing the speaker's feeling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.why: 母から identifies the source, while にもつがとどいて states the event that gives the reason. The form て naturally connects that reason with the feeling うれしいです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause is stated more clearly as a complete reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: もらって emphasizes who the speaker received it from, while とどいて emphasizes that the package arrived.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q8.kobun.tip: The form て here not only connects two consecutive actions but can also connect a cause with a feeling.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vi: I was told by my teacher not to forget my homework.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: In a passive sentence, に shows the person who said something or requested an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the homework as the object being mentioned.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 忘れないように states the content of the reminder, intended to prevent something from happening.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 言われました is the past passive form, showing that the speaker received a reminder from the teacher.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.why: 先生に marks the person who gave the reminder in the passive sentence. 忘れないように places the thing to avoid before 言われました, creating the structure meaning that the speaker was told not to forget it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Vないでください is a direct request, while ように言われました reports a request that was made.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Vるように言われました asks someone to do something, while Vないように asks someone not to do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.tip: Do not understand に after 先生 as the object of the speech; in a passive sentence, it shows the person who performed the speaking action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t24-q9.kobun.cn: Vない形＋ように＋言う／言われる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: I have a slight headache, so I want to rest at home. May I leave early?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of small degree that modifies the adjective いたい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が shows the body part that hurts in the reason clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: Conjunction ので gives an objective and polite reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle で shows the place where the resting action takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The ending たい expresses the speaker's own desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb that modifies the manner of the verb 帰る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern てもいいですか is used to ask the other person for permission to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The speaker gives an objective reason with ので in the first sentence, then uses てもいいですか in the next sentence to ask the listener for permission to leave early.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses a prohibition: something must not be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Used to ask or request that the other person do something, not to ask permission for oneself.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: The pattern てもいいですか is used to ask permission for the speaker's own action, not to ask the other person to do something for the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もいい／もいいです／もいいですか
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: "This envelope is dirty now, so we do not need it anymore, right? May I throw it away?" - Tanaka: "Oh, we still use that, so please do not throw it away."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Give the speaker's name with an opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A demonstrative plus a noun is moved to the front as the topic of discussion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb form ている combines with から to show a cause or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.vi: we do not need it anymore, right.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: A negative verb combines with the modal particle ね to seek agreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜てもいいですか is used to ask the other person for permission to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: An indented space followed by the responding speaker's name and an opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: An interjection combines with a demonstrative pronoun and particle は to take up the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The adverb まだ goes with the verb, and から explains why it cannot be thrown away.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.8.vi: please do not throw it away."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: The pattern 〜ないでください is used to politely ask or advise the other person not to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: Yamamoto uses the permission pattern 「〜てもいいですか」 to ask the listener before throwing the item away. Tanaka gives a reason with 「〜から」 and uses the polite request pattern 「〜ないでください」 to stop him.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It has a strict prohibition from a superior, rather than a polite request for permission or help.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It becomes a request to take action (please throw it away), the complete opposite of asking someone not to throw it away.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish the pattern for asking permission for oneself 「〜てもいいですか」 (may I do...?) from the patterns for asking someone else 「〜てください / 〜ないでください」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vi: You must not look at a smartphone during the exam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase plus のときに identifies the time context in which the rule applies.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of looking at.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜てはいけない in the plain form expresses a prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.why: The phrase 「試験のときに」 sets the regulated exam-room situation. The predicate uses 「〜てはいけない」 to state the prohibition that applies to all examinees.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It becomes a sentence expressing permission (you may look at a smartphone during the exam).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It becomes a sentence expressing obligation (you must look at a smartphone during the exam).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.tip: When a noun connects with とき, it must have particle の (N のとき); the noun cannot be attached directly to とき.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ はいけない / はいけません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は identifies the subject whose ability is being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い directly modifies the noun for food that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the direct object of the eating action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The structure V辞書形 ＋ ことができますか is used to ask about the ability to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.why: This asks about the topic's 「ヤンさんは」 ability to perform an action, using the nominalized structure 「V辞書形 ＋ こと」 together with 「ができますか」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It changes from asking about ability to asking whether the person has ever eaten spicy food in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It changes from asking about ability (can the person eat it?) to asking about desire (does the person want to eat it?).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.tip: The verb before ことができる must always be in the dictionary form (辞書形); it cannot be changed to the ます or て form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる / できます
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: Because I caught a cold, I must take this medicine after meals.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: It goes with the fixed verb phrase かぜをひく to mean catching a cold.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The polite past-tense verb combines with particle から to state the reason for the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun combines with particle の to modify the noun showing the time point 後 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle に identifies the time when the medicine is taken.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun くすり that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: Particle を marks the direct object of the action 飲む.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.6.vi: if one does not take it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb takes the conditional negative form なければ to create the required-condition clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.7.vi: then it is not acceptable (one must take it)
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: The predicate combines with 〜なければ to form a pattern expressing an obligation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.cn: Vない形（remove い） ＋ ければならない／ければなりません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason for catching a cold with から. The second clause uses 〜なければなりません to show that taking medicine after a meal is a required rule or instruction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses that something does not need to be done, the complete opposite of 〜なければなりません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Expresses a prohibition against doing something, while the original sentence requires the action to be performed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often make mistakes when changing Group 1 verbs into the negative form before ければなりません (for example, incorrectly changing them to 飲み- instead of 飲ま-).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: There is an important meeting tomorrow, so you must not be late.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes a time point the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in な keeps な to modify the noun 会議 that comes immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists together with the verb あります.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb あります combines with the particle から to explain the reason for the prohibition that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the て form combines with the particle は to state the action considered in the prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate follows 〜ては to form a strong prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: The structure has two parts connected by から: the first part gives the objective situation that there is an important meeting, and the second part uses 〜てはいけません to prohibit being late.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the polite meaning “please do not be late,” which is gentler than the rule or prohibition expressed by 〜てはいけません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses permission (it is all right to be late), which is completely opposite to the prohibition in the original sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing 〜てはいけません (prohibited to do) with 〜なくてもいいです (it is all right not to do).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + はいけない/はいけません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the speaker and their ability the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative modifies the noun 問題 that comes immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the object that receives the action of answering 答える.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the dictionary form modifies the formal noun こと to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The formal noun こと combines with the particle が and serves as the subject of the ability predicate できます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate expresses the ability to perform the action and completes the sentence pattern ことができる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: To express the ability to do something, turn the verb into a noun with ことが and combine it with the ability predicate できます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Changing the verb directly into the potential form is shorter and is often used in casual daily conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses permission (being allowed to answer), not personal ability like ことができます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: The verb before ことができます must be in the dictionary form (the basic form); it cannot be changed into the ます or て form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる/ことができます
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: This store does not allow customers to enter with pets.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative modifies the noun 店 that comes immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the place the topic to which the rule applies.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と shows the companion who takes part in the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb shows an accompanying state and modifies the verb 入る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the dictionary form modifies the formal noun こと to create the phrase “the act of entering the store.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The formal noun こと combines with the particle が and serves as the object considered in terms of possibility.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The negative predicate of できる expresses a condition or rule that does not allow the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The sentence topic is この店は, and the second part uses 〜ことができません to clearly state the objective rule of the place: pets cannot be brought inside.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It is a more direct and stronger prohibition, while ことができません expresses a rule in a polite, objective way.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses that something must be done, which is opposite to the original sentence’s meaning that entering is impossible or not allowed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often forget the particle と when it is used with the phrase といっしょに, or incorrectly change the form of the verb before こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができない/ことができません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: It is dangerous, so you must not run in the hallway.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective ending in い combines with ですから to explain the reason politely for the following part.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を combines with a movement verb to show the space or path through which the movement takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 走る in the て form combines with the particle は to set the condition for the prohibited action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative predicate combines with 〜ては to form a strong prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The first part uses あぶないですから to state the reason, and the second part uses 〜てはいけません to prohibit running in the hallway.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It is the polite request “please do not run,” which is gentler than the prohibition using only 〜てはいけません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It means that one does not need to do something, which is completely opposite to the prohibition in the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: The particle を here shows the space through which movement passes, so learners can easily confuse it with the particle で.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + はいけない/はいけません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: I must return this book to the library by Friday at the latest.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle までに identifies the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination or the receiver of the returned book.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The demonstrative modifies the noun 本 that comes immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of returning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.4.vi: if one does not return it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb かえす in the ない form changes い into ければ to state a hypothetical required condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate combines with 〜なければ to complete the sentence pattern expressing an obligation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.cn: Vない形（remove い） + ければならない/ければなりません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the deadline までに, followed by the return place (図書館に) and the returned item (本を), and ends with the obligation structure 〜なければなりません to clearly state that the action must be completed before the deadline.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It only indicates an action continuing until that point, while 〜までに is the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses permission (returning it is allowed), which is opposite to the obligation expressed by 〜なければなりません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish まで (an action continuing until a certain time) from までに (the deadline by which the action must be completed).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: In Japan, people must not smoke until they are 20 years old.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle では emphasizes the country or spatial area as the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The modifying clause with まで shows the time limit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of smoking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜てはいけません is used for prohibitions and expresses something that is not allowed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The phrase 「日本では」 establishes the scope of the legal rule. Next, 「はたちになるまで」 sets the time limit, and the sentence ends with the prohibition pattern 「〜てはいけません」 to state the ban.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Change the meaning from prohibition to permission not to do something (it is all right not to smoke).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Change the meaning to an obligation to do something (one must smoke).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing the particle は in 〜てはいけません with the usual topic particle, or changing the verb incorrectly into the て form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ はいけません / はいけない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: Jun: "What kind of partner does Aya want?" - Aya: "Someone kind is enough. It is also fine if they are not rich."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name with an opening quotation mark and the particle は directed toward the person being asked.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: An interrogative word that modifies the noun for partner that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が is used with the adjective expressing desire ほしい to show the desired object.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ほしい expresses the desire to possess something. It combines with the question ending ですか and a line break.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Indentation spaces with the responding speaker's name and an opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: An adjective that modifies the noun 人 immediately after it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The noun phrase + がいい expresses the speaker's preferred choice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.7.vi: it is also fine if they are not rich."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern 〜なくてもいい expresses permission or shows that meeting this standard is not required.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The questioner uses the structure「どんな N がほしいですか」to ask about the desired model. The respondent gives the preferred criterion with「〜がいい」and states a non-required condition with the pattern「N じゃなくてもいい」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Turn it into a prohibition sentence (the person must not be rich).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Turn it into an obligation sentence (the person must be rich).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Note that when the negative form of a noun or an adjective ending in な connects to てもいい, it is「じゃなくてもいい」or「でなくてもいい」, not くなくてもいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.cn: Vなくても・Aくなくても・Na/Nじゃなくても ＋ いい（です）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: In Tokyo, it sometimes snows in winter.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the place the topic of a sentence describing a natural phenomenon.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に is used with a noun showing a time or season to identify the point in time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the natural subject used with weather phenomena.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜ことがある shows that an event or phenomenon sometimes occurs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: The topic「東京は」is given a time reference「冬に」and a phenomenon「ゆきが」, ending with the pattern「V辞書形 ＋ ことがあります」to describe something that happens only sometimes, not regularly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Change it from describing an occasional phenomenon to talking about an experience that happened in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Change it to describe snow falling now or a continuing state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: The distinction is important:「V辞書形 ＋ ことがある」(sometimes doing something or something happening) and「Vた ＋ ことがある」(having experienced doing something).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことがある / あります
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: "What did you do during the New Year holiday?" - Lee: "I went back to my country, spent time with my parents, and did things such as going out with friends."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The questioner's name at the beginning of the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.1.vi: as for the New Year holiday
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the New Year holiday the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word 何 is used with the object particle を to ask about the content of an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate verb する in the polite past combines with か to form a question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The responding speaker's name at the beginning of the answer.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle へ shows movement toward one's home country or homeland.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb is changed into form て to connect actions in time order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle と shows the person who takes part in the action together with the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb is changed into form たり to give the first representative action in a list.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: The particle と shows that friends are the people who go out together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.10.n: The verb is changed into form たり to give the second representative action, together with the auxiliary verb する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.11.n: The verb する is changed to the past form しました to complete the listing pattern 〜たり〜たりする.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.why: To answer a question about holiday activities, the speaker uses form て to connect the first action (帰って), then uses the pattern 〜たり〜たりしました to list representative activities they did.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It only lists two actions in time order. It does not have the meaning of giving representative examples like たり〜たり.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes a repeated habit in the present or future, so it is not suitable because the sentence answers a question about something done in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the final verb to the past form しました and leave only あそんだり at the end of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.tokens.13.m: spend time, celebrate the New Year
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q10.kobun.cn: V1たり ＋ V2たり ＋ する
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vi: Sometimes, before eating near home, I have to wash my hands.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing how often an event occurs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun 家, which modifies the location 近く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase + の modifies the phrase that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before 前に to create a phrase meaning 'before eating'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern V辞書形 ＋ 前に shows the point in time before an action is performed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of washing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: The shortened conversational form of 〜なくてはいけない expresses an obligation to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ 前に ／ Vない (omit い) ＋ なくては（いけない）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.why: The sentence combines the time-point structure V辞書形＋前に (before doing something) with the obligation pattern 〜なくては (must do something) in a shortened casual form at the end.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses permission not to do something: 'it is fine not to wash one's hands.' This is the complete opposite of obligation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It is more formal and more common in writing, while なくては has a casual, everyday conversational tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q11.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the past form before 前に (changing it to 食べた前に). The correct rule is always the dictionary-form verb (V辞書形 ＋ 前に).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to a ramen shop with a friend.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: A time adverb that identifies a past point when an event occurred.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と shows the person who accompanies the speaker in the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に follows a place noun and shows the destination of movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が follows the nominalizer こと and makes it the subject of the predicate that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern Vる＋ことがある describes sometimes performing an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb なる is in the polite past and ends the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.why: The sentence sets up the time adverbial (きのう), the person acting together (ともだちと), the destination (ラーメン屋に), and the predicate phrase 行くことがありますなりました.
