default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: To describe the experience of 'having gone,' use the past-form verb た instead of the dictionary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes an event or plan that has been decided or arranged to happen.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse Vる＋ことがある (sometimes doing something) with Vた＋ことがある (having experienced doing something).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形 / Vない ＋ ことがある
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: When I am busy, I sometimes do not eat breakfast.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: It serves as the topic of the whole sentence and is used with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A subordinate phrase showing the time that provides the context for the action in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The direct object of the action of eating, used with the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the short negative form ない to modify the noun こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: A sentence pattern that describes something that happens sometimes or occasionally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: This sentence makes the speaker the topic with は, clarifies the time setting with the clause 'いそがしいとき', and combines the ending 'Vないことがある' to show something that only happens sometimes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes an experience that happened in the past. It is different from a habit of sometimes doing or not doing something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes a habit that the speaker consciously decides to maintain regularly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 'Vる/Vない ＋ ことがある' (sometimes...) with 'Vた ＋ ことがある' (having done something in the past).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことがある
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vi: Yesterday was my birthday. I turned 19.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.sk: N(time) は ＋ N の ＋ N でした。N に ＋ なりました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: Presents a time reference as the topic of the sentence, together with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の shows possession and modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun predicate in the polite past tense, describing a completed event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Used with the particle に to show the result reached in an age change.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb なる in the polite past form expresses a natural change of state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: The first sentence confirms the past birthday event. The second uses the change pattern 'Nになる' with the particle に to describe turning a new age.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes a person's subjective decision or choice, such as ordering food or choosing an option. It is not used for a natural increase in age.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes a state or age that changes naturally according to objective rules.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particles を or で instead of the particle に before the verb なる when talking about changing to a new age.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.cn: N に・Aな に・Aい(く) ＋ なる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: Today, it has been raining and stopping repeatedly since morning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: Presents a time reference as the topic of the sentence, together with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point of a period of time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing a state that continues without interruption.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The natural subject of a weather event, used with the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb ふる is changed to form たり to list the first action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb やむ is changed to form たり to list the second contrasting action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb する is changed to form しています as the required ending of the pattern たり...たり.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The two contrasting verbs 'ふったり' and 'やんだり' are connected with 'しています' to describe the weather repeatedly changing between rain and no rain throughout the period since morning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes two actions that happen one after another in time. It does not express repeated alternation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes two actions happening at the same time by one subject.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Remember that the pattern for listing alternating actions must always have the verb する at the end of the sentence in the suitable form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい(かった)・Aな/N(だった) ＋ り ＋ Vた/… ＋ りする
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: I have eaten sushi only once.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A counter word combined with the particle だけ to show that the number of times is limited to one.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The direct object of the action of eating, used with the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is changed to the short past form た to modify the noun こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: A sentence pattern describing an experience of having done something in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The pattern 'Vたことがある' combines with a verb in the short past form to talk about a life experience. The counter word '１かいだけ' emphasizes that it happened rarely.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes sometimes doing or not doing something, rather than a past experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes an action that has just been completed shortly before the time of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: When talking about having done something before, the verb before ことがある must be changed to the short past form (Vた), not the dictionary form (Vる).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: The sun rose, and the outside of the window became bright.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The subject of the first clause performs the action of rising.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb is changed to form て to connect events in time order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の modifies the spatial range of the noun 外.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The subject of the second clause undergoes a change of state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending い changes to the ending く to modify the verb なる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: A predicate describing a natural change of state in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.cn: Aい( remove い + く)・Aな( + に)・N( + に) ＋ なる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses て to connect actions in time. The second clause uses the adjective ending い, changed to “明るく,” together with “なりました” to show a natural change in the environment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes a person's intentional action that makes something bright, such as turning on a light, not a natural event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This is grammatically incorrect because the adjective ending い must change to 明るかったです in the past tense.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: When combining the adjective ending い with the verb なる, you must remove the ending い and add く (明るい -> 明るく).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: I have never been to Japan, so I really want to go there at least once.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb used with a negative form to describe something that has not happened up to now.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination of an action of movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is changed to the short past form た to modify the noun こと.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The formal noun こと, together with the particle が, serves as the subject of the negative predicate ない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The negative adjective ない combines with the conjunction から to give the reason for the wish in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: A counter word functioning as an adverb showing the number of times the speaker wants to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb ending たいです expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: The first clause combines the adverb 'まだ' with the negative experience pattern 'Vたことがない' and the conjunction 'から' to give a reason for the wish in the second clause, 'Vたいです'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes an intention not to go in the future, not a lack of past experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Simply describes something that has not been completed at the present time, without expressing accumulated experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: Do not change it incorrectly to 'まだ日本に行かないから' because the negative experience pattern must keep the verb in the Vた form combined with ことがない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vi: Because the room has become clean, I feel very comfortable.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the first clause that undergoes a change of state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な changes to に to modify the verb なる, which shows the result of the change.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb なる in the past form combines with the particle から to give the reason for the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the feeling in the result clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が combines with the noun 気持ち to make the subject of the adjective いい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending い acts as the main predicate and ends the sentence in the polite form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ になる / N ＋ になる / Aい (remove い) ＋ くなる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: The sentence describes a change in the room's state (きれいに＋なった) as the cause (connected with から) that leads to a pleasant feeling in the second clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Gives an objective reason and sounds more formal and gentler than から.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Shows the intentional action of cleaning the room, rather than a natural change of state such as になる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to add the particle に when connecting the adjective ending な with the verb なる (it is easily mistakenly written as きれいなった).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vi: Yamada: "Do you like studying Japanese?" - Park: "Yes, I like it very much. I have never been late for class, not even once."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name at the beginning of the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun 日本語 to modify the noun 勉強.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes studying Japanese the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective predicate ending in な combines with the question particle か to ask about preferences.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The respondent's name together with the affirmative word はい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective predicate ending in な shows a high level of liking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle に marks the object of the action of being late, together with も for emphasis.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The number word 一度 combines with the particle も and a negative ending to mean 'never, not even once.'
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb in form た combines with ことが to serve as the subject of the negative experience predicate ありません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: The negative form of あります, forming the pattern Vたことがない to show that the speaker has never had that experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: To describe an experience that has never happened up to now, the speaker uses the negative experience structure Vたことがありません together with the emphatic adverb 一度も.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It only expresses a promise or habit of not being late and does not highlight experience up to now like 遅れたことがありません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Use the dictionary form V to express that sometimes someone is late, showing frequency, which contrasts with the negative experience form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly change the verb to the dictionary form (Vる＋ことがある means sometimes doing something) instead of the past form (Vた＋ことがある means having done something before).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ことがある / ことがない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vi: I think the sea in Okinawa is very beautiful.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the place name noun to the noun 海.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the sea of Okinawa the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the adjective きれい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in な in the plain form is followed by だ before the quotation particle と.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate expresses the speaker's personal thought or opinion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: The topic is placed at the beginning with は (沖縄の海は). The speaker's judgment in the plain form (きれいだ) is quoted with the particle と and followed by the verb expressing an opinion 思います.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It only makes a judgment based on appearance, 'looks beautiful,' rather than expressing a personal opinion or thought like だと思う.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It reports another person's words, 'said that it was beautiful,' instead of expressing the speaker's own thought.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to add だ when combining an adjective ending in な or a noun before と思います (often incorrectly written as きれいと思います).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.cn: 普通形 (V / Aい / Aなだ / Nだ) ＋ と思う
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vi:
Tanaka: "Would you like to have lunch with me? What would you like to eat?"
　Yoshida: "Anything is fine. Tanaka, please decide."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The name of the person making the invitation and asking the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the purpose of the movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The ending 〜ませんか is used to make a polite invitation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The question word combines with the particle が to mark the thing the person wants to eat.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate asks about the other person's wish and ends the first line of dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The respondent's name with a space at the beginning of the line.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The question word combines with でも to express an unrestricted affirmative meaning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The predicate shows acceptance and comfort with any option.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: The particle が marks the person who will perform the action of deciding.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: The pattern 〜てください is used to make a request and let the other person choose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.why: Tanaka makes an invitation with 「〜行きませんか」 and asks about the other's wish with 「何が〜たいですか」. Yoshida then uses 「何でも」 with an affirmative sentence to say that any food is fine and gives the choice to the other person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「何も」 is used, the following part must be negative 「何も食べたくない」, meaning 'do not want to eat anything at all.' This is the complete opposite of 「何でもいい」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「どれでもいい」 is used, the meaning is limited to specific choices available in front of the speaker, while 「何でもいい」 has a broader meaning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q10.kobun.tip: Remember the rule clearly: a question word + でも is used with the affirmative form, meaning 'anything is fine,' while a question word + も must be used with the negative form, meaning 'nothing at all.'
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vi: As for tomorrow's party, I think the teacher will come too.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: A time noun combines with the particle の to modify the event noun that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は identifies the main topic of the whole statement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle も shows addition, meaning that even the teacher will take part.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the dictionary form is followed by the particle と to introduce the content of the prediction.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate ends the sentence and expresses the speaker's subjective opinion or thought.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.why: The sentence topic is placed at the beginning with 「〜は」. The speaker then uses a subordinate clause with the particle 「も」 to emphasize the next participant, and ends with the pattern for a personal opinion or prediction 「〜と思います」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「来るつもりです」 is used, it expresses the speaker's own intention, so it is not used to predict another person's action, such as the teacher's.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「来るかもしれません」 is used, the certainty is much lower, meaning 'may come' or 'might come.'
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.tip: The clause before the quotation particle 「と」 in the pattern 「〜と思う」 must be changed to the plain form (普通形).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q11.kobun.cn: 普通形（V・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ） ＋ と思う
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vi: I have to finish cleaning the room before my friend comes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject inside the subordinate clause showing the time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern 〜までに sets the deadline by which the action in the following clause must be completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the cleaning action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜なければいけません expresses a duty or something that must be done.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「〜までに」 to set a deadline, before the friend arrives. The second clause describes a one-time completed action, cleaning the room, with the obligatory structure 「〜なければいけません」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「来るまで」 is used, the following clause must be an action that continues until the friend arrives, such as 'wait until the friend arrives.'
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「来るまえに」 is used, it only shows the order of the actions and does not emphasize a deadline like 「までに」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q12.kobun.tip: Carefully distinguish between 「まで」, an action that continues until a point in time, and 「までに」, an action that must be completed once before that point.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vi: Because there is a test tomorrow, I will still go to school even if I have a fever.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The time 'tomorrow' is made the topic of the sentence with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The reason is stated with the structure Noun + だから.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: even if I have a fever,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: A concessive condition, meaning 'even if...,' is expressed with form 〜ても.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The destination of the movement is marked with the particle に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate uses the polite future form ます to express intention.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses だから to give an objective reason as the premise. The second clause uses 〜ても to express determination to perform the action (go to school) despite an obstacle (having a fever).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 'ねつがあったら', the sentence means a favorable condition (if I have a fever...), so the second clause would usually be resting, not going to school.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Use it only when an unexpected event has already happened and carries a feeling of regret or reproach. Do not use it for a future action that expresses intention.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often forget the change required for nouns and な-ending adjectives before も (it must be で＋も, for example: びょうきでも).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aな/Nで ＋ も
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vi: While I was at my friend’s house, I had a stomachache continuously.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: It shows possession for the noun 家 that follows, using the particle の.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: It marks a place of existence with the particle に, used with the verb いる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.vi: during the whole time I was there,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜間 expresses a continuous period from beginning to end.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb emphasizes that the stomachache continued without stopping.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The subject of the painful condition, marked by the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate is an い-ending adjective changed to the polite past tense (〜かったです).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: Because the condition in the second clause (a continuous stomachache - ずっといたかった) continued throughout the entire time at my friend’s house, the sentence must use 間, not the particle に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 'いる間に', the second clause must be a brief, momentary action (such as 'take medicine' or 'go to the toilet'). It cannot be used with the lasting condition 'ずっと'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Use it only when the same subject performs two intentional actions at the same time. Do not use it for a period containing a medical condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: Remember: '間' goes with an action or condition that continues throughout the period, while '間に' goes with a short action that happens at one point during that period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vている・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ 間
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: Please do not talk until the exam ends.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The subject in the subordinate clause, marked by the particle が.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern V辞書形 ＋ まで expresses a limit that an action or condition continues up to.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate is a request telling the listener not to perform an action, using the pattern Vないでください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: The action of 'not talking' is maintained continuously until the exam ends. Therefore, the sentence uses まで to mark the ending point of that continued condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use '終わるまでに', the second clause must be an action completed before the time limit (for example: 'submit the paper before time runs out').
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It has the sense of taking the chance to do something before a condition ends. It does not express maintaining a limit like まで.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: The key rule is: 'まで' goes with an action that continues (such as waiting, staying silent, or keeping a door open), while 'までに' goes with a one-time action that is completed (such as submitting a paper, arriving, or sending money).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This demonstrative comes before and directly modifies the noun 図書館.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: It makes the noun phrase 'this library' the main topic of the sentence with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word だれ combines with でも to affirm the entire group of people (anyone is allowed).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: It turns the verb 使う into a noun with こと and uses the particle が to mark it as the object of ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: This verb expresses ability and completes the ability structure 〜ことができる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: The sentence makes 'this library' the topic, then uses 'だれでも' to affirm that there is no limit on the people allowed, together with the ability pattern 'Vことができる' to state the permission or rule for using it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 'だれも', the sentence must use the negative ending (だれも使うことができません), meaning completely negative: 'no one can use it'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It refers to one unspecified person and cannot express the universal meaning 'anyone' like だれでも.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: The distinction is clear: 'question word + でも' always goes with an affirmative sentence (everyone, everything), while 'question word + も' goes with a negative sentence (no one, nothing).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: No matter how busy I am, I still study Japanese every day.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This adverb expresses a high degree and pairs with 〜ても to emphasize a concessive condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: no matter how busy I am,
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes its ending to 〜くても to connect the sentence and express a concessive condition (no matter how...).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: This time noun or frequency adverb modifies the action of studying.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The direct object of studying, marked by the particle を.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate expresses a habit or determination to perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: The adverb どんなに works naturally with the 〜ても form to create a structure that emphasizes the greatest difficulty (no matter how busy I am), highlighting the speaker’s unchanged determination to study in the main clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the same meaning and can completely replace 'どんなに〜ても' with the same exaggerated concessive nuance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses strong determination, 'I will do it no matter what...', but it does not go with the concessive condition 〜ても in the middle.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: When changing an い-ending adjective to the 〜ても form, change い to くて (いそがしい → いそがしくて ＋ も). Never keep い and simply add ても.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.cn: どんなに ＋ Vて・Aくて・Aな/Nで ＋ も
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vi: I have to go to the company before 10 o’clock.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The pattern N ＋ までに indicates the deadline by which an action must be completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: It marks the destination of a movement verb with the particle に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate expresses an obligation with the grammar pattern Vなければならない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: The verb 'go to the company' (会社に行く) is a completed action that happens at one point, and it must be completed before the 10 o’clock deadline. Therefore, the sentence uses the structure '〜までに'.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use '10時まで', the second clause must be an action that continues from the beginning until 10 o’clock (for example: '10時まで働きます' - work until 10 o’clock).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This prohibition structure means 'must not do' and is the complete opposite of the obligation structure 'must do' (なければなりません).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: Never confuse 'まで' (maintaining a condition until a point) with 'までに' (completing an action before the specified time).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vi: While I am in Japan, I want to climb Mount Fuji at least once.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に goes with the verb いる to identify a place of existence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun 間に that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜間に indicates an action that occurs during a specified period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.vi: even just once is enough, so
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: This phrase expresses a minimum condition or concession to show a wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に marks the destination or target of the verb のぼる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The ending 〜たいです ends the sentence and expresses the speaker’s wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「〜間に」 to set a period of time, while the second clause uses 「〜たいです」 to express a momentary action that the speaker wants to perform during that period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 「〜間」 without 「に」, the second clause must be an action or condition that continues throughout the entire time in Japan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 「〜うちに」, the sentence also suggests urgency: you should climb before the conditions change or before you return home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 「間」 (an action that continues throughout the period) with 「間に」 (an action that happens at one point within the period).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vている・Vない・Nの ＋ 間に
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vi:
Yamada: "When will Yamamoto come?"
　Park: "I heard that he will come in about 30 minutes."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: It appears at the beginning of a dialogue to introduce the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes Yamamoto the topic of discussion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The question adverb used to ask about a time point.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate uses the dictionary form combined with the ending の？ to ask a question in informal speech.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The responding person's name with a leading space and an opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb showing the amount of time left before something happens.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle で shows the time limit within which the action will take place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle って is used in speech to quote something someone said or information one heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The main predicate is in the past tense, with the modal particle よ added to inform the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: Yamada asks a casual question with the ending 「〜の？」, while Park repeats information heard from someone else using the colloquial quotation particle 「〜って」 combined with the predicate 「聞いた」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「〜と聞いた」 makes the sentence more polite and formal than the shorter expression 「〜って聞いた」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 「来るそうだ」 simply passes on information that was heard, without emphasizing that the speaker has just asked about it or heard it directly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: The particle 「って」 is used only in casual conversation between friends or with someone of lower status. It is not used in formal situations.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.cn: 普通形（V・Aい・Aな・N） + って
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: Houses in Tokyo are expensive and cramped, so I do not want to live there.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: It modifies a geographical location for the noun 家 that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the thing being evaluated the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle も adds another factor with the same negative tendency.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜し states the first reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜し adds a second reason that leads to the same conclusion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.5.vi: do not want to live there.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The ending 〜たくないです shows that the speaker does not want to perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The speaker uses the reason-listing structure 「〜し、〜し」 to link two negative points—the rent is expensive and the space is cramped—and naturally leads to the conclusion in the following part: they do not want to move there.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「高くて、せまくて」 simply describes parallel characteristics. It does not highlight their role as reasons as 「〜し」 does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 「高いから、せまいから」 makes the sentence more repetitive and disconnected than using 「〜し」 to link several reasons.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: When connecting an adjective ending in な or a noun with 「し」, you must keep 「だ」, such as 暇だし and 雨だし. Do not omit 「だ」.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: 普通形（V・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ） + し
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: “How was the party yesterday?” Tanaka: “I could not go. The place was far, and I was busy too…”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.sk: N の + N は + どうでしたか。N には + past negative potential V。N も + Aかったし、Aかったし
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the time きのう with the noun パーティー.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes yesterday's party the topic being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: どう asks about an impression or state; でしたか is the polite past form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the destination, while は adds contrast or emphasis.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: 行ける is the potential form of 行く; the past negative form means that the speaker could not go.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: も replaces が and adds another reason why the speaker could not go.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: し connects one reason in a series of reasons.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: し at the end shows that other reasons have been left unstated.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: The answer first states the result—that the speaker could not go—and then gives the reasons using し. Repeating し shows that several reasons are being listed, and the final part may continue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Using から expresses a more direct cause-and-effect relationship and usually ends clearly with a conclusion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ので gives a softer and more objective tone when explaining a reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: し does not only mean “and”; in this sentence, it lists the reasons one by one that led to the result that the speaker could not go.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + し
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamashita speaks very quickly. I want him to speak a little more slowly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose way of speaking is being described.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies はやく to increase the degree.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective はやい changes to はやく to modify the verb 話します.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: もう少し modifies ゆっくり and indicates a slightly slower degree.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: ゆっくり modifies 話して and shows the manner of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: Vてほしい expresses the speaker's wish for another person to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The first sentence describes the current way of speaking with the adverb はやく. The second uses ゆっくり + 話してほしい to express a wish for the other person to change how they perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes the wish to receive help or an action from the other person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a direct request. It does not emphasize the feeling of wanting something as ほしい does.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: After ほしい, when you want someone else to do something, you must use the て verb form, not the dictionary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: My mother, who lives far away, always wants to meet me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the place where the mother lives.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ～ている describes the state of living somewhere; the character in the sentence is kept as given in the exercise.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the mother the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: いつも modifies the wish to meet and shows frequency.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the person whom the mother wants to meet.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてほしい expresses the wish for another person to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The clause 遠くに住んでいる comes before 母 and modifies “mother,” identifying which mother it is. In 会ってほしい, に marks the person whom someone wants to meet, while the person who has the wish is 母.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: With 会いたい, the person who wants to meet is the subject of the sentence; the current pattern emphasizes the mother's wish for me to meet her.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: With 会ってください, the sentence becomes a direct request rather than an indirect wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in Vてほしい with a place marker. Here, に marks the person who is expected to perform or receive the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: Yesterday I wrote the report, but I accidentally left it at home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing the time point when the action of writing the report took place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of writing.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure 〜んですが is used to explain the situation and give background before presenting an undesired result in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the place where the forgotten item remains.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate uses the polite past tense to describe having forgotten something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: The first clause uses a past-tense verb with the ending んですが to give the listener the background and naturally lead to the unfortunate event in the following clause: leaving it at home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書いたけれど is used, the sentence only expresses an ordinary contrast and lacks the explanatory, apologetic tone of んですが.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書いたのに is used, the sentence expresses stronger annoyance or regret, with a blaming tone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: When saying that an object was forgotten somewhere, Vietnamese learners often mistakenly use the particle で instead of に, which indicates where the object remains.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・N（な） + んですが
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: I want my child not to play games for a long time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle には identifies and emphasizes the person toward whom the speaker directs the wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い directly modifies the noun 時間.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase showing an amount of time works as an adverb and modifies the degree of the action of playing games.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of playing games.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜ないでほしい expresses a wish for another person not to do an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The pattern 〜ないでほしい goes with the person who receives the wish, 子ども, marked by に/には. It expresses the speaker's wish that the child control themselves and not play games for too long.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ゲームをしてほしくない is used, the sentence emphasizes not wanting something, while しないでほしい emphasizes the expectation that the other person will carry out the action of “not playing.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If しないでください is used, the sentence becomes a direct request to the listener, while しないでほしい expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle marking the person concerned before 〜てほしい / 〜ないでほしい with を or が, instead of using に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でほしい / でほしいです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: In Japan, I want to bathe in a hot spring, and I also want to go to Mount Fuji.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle では identifies the location where the activities mentioned take place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of entering a hot spring.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The connecting particle し lists the first wish in a series of wishes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the destination of going. Together with も, it expresses “also” or “as well.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate uses the ending 〜たい to express the speaker's own wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The particle し lists wishes of the same type in parallel when traveling in Japan. Adding も in the later clause emphasizes the accumulation of these wishes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入って、行きたい or 入ったり行ったりしたい is used, the sentence simply tells the order of actions or lists typical actions. It does not emphasize parallel wishes like し.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入り合いたいから is used, the first clause becomes the reason for the second clause, which changes the intended meaning of listing desired destinations.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: When 〜し is used to list equivalent wishes or reasons, learners often forget to use も in the later clause to make the sentence more natural.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（だ）・N（だ） + し
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: My son hates school, so he does not want to go. He often skips school.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence, which is a third-person subject.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that receives the feeling of liking or disliking expressed by the adjective きらい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The ending だから connects the sentence to a direct cause of the action in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜たがる in polite negative form expresses that a third person does not want to perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The frequency adverb modifies the verb 休みます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate describes an action that happens regularly in the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Vます（remove ます） + たがらない / たがりません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: Because the person who does not want to go to school is むすこ, a third person, the sentence must use the negative form 行きたがりません of 〜たがる instead of 行きたくありません, to match the grammar for describing another person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行きたくありません is used, the sentence is grammatically incorrect because the ending 〜たくない is used only to express the speaker's own feelings.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行かないつもりです is used, it only expresses an intention not to go and does not highlight the son's outwardly expressed dislike.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Many learners mistakenly use the ending 〜たくありません for a third person instead of using the form 〜たがりません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: Tappu does not eat vegetables. Therefore, he only eats meat.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being talked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food affected by 食べる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べない is the negative form; んです is used to explain a situation or reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: それで connects the preceding cause or situation with the result that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: だけ limits the food being eaten to meat.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな+なんです／Nな+なんです; それで、 + result
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: The first sentence states that he does not eat vegetables and uses んです to explain this. それで connects that situation to the result, which is eating only meat, while だけ emphasizes the limit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing それで with だから makes the conclusion more direct and conversational.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use を after だけ in the pattern 肉だけ食べます; だけ already follows a noun to limit its range.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q8.tokens.5.m: emphasis on a reason or explanation
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: Jun: “Excuse me, teacher. My stomach hurts. May I go home?” Teacher: “Are you all right? Go home and get plenty of rest.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 先生 is the person being directly addressed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: いたい is an adjective ending in い; んですが states the condition that serves as the background for the request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: 帰っても is the て form + も, creating the condition in a permission-request pattern.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: てもいいですか asks whether the listener permits the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The mark 「 opens the teacher's dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: ですか creates a polite question to confirm the person's condition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: The て form connects going home with the following action of resting.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: よく modifies 休んで and shows the degree of rest.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: Jun first states the symptom with んですが and then asks for permission with てもいいですか. The reply uses two verbs in the て form to connect going home with the request to rest.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the question, the meaning changes to “you must not go home,” expressing prohibition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only expresses the speaker's wish; it does not directly ask for permission.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use the dictionary form before ください. They need to use the て form, such as 帰ってください and 休んでください.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい＋んですが／Aな・N＋なんですが；Vて＋もいいですか；Vて＋ください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: I dropped the glass, so I accidentally broke it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a material ガラス with a noun コッフ.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the cup as the object affected by the action of dropping.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of dropping with the action of breaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてしまいました describes a completed action with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The two consecutive actions are connected with the て form: dropping the cup and then breaking it. しまいました comes at the end to show that the result happened and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If しまう is omitted, the sentence only reports that the cup broke, without stressing regret.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: おく expresses doing something in advance or preparing it, so it does not fit an accidental breakage.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: しまう after the て form does not only mean “put away”; with an accident, it often expresses accidentally doing something or regret.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: Vて＋しまう／しまいました
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: What should I do with this book? Tanaka: Please just leave it there.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: この本 is the topic placed before the comma to ask how it should be handled.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: どう asks how to handle or decide what to do with the topic この本.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates where to put the book.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: そのまま modifies the action of putting the book down and shows that its position or state is not changed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: Vておく in the 置いておいてください form describes keeping something in that state as requested.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.why: この本 is presented as the topic, and then どうしますか asks how to handle it. In the answer, そこに shows the place to put it, そのまま shows that it should remain as it is, and Vておく shows that the state is maintained intentionally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいて is omitted, the sentence only asks someone to put the book there, without stressing that it should remain there.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 置いてあります only describes a book that has already been placed; it is not a request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate おく as “put,” but in the pattern Vておく it often means doing something in advance or keeping something in the same state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q10.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ おく ／ Vて ＋ おいてください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vi: It is already time to go out, so please quickly finish eating.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: もう shows that the time has almost arrived or has already arrived.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is time to go out
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 出かける modifies 時間, while だから connects the reason to the request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 早く is the adverbial form of the adjective い and modifies 食べる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べてしまう expresses completion of an action and combines with ください to make a request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.why: 出かける comes before 時間 to form the phrase “time to go out.” だから gives the reason for doing it quickly. 食べてしまってください combines the て form with しまう to stress finishing the meal before leaving.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 食べてください, it only means “please eat,” without stressing that the eating should be finished.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 食べなければなりません, the meaning is that eating is required, rather than a gentle reminder to hurry.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.tip: Do not understand しまう here as “put away”; after the て form, it usually stresses completion of the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう ／ Vて ＋ しまってください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vi: There is an exam next week, so please study properly in advance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 来週 indicates when the exam will take place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks an existing event, while から connects the reason to the request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ちゃんと modifies 勉強する and asks the listener to study seriously.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: Vておく describes preparing in advance for something that will happen soon.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.why: 来週 is placed at the beginning to set the time of 試験. から gives the reason, and then 勉強しておいてください asks the listener to prepare in advance for the upcoming exam.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 勉強してください, it only asks someone to study and does not express preparation in advance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 勉強しなければなりません, it stresses obligation more strongly.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.tip: Learners may forget おく, which removes the meaning of “doing something in advance to prepare for what is coming.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q12.kobun.cn: N ＋ があるから; Vて ＋ おく ／ Vて ＋ おいてください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: We will ride a bus for about three hours from now, so please use the toilet first.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.sk: これから ＋ Duration ＋ N に ＋ V辞書形＋から、N に ＋ Vて＋おいてください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates when the upcoming action begins.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: くらい indicates the approximate duration of the bus ride.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the means of transport used with the verb 乗る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the destination of the action 行く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects going to the toilet with おく and shows that it is done in advance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: Vておく expresses preparation in advance; ください turns it into a polite request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The first clause gives the situation and reason with から. Going to the toilet is placed before the trip and combined with おく to express preparation for a long journey.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It only means “please go” and does not clearly express going in advance to prepare.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It means “you must go,” stressing obligation instead of a reminder to prepare.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Vておく must keep the auxiliary verb おく after the て form; it should not be translated and used as an independent verb meaning “put.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形＋から；Vて＋おく；Vて＋ください
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: My younger brother has been studying in his room since a little while ago.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から indicates when the action began.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where studying takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the Vています form describes an action that has continued from the recent past up to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The topic 弟は is placed at the beginning, followed by the starting time さっきから and the place 自分のへやで, which modify the continuously ongoing action 勉強しています.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If the simple past is used, the sentence only reports that studying ended and does not show that he is still studying now.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to use the ています form when an action began in the recent past (さっきから) but is still continuing now.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: My 90-year-old grandfather is very healthy and jogs in the park every day.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase that states the topic of the sentence goes with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な changes to で to connect two parts of a sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The frequency adverb modifies the verb that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action of jogging takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in form Vています combines with the adverb 毎日 to show a regularly repeated habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: The first part uses で to connect an adjective describing health, while the second part uses 走っています together with the adverb 毎日 to describe a regular daily habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 走ります is used, it only refers to a general action in the future, without emphasizing a regular routine or habit.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: When describing a regular daily habit (with 毎日), Japanese usually uses Vています instead of the ordinary dictionary form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: The alcohol and soft drinks for the party have already been bought.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The relative clause directly modifies the noun for the drinks that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.vi: as for the alcohol and soft drinks
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The object is moved to the topic position and used with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb emphasizes that the preparation was completed earlier.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Vてあります with a transitive verb describes a prepared state for a purpose.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: The noun phrase used as the topic (the items prepared) goes with は and combines with the pattern Vてあります to emphasize that the result of preparing for the party is still maintained.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買っています is used, it only describes possession or an ongoing buying action, and does not highlight advance preparation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 買いました is used, it is simply a statement that the items were bought in the past, without emphasizing that they are ready for the party.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: The pattern Vてあります is used only with transitive verbs to describe an intentional preparatory action. It does not combine with intransitive verbs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: V他動詞て形 + あります
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vi: Because the TV is broken, it cannot be watched.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject in the clause expressing the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The intransitive verb in form Vている shows the current broken state and combines with から to give the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is turned into a noun with こと and used with the particle が to mark the object of ability.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative predicate form of できる shows that the action cannot be performed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: The first part uses an intransitive verb in form こわれている to show the broken state as the reason (から), leading to the result in the second part: being unable to watch (見ることができません).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If こわしたから is used, it means that someone deliberately broke or damaged the TV, instead of simply stating objectively that the TV is broken.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If the potential form 見られません is used, the sentence is shorter, while the structure ことができません is more formal and fixed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: The broken state of an object must use the intransitive verb in form Vている (こわれている), not the plain form (こわれる), when the machine is already broken.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる / ことができない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vi: I still have not read the book I borrowed last week.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The relative clause modifies the noun for the book that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the direct object affected by the action of reading.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb is used with the negative form to show that something has not happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern まだ + Vていません describes an action that has not been performed up to the present.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: The modifying clause 先週借りた clarifies the object 本を, and then combines with the pair まだ ... 読んでいません to show that reading has not been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 読みませんでした is used, it means that the person did not read it in the past or missed the deadline without reading it. It does not express the intention to continue reading.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: To say “still have not done V,” Japanese must use まだ〜ていません, not the negative past tense (まだ〜ませんでした).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.cn: まだ + Vて形 + いません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vi: I finished all the moving preparations by myself last week, so there is no need to ask my friends for help anymore.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The moving preparations are made the main topic of the sentence with the particle は.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb emphasizes that the cleaning has been completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing the time when the action happened in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: A phrase showing that the person did the work alone.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vてしまう shows complete fulfillment and combines with から to give the reason.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に indicates the person who receives the request for help or performs the helping action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern Vてもらう describes receiving help from another person and modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle は follows a noun to emphasize a negative meaning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: The negative predicate means that something does not exist.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: The reason clause uses してしまった to emphasize that the moving preparations were fully completed alone last week, leading to the result that it is unnecessary (ひつようはありません) to ask friends for help (ともだちにてつだってもらう).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If してあげたから is used, the sentence means that I did something to help another person, which completely changes the meaning of preparing my own things.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If てつだってくれるひつよう is used, the focus changes to the friend actively helping, while てつだってもらう shows that I ask the other person for help.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse てもらう (I ask another person to do something for me) with てあげる (I do something to help another person).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.cn: Vて形 + しまう / Vて形 + もらう / V辞書形 + 必要はない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vi: Yamada: This plate is beautiful. I want to buy it, but I wonder if it is expensive. Tanaka: The price is written there already.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: きれいな modifies the noun おさら that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.vi: it is a plate, isn’t it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: だね is used to gently confirm something that both speakers notice.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.3.vi: I want to buy it, but
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 買いたい expresses a desire, while けど connects it to the contrasting idea that follows.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.4.vi: I wonder if it is expensive
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: かな is placed at the end of a sentence to express a gentle question or uncertainty.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: に indicates the place where the price is written.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the subject of the state 書いてある.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: Vてある describes the result of an action performed by someone that still remains.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: The adjective な comes before a noun and must have な to modify おさら. けど connects a desire with uncertainty, while かな expresses a question to oneself. そこに indicates the place, and が indicates the thing that is in the state of having been written.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書いている is used instead, it means that someone is writing, without emphasizing the result that has already been written.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 高いでしょうか is used instead, the question is more polite and directly addressed to the listener.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: Learners may easily confuse Vてある with Vている; Vてある emphasizes a result that has been prepared or completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: When I moved, my friends came to help me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the moving action in the time clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the noun that is the object of した.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: したとき creates a time clause that sets the background for the action in the main clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject who performs the action of coming to help.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: に shows the purpose of coming.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: 来てくれました combines with Vてくれる to show that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: The 私がひっこしをしたとき clause comes first to state the time. In the main clause, ともだちが is the subject, に shows the purpose of coming, and てくれる shows that the help benefits the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 来ました, it only says that the friends came and does not show that they came to do something helpful for me.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 手伝ってもらいました, the focus shifts to my receiving help.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に as a place marker, but in 手伝いに来る, に shows the purpose “come to help.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.cn: Vた + とき; N + に + 来る; Vて + くれる
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vi: Child: I do not want to eat it because I hate vegetables. Father: You must not say that.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that vegetables are the topic being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: だから connects the reason to the conclusion that the speaker does not want to eat.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べたい expresses desire; it changes to 食べたくない to negate the desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the content being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: Vてはいけません expresses a prohibition or something that is not allowed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.cn: Aな + だから; Vます-removeます + たい/たくない; Vて + はいけません
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: やさいは sets the topic, while きらいだから gives the reason leading to 食べたくない. The father uses そんなことを to replace everything that was just said, then uses Vてはいけません to prohibit that way of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 言わないでください, it becomes a request not to say it, which is softer than the prohibition expressed by 言ってはいけません.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 言ってはだめです, the meaning is almost the same, but the expression is more casual.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake きらい for a verb; it is the adjective な, so use だから, not くて.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: Nakamura: "Have you ever watched sumo wrestling?" - Smith: "I watched it when I went to Tokyo last year. It was very interesting."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: State the name of the person asking the question in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of watching.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vたことがある is used to ask about past experiences.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: State the name of the person replying in the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: A time adverb that modifies the time when the speaker went to Tokyo.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the destination of movement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern Vたときに identifies the completed trip as the time when the speaker watched it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: An affirmative predicate showing that the action happened in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the past tense to express an impression after watching it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: The question uses the pattern 『Vたことがある』 to ask about an experience that someone has had in life. In the answer, the speaker uses 『Vたときに』 together with the past tense 『見ました』 to describe a specific event that happened at a definite time in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 『見ることがありますか』 is used, the sentence changes to asking whether the person sometimes watches sumo, rather than asking about experience.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If the dictionary form 『行くときに』 is used, it shows that the person is on the way to Tokyo, not yet at the destination to watch it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse Vたことがある (having done something before) with Vることがある (doing something sometimes).
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.cn: Vた + ことがある / ことがあります
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vi: Because the office lights are off, I think Mr. Sato has already gone home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects noun phrases to identify where the light is located.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が is used with the intransitive verb きえる to mark the subject of the off state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The progressive form of the verb combines with から to state the current condition used as a basis for the judgment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes Mr. Sato the main topic of the supposition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb showing that the action was completed before the time of speaking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle と is used to quote the content of a thought or judgment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: A predicate that expresses the speaker's personal supposition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: The first part uses 『きえているから』 to describe a resulting state that continues, providing factual evidence. The second part then gives a personal supposition, using the plain form before 『〜と思います』.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 『帰ったそうです』 is used, the sentence means that the speaker has heard that Mr. Sato has gone home, rather than expressing the speaker's own supposition.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 『帰ったはずです』 is used, the sentence expresses almost complete certainty based on logical evidence or a schedule.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: Before the quotation particle と in the pattern と思います, the form must be changed to the plain form (普通形); do not mistakenly keep the polite form ます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.tokens.6.m: Mr., Ms., Mrs., or another polite title
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(だ)・N(だ) + と思う / と思います
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vi: While I was on the train, I kept reading a book.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the support or means used to board, together with the verb 乗る.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vている間 describes the entire period during which an action continues.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb emphasizing that the action of reading continues without interruption.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of reading.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate is in the past progressive tense, describing an action that continued in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: Because the action in the second clause 『ずっと本を読んでいました』 continued for the entire time of sitting on the train, 『間』 must be used without 『に』.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 『間に』 is used, the action in the second clause must be a momentary action, such as falling asleep or dropping something, rather than a long-lasting action like ずっと読んでいました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 『乗りながら』 is used, it emphasizes doing two things at the same time by the same subject, while 『間』 emphasizes the time period that provides the context.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 間, in which the second clause continues throughout the period, with 間に, in which the second clause happens momentarily during that period.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形/Vている/Vない・Nの + 間
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: Yamashita: "Was Yamamoto well? I also really wanted to meet her." - Sato: "She was very well. Yamamoto also wanted to meet you very much."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Names the person who starts the conversation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: A name used to address the person being asked about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending な is changed to the casual past form to ask about someone's health.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も shows that the speaker has the same feeling or desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The ending 〜たかった, together with the modal particle なあ, expresses the speaker's desire in the past.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the state of being well.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: The predicate confirms the good condition of a third person.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.8.n: The particle も makes the third person the topic for describing their feelings or wishes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.9.n: The particle に marks the person toward whom the action of meeting is directed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.10.n: The pattern 〜たがる is changed to the past progressive form to report a third person's desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.cn: Vます (remove ます) + たがる / たがっている / たがっていた
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: When talking about the first person's desire, the speaker uses 『会いたかった』. However, when reporting the desire or feeling of a third person, Yamamoto, Japanese requires the form 『〜たがっていた』 instead of directly using 〜たい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 『会いたかったよ』 is used, the sentence is grammatically incorrect because the ending 〜たい can be used directly only for the speaker's own desire.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 『会いたいそうだ』 is used, it conveys an indirectly reported statement, meaning that the person is said to want to meet, rather than describing an observed psychological expression.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Learners of Japanese often incorrectly use the ending 〜たい for a third person instead of changing it to 〜たがる / 〜たがっている.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q6.tokens.10.m: I really mean it / don't you think?
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vi: I want you not to smoke inside because the walls will get dirty.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that will become dirty through the intransitive verb よごれる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern から connects a clause stating the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で marks the place where the action of smoking takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of smoking.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.4.vi: I want you not to smoke.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜ないでほしい is used to express the wish that the other person will not perform an action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: The first clause uses 『から』 to give an objective reason, fear of dirtying the walls. The second clause combines the negative form with the ending 『〜ないでほしい』 to politely express the wish that another person will not do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 『すわないでください』 is used, the sentence sounds more like a direct request or command, while 『すわないでほしい』 emphasizes the speaker's feelings and wishes.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 『すいたくない』 is used, it means that the speaker does not want to smoke, rather than referring to another person's action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish between 〜たくない, meaning that the speaker does not want to do something, and 〜ないでほしい, meaning that the speaker wants the listener or another person not to do it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.cn: Vて / Vないで + ほしい（です）
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: It is very difficult because I have to write and send an essay to the teacher by tomorrow.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle までに marks the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun referring to the person who receives the assignment.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object that must be written and sent.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the て form to connect a sequence of actions in time order.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.4.vi: because I have to send it
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜なくてはいけない expresses a compulsory duty, and it is followed by から to explain why the situation is difficult.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate expresses an evaluation or feeling about a difficult or busy situation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.cn: Vない (remove い) + なくてはいけない / なくてはならない
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: The sentence combines the て form to connect two consecutive actions, writing and then sending, with the compulsory-duty structure 『〜なくてはいけない』 and the particle 『から』 to clarify the reason for the difficulty.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 『送らなくてもいい』 is used, the sentence means that sending it is not necessary, which is the complete opposite of the context.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 『送ってはいけない』 is used, the sentence expresses prohibition, meaning that sending it is not allowed, instead of expressing a duty to send it.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the compulsory structure 『〜なくてはいけない』, meaning "must do," with the prohibitive structure 『〜てはいけない』, meaning "must not do."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vi: I plan to work for a Japanese company in the future.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time and topic of the plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with 会社 to modify 会社.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で marks the place where the action of working takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary form はたらく comes before つもり to modify the plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: つもりです expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: しょうらいは sets the time range, and then the place is stated with で. The dictionary-form verb comes before つもりです to create a structure for talking about a plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead emphasizes a fixed plan or schedule and places less emphasis on personal will.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に to indicate a workplace, but because the action of working takes place there, で should be used.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Nの + つもりです
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vi: Yamamoto: “Let's talk comfortably tonight.” Tanaka: “Yes, let's do that.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.sk: Time は + Adverb + V意向。／そうしょう。
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker's name comes before the dialogue.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the time as the topic of the suggestion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb modifying the action of talking.
