default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 話そう is the volitional form of 話す, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The second speaker's name starts the reply after the line break.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: うん is a reply confirming the previous suggestion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: This phrase is used to agree to do what was just suggested.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + そう／V意向形
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.why: The volitional form 話そう is used to make an invitation to do something together. The reply uses そうしょう to agree with what was just said.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: 話してください asks the listener to speak, while 話そう invites the speaker and listener to do it together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q10.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the volitional form 話そう with 話します; 話そう has the meaning "let's do it together" or "I will do it."
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vi: At this university, you can also study Arabic, Russian, and many other languages.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where studying takes place; は states the scope of comparison or the topic.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とか connects an object given as an example in a list.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: とか adds another object, while も means “also” and emphasizes the expanded scope.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: できます expresses the ability to study the listed languages.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.why: で identifies the place of study, while とか lists examples of subjects or languages that can be studied. も adds the meaning “also” and expands the list.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: や usually connects nouns in an incomplete list, while とか has a more flexible example-listing nuance.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q11.kobun.tip: とか does not mean the compulsory choice “or”; it usually indicates only a few examples in an open-ended list.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: This year, I want to travel to places such as Kyushu or Okinawa.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents this year as the time and topic of the wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: とか gives Kyushu as an example in the list of destinations.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: とか continues giving examples, while に indicates the place the speaker wants to go to.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたいです expresses the speaker’s wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: The destinations are listed with とか, creating an example-listing nuance rather than necessarily giving a complete list. に attaches to the destination of 旅行する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: や also lists a few examples, but it usually has a clearer noun-listing nuance than とか.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use で after a place name when saying that you want to go there; with 旅行する, the destination usually goes with に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vi: A: What will you do this Friday? B: I plan to eat sushi with my friends.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今週 with 金曜日 to identify which Friday.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this Friday the topic of the question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb します.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: と indicates the people who will perform the action of eating sushi together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks sushi as the object of 食べる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: 食べよう is the volitional form, and と marks the content of the intention expressed by 思っています.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: と思っています expresses an intention that has been formed and still remains unchanged.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.why: The question makes a time the topic and asks about the object of the action with 何を. The answer uses と to connect the volitional form 食べよう with 思っています, expressing the speaker’s plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: つもりです also talks about plans, but 食べようと思っています emphasizes the speaker’s present intention or thought.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Do not connect 食べよう思っています directly; と must come between the volitional form and 思っています.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思っています
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vi: I watched a news report about an earthquake that happened abroad yesterday.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the earthquake happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: きのう adds the time when the event happened.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the event that happened in the clause.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: という turns the clause あった into content that modifies ニュース.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the news report as the object that was watched.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 見ました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: 外国で and きのう respectively state the place and time of the event. The clause じしんがあったという comes before ニュース to explain what the news report was about.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と聞きました, it means that the speaker heard the information, not that they watched the news report.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place という after ニュース, but in this structure the content of the news must come before という＋ニュース.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ という ＋ N
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: During summer vacation, let’s climb Mount Fuji.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates the time and emphasizes that summer vacation is when the action will take place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object or destination of the climbing action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: のぼろう is the volitional form and expresses a decision or an invitation to do something together.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: には puts the time first to provide the background. に goes with のぼる to indicate the mountain being climbed, while the volitional form at the end gives a decision or invitation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: のぼりましょう is a more polite invitation, while のぼろう is more casual and direct.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: のぼる goes with に when talking about climbing a mountain; do not use を based on a direct translation from Vietnamese.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vi: At the weekend, I plan to sleep at home.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the weekend as the time and topic of the plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the action of sleeping or resting takes place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ねよう is the volitional form, and と marks the content of the plan expressed by 思います.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: と思います expresses the speaker’s intention or decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: The sentence presents the time, place, and then the planned action in order. The volitional form ねよう combines with と＋思います to express the intention naturally.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: ねるつもりです also means planning to sleep, but saying it with と思います emphasizes the speaker’s present thought or decision.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: After 思います in this pattern, と must follow; do not use ねように思います instead when speaking directly about a plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思います
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: My son says that during this summer vacation he will work part-time or travel.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time に ＋ N を ＋ Vるとか ＋ N に ＋ Vるとか ＋ 言っている
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates when the activities will take place.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: とか connects one example in the list of mentioned activities.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the direction or destination of 行く.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: とか connects another possibility in the list.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: 言っています is the main predicate and reports speech happening now.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: The two actions come before 言っています and are connected with とか to form speech content containing several examples. に in 夏休みに indicates the time, while に in 旅行に行く indicates the destination.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: や usually lists nouns, while など means “and so on” and is less natural than とか when listing actions or speech.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use とか to mean “or” for a single choice, but this pattern usually gives two or more examples.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・N＋とか、V普通形・N＋とか ＋ 言う／話す
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vi: I heard that Mr. and Mrs. Nishida will leave their company.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the people who will perform the action of leaving their jobs.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the workplace being left in the expression 会社をやめる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form comes before という話 to modify 話.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: という turns the preceding clause into the content of 話; を marks the whole phrase as the object of 聞きました.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞きました is the main predicate and expresses that the speaker heard that information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: The clause 西田さんが会社をやめる comes before という話 to identify the content of the story. The whole phrase という話を becomes the object that was heard.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Vるそうだ directly conveys the information heard, while という話 emphasizes that it is a specific story or piece of information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: Do not place という after 話; the content clause must come before という話.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + という話/ニュース/うわさ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vi: Jun: “Shall we go to a good ramen shop? But we have to wait in line for about an hour.” Kai: “Huh? We have to wait in line for a whole hour? I’m hungry, so it would be better to choose another shop.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The name Jun comes before the opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.vi: go to a good ramen shop
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective おいしい modifies the ramen shop, while に indicates the destination.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 行かない uses the negative form to make an informal invitation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: くらい shows an approximate amount or length of time.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.4.vi: but we have to wait in line
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: けど connects additional information with a contrasting or cautionary meaning.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The name Kai comes before the second opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: えー shows surprise or disagreement.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle も emphasizes that the time is longer than the speaker expected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.8.vi: do we really have to wait in line
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: の at the end of the sentence asks for confirmation or an explanation about waiting in line.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: The particle が marks the subject in the hungry state.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: から connects the reason to the conclusion that they should choose another shop.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.11.n: ちがう modifies 店, forming the phrase “another shop.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.12.n: The particle が marks the object judged to be suitable.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.13.n: いい is the evaluative predicate, while よ emphasizes Kai’s opinion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.why: に indicates the destination, while 行かない? is an informal way to invite someone. も emphasizes that one hour is too long; から gives the reason for concluding 店がいい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか～ない is used, the meaning changes to “only one hour,” without the emphasis that it is a whole hour.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If から replaces ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.2.d: If んですか is used, the question has a stronger sense of asking for a clear explanation.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate も as “also,” but in １時間も, も emphasizes that the amount is more than expected.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t15-q9.kobun.cn: N + も; V普通形 + の？
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: Nana invited me to a party. I brought a cake.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the inviting action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place or event toward which something is directed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb しょうたいする with the auxiliary verb くれる.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: くれる shows that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は makes the speaker the topic of the next sentence.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the item being carried.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: 持っていく combines the action of holding something with movement away from the place where the speaker is.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The person performing the action uses が, while the event being approached uses に. Then, は changes the topic to the speaker; を marks the cake as the item being carried.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらう is used, the focus is on the speaker receiving help from Nana.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 持ってくる is used, it means bringing the cake toward the speaker or the place being discussed.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse が and は, but here が clearly shows that Nana is the person who invited the speaker.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる; Vて + いく
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vi: It is so noisy. Be quiet.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: うるさい is an evaluative predicate, while なあ expresses the speaker’s strong emotion.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 静かな changes な into に to modify the action する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: しろ is the imperative form of する, creating a strong and direct request.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.why: 静かに changes the adjective 静かな into an adverb to describe how to perform する. しろ is a direct command, so the sentence sounds strong.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 静かにしてください, the request becomes much more polite and gentle.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 静かになってください is used, it emphasizes becoming quiet, not just being asked to perform the action する.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use 静かなに, but when the adjective な modifies a verb, it must change to 静かに.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t22-q1.kobun.cn: Aな + に + する; する → しろ
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: My friend has a Japanese test tomorrow. I hope my friend does their best.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the friend as the topic of the upcoming information.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The time expression comes before the predicate to specify when the test exists.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects 日本語 with 試験, showing that the test is for Japanese.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the existing thing as the test.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is a predicate that expresses the existence of an object or event.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the person who is expected to perform the action.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: The て form connects the action がんばる with ほしい.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: Vてほしいです expresses a wish for someone else to do something.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: は introduces the topic, while が marks the existing test. With てほしい, the person who has the wish is the implied subject, and the person expected to act is marked by に.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてください, the sentence becomes a direct request, no longer the speaker’s gentle wish.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたいです is used, the speaker wants to do their best, rather than wishing for the friend to do so.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place に after the verb, but in Vてほしい, に must come after the person expected to act.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: Mai: “Kai, are you going to the party tomorrow?” Kai: “No, I do not plan to go.”
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker’s name comes before the opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The name of the person being addressed comes at the beginning of the question, separated by a comma.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects あした with パーティー to describe the party.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows the destination of 行きます.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the predicate, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: Kai’s name comes before the second opening quotation mark.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: いいえ negates the content of the previous question.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle は identifies me as the person who has the plan.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The plain negative form 行かない modifies the noun つもり.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: つもりです ends the sentence and expresses the speaker’s intention.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: For the destination, use に, and then 行きますか forms the question. In the answer, 行かない comes before つもり to describe the intention not to go.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定です is used, the meaning is more focused on a schedule or a decided plan, and is more objective than つもりです.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないと思います is used, it only expresses a thought or guess and does not emphasize personal intention.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use the polite form before つもり, but before this pattern, they must use the plain form, such as 行かない.
default.q.pointvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形 + つもりだ/です
